全名《白得先破车上河弦取胜总变局》，出自元至顺年间西园精舍本《事林广记》。
《事林广记》是现存最早载有象棋内容的书籍，由南宋末年的陈元靓编写。原宋本已不可见，现存的元、明刊本均经过增扩与删改。因元至顺年间西园精舍刻本的年份较早，其中记录的棋谱数量较多，故以此为参考。
en:
Its full title is The Winning Endgame of White: Breaking the Chariot to Seize the River String, recorded in the Xiyuan Studio edition of Shilin Guangji, printed during the Zhishun reign of the Yuan dynasty. 
Shilin Guangji is the earliest known book to document Xiangqi (Chinese chess), compiled by Chen Yuanjing at the close of the Southern Song. Though the original Song edition is lost, surviving Yuan and Ming versions were later expanded and edited. The Xiyuan edition stands out for its early date and rich collection of recorded games, hence its value as a reference.

Dance on, for the songs of Skybrim shall never cease.

五、写给秋娘
一院子怪人，叫我“种地先生”，还叫我写书。咱种地的总被老爷们当猪狗，还能当先生？要是你和苗娃还在就好嘞。以前村里算命的说，人都能投胎转世，你们下辈子去好人家去，天天都吃饱饱的……听书院的人说，以后人人都能吃饱饭，真能这样就好了，那你们万一投到寻常人家，也能吃饱了。
en:
Part I. To Qiuniang
Master He is teaching me to write. I did not want to learn. He said learning a few characters does a person good. Said it lets you write letters. Qiuniang, so I'm writing to you, all right? I miss you. I think of you all the time... It would have been better if I'd gone with you...
...
Part II. To Miao
I dream of you all the time, Miao. You and your mother are both gone. Why am I still here, still alive... I worked the fields all my life. How did I still let your mother and you starve? What kind of farming is that?
...
Part III. To Miao
Miao, I failed you. I did not keep watch over you... that dirt was not to be eaten, not that much... I know you were hungry. I know you were hungry...
...
Part IV. To Miao
I have learned a few more characters now. If only I could have taught them to you. They even gave me a proper name, Liu Sinong. Heh.... I have a real name now. No one calls me Liu Er anymore. They say they are studying farming. Farming... what is there to study?
...
Part V. To Qiuniang
This place is full of strange people. They call me "Master Farmer." They want me to write a book. We who work the fields were always treated like dogs. Since when could people like us be called "master"? If only you and Miao were still here... Back in the village, the fortune teller used to say people are born again in another life. In your next life, I hope you both be born into a good family, with full bellies every day... They say here at the academy that one day everyone will have enough to eat. If that ever comes true, then even if you two are born into an ordinary family in your next life, at least you'll still have full bellies.

后来，它成了一只远近闻名的老鹅，脾气依旧。失魂落魄行走江湖的这些年，有人因为“疯病”赶他，也有人因此护它；有孩子拿着小木刀、小木剑陪它玩，也有孩子偷偷从医馆为它寻来清凉膏。
扬风鹅的疯病原来并不碍事，只消耐心应对，为它擦擦药，再到瀑布下浇淋一番——呼，今日鹅的修为又精进了！

zh: 取鲜鱼一尾，涤净去鳞，刮肉为蓉，制成细面。煎鱼头至金黄，注沸水于釜，烈火烹之，撇去浮沫，投以调料，熬至汤色乳白。继入前之细面，加大茴叶。如此烹之，鱼汤色白香醇、甘旨肥浓，鱼面滑而不腻、口感筋道。鱼香四溢，其味无穷，食之难忘。
en: Take a fresh fish, clean and scale it, then scrape the flesh into a smooth paste and shape it into delicate strands of noodles. Pan-fry the fish head until golden brown, pour boiling water into the pot, and bring it to a vigorous boil. Skim off the foam, add seasonings, and continue simmering until the broth turns milky white. Add the handmade fish noodles and a piece of star anise. The result is a fragrant, creamy soup with deep, savory richness. The noodles are springy yet light, leaving no trace of greasiness. As the aroma rises, so does the appetite—it's a taste that lingers long after the meal.

zh:
胡小旭生体弱多病，罹患喘疾。因此，胡家娘子从来都不让胡小旭出门。
胡小旭就像一只被困在巢穴里的幼鸟，失去了展翅体会天地浩渺的机会。
小小的房间里，胡小旭读书，习字，倒也乖巧。可他最喜欢的，还是阿爷给自己带回来的嫖姚棋。
听阿爷说，这是纪念霍去病大将军的玩具。
“我知道！霍去病是汉代的大将军！他一生征战四方，是个大英雄！阿爷，咳咳……我也想成为像他一样的大英雄！”
看着孩子眼中的光芒，胡家娘子心中一阵酸楚。

天下哪个母亲不希望自己的孩子健康呢。如果可以，她甚至愿意用自己的命，换小旭健康的身体。
胡家娘子时常陷入深深的自责。她觉得自己没有给孩子一个健康的身体。所以，她用一种几乎偏执的方式来弥补。她亲力亲为照顾着小旭的衣食住行，事无巨细。
她的爱像一张巨大的网，护着了小旭，却也困住了她自己。
en:
Hu Xiaoxu was born weak and sickly, afflicted with asthma. Because of this, Lady Hu never allowed Xiaoxu to go out. 
Xiaoxu was like a fledgling bird trapped in its nest, denied the chance to spread its wings and experience the vastness of heaven and earth. 
In his small room, Xiaoxu read and practiced calligraphy, behaving quite obediently. But his favorite thing was still the Piaoyao Battleboard set his grandfather had brought back for him. 
He heard from Grandpa that this was a toy commemorating the great General Huo Qubing. 
"I know! Huo Qubing was a great general of the Han Dynasty! He fought campaigns in all directions throughout his life, a true hero! Grandpa, cough... I want to be a great hero like him too!" 
Seeing the light in her child's eyes, Lady Hu's heart ached. 

What mother in the world doesn't wish for her child to be healthy? If she could, she would even trade her own life for Xiaoxu's health. 
Lady Hu often fell into deep self-blame. She felt she hadn't given her child a healthy body. So, she compensated in an almost obsessive way. She personally attended to every detail of Xiaoxu's clothing, food, shelter, and travel. 
Her love was like a giant net, protecting Xiaoxu, but it also trapped herself.

zh:
扇面上题的《沧浪歌》是回春堂传下来的训诫。扇子是兄弟俩一人一把。兄长子真总能讨几位长辈欢心。他展开扇子讲，这水清恰如西湖，水浊便似钱塘，清有清的灵秀，浊有浊的辽阔，行医济世也当如此。至于到底如个什么此，他其实也没细说，只是拿着扇子一表人才地微笑，就博得满堂称赞。
溜出厅堂，陈子奚拿扇骨点他哥肩膀，笑：“你是那讨喜的清水，我是那惹人嫌的浊水。”
陈子真摇了摇头：“子奚，容不得沙子的才是清水。”
en:
The "Song of Canglang" inscribed on the fan is an admonition handed down by the Spring's Return Hall. Each brother received one. The elder brother, Zizhen, always knew how to please the family elders. He would unfold his fan and explain that clear water was like West Lake, while turbid water was like the Qiantang River: clear water had its delicate beauty, turbid water its broad expanse, and the practice of medicine should embrace both. What exactly he meant by that, he never explained. He simply stood there, handsome and smiling with fan in hand, and won a roomful of praise.
Once they had slipped out of the hall, Chen Zixi tapped his brother on the shoulder with the fan's ribs and laughed. "You're the clear water everyone likes, and I'm the muddy water everyone scorns."
Chen Zizhen shook his head. "Zixi, it is clear water that cannot abide even a grain of sand."

Grind them into a fine powder, add honey and some musk.  

Apply with flower dew. Use a wet silk handkerchief to wipe away after a short period of time to remove old skin.  

Needles and knives, after being in a fire for fifteen minutes, can reshape bones after being covered in the balm.

zh:
河东八俊四散分开之后，仇越海做回了渔翁。他每天钓三条鱼，吃一条，放一条，卖一条。

卖鱼的次数多了，他也和鱼铺的老板熟识起来。老板问起他名字。
“名字嘛，仇越海。”
“哎，怎么有点耳熟……你不会是八俊里那个仇大侠吧！”
“同名、同名，你看我像大侠吗？”
两人一起哈哈大笑起来。
然后，仇越海拿卖鱼的铜板打了一壶酒，晃着瓶子回家了。

八俊四散之后，每个人都有自己的选择，这便是他的选择。他本来就是一个普通人，由于因缘际会偶然发出了一瞬恍如错觉的亮光，光暗之后，他还是他。
那些曾一同拼搏的旧友们，仇越海咧嘴一笑，将酒洒在天地之间，来日有机会再找我喝酒啊。
记好了，是找一个叫仇越海的渔夫喝酒，不是找那个叫仇越海的江湖侠客！有些人、有些事啊，就应该结束在最光辉灿烂的时候。
en:
After the Eight Talents of Hedong were scattered, Qiu Yuehai returned to being a fisherman. Every day he caught three fish. One he ate, one he released, and one he sold.

From selling fish so often, he grew familiar with the fishmonger. One day, the shopkeeper asked his name.
"The name's Qiu Yuehai."
"Hmm, that sounds familiar... You wouldn't be that Hero Qiu from the Eight Talents, would you?"
"Same name, that's all. Do I look like a hero to you?"
The two burst out laughing.
Qiu Yuehai then used the copper coins from selling fish to buy a jug of wine and staggered home, swinging the bottle.

After the Eight Talents went their separate ways, each made their own choice—and this was his. He had always been an ordinary man. By some twist of fate, he'd briefly shone like a passing illusion. Now that the light had faded, he was still himself.
As for his old comrades-in-arms, Qiu Yuehai grinned and poured a libation to the heavens. Come find me for a drink someday!
Just remember—you're looking for a fisherman named Qiu Yuehai, not Qiu Yuehai the jianghu swordsman! Some people and some stories ought to end at their brightest moment.

少年一挑眉。我梦到了，以后自然会有。在它出现之前，你得给我把斩它的刃做出来。它是横刀，要有精美的环首，笔直的刀锋；我要拿它做我的利刃，斩尽拦在我面前的劲敌。
这模样倒是与众不同。不过一把特殊的横刀，你想要，就能有。
我把它捧给少年。少年抚摸过漆黑的环首，它的刃身将刚破晓的天光映在我脸上，划破了凉州刺骨的风。
这把兵刃，破天光，斩白蛇，便叫它破白。
我望着破白。若是有一天……你有了更好的剑，记得把破白送还给我。它是我最得意的剑。
少年用刀背拍了拍我的肩。破白坏了，我就会来找你。只要你活着，它就是最好的剑。
en:
An unwashed seventeen-year-old boy knocked on my door at dawn. "I want a weapon," he said. "It must be white, white as snow falling from the sky. And black, black as obsidian in the mountains. It must be a divine weapon, capable of slaying a white serpent three stories tall." 
You fool! Where in Liangzhou would you find such a huge white serpent? 
The boy raised an eyebrow. "I dreamed of it. It will come someday. Before it does, you must forge the blade to slay it. It's a horizontal saber with an exquisite ring pommel and a straight blade. I will use it as my sharp weapon to cut down all foes in my path." 
You have quite a unique vision. But a special heng blade, if you want it, you shall have it. 
I handed the saber to the boy. He stroked the pitch-black ring pommel, its blade reflected the dawn light onto my face, cutting through Liangzhou's bitter wind. 
"This weapon breaks the dawn and slays the white serpent, let it be called Palebreak." 
I stared at Palebreak. "If ever... you get a better sword, remember to return Palebreak to me. It is my proudest creation." 
The boy patted my shoulder with the back of the saber. "If Palebreak breaks, I will come back to you. As long as you live, it will always be the best sword."

zh:
看着喝空的药罐，殷松释然地躺下。贫病交加，他早已家徒四壁。儿子前些年又上山采药，跌到山底下去了。
他不怨命。只是，他不想自己一个人继续撑下去了。

殷松的老家来自荆楚。此地好巫，常有招魂祭祀之法。听说那汨罗江中的大巫曾使用过名为“椒糈”的祭祀，殷松决定效仿他，在自己死之前请众神接引，去找儿子。

他搜刮了所有的角落，只在米缸里发现了还剩下半碗的干粟。然而，事神之仪不可怠慢。他要去集市上买一份最好的秦椒。
说到天水集最好的秦椒，当然是老李头家的。那老头有些本事，种的秦椒又红又香。也只有这样的好东西，才能取悦众神。

可到了天水集，殷松却看到，那个种秦椒的老李头竟摇身一变，成了烫菜摊的店主。
看着老李头脸上热火朝天的欢喜，嗅着秦椒被热油激出的香气，殷松攥紧了衣角，却也忍不住吞了吞口水。

“哟！老殷！来啦！快坐，我给你做个烫菜，你尝尝！”
“不，不了……老李，我想，买点秦椒……”殷松掏出了最后的几个铜板。 “你看，就这些……买一点就好。”殷松顿了顿。“你家椒好，我拿来做饭拜神。”
“老哥，今年秦椒虽然贱，但咱这……”幺昭布心里一算，便知这买卖不好做。
“莫说了。”李白元出言打断了幺昭布。“老张，舀一碗秦椒。阿妹，烫一碗菜。”
李白元又蹲下，在摊位后面摆弄了些什么。随后，将一只布袋和一个食盒交给殷松。
“这是椒，回家再打开，小心漏了。”
“这是烫菜。里面还有两份呱呱。不过这食盒贵得很，还请还回，可好？”
“爱吃的话，就再来啊。”
殷松百般推辞，奈何几个人都要殷松收下。他便惭愧地拿着食盒走了。

若自己今天死在家里，又该麻烦谁把这食盒送回来呢。
殷松想了想。还是先把这食盒还给人家，再去找儿子吧。
en:
Looking at the empty medicine jar, Yin Song lay back, resigned. Trapped by poverty and illness, his home was already bare. His son had gone up the mountain to gather herbs a few years back and fallen down a cliff. 
He didn't blame fate. He just didn't want to keep struggling on alone anymore. 

Yin Song came from Jingchu, where shamanism was revered, with soul-summoning rituals being normal. Hearing that the great shamans of the Miluo River had once used a sacrifice called "pepper and rice," Yin Song decided to emulate them, inviting the spirits to guide him to his son before he died. 

He searched every corner, finding only half a bowl of dried millet left in the rice jar. However, rituals for the spirits couldn't be slighted. He would go to the market to buy the finest Qin pepper. 
Speaking of the best Qin pepper in Skybrim Market, it had to be from Old Li's. The old man had a knack; his peppers were red and fragrant. Only such good stuff could please the spirits. 

But when he reached Skybrim Market, Yin Song saw that Old Li, the pepper grower, had transformed into the owner of a hot pot stall. 
Watching Old Li's face flushed with bustling joy, smelling the aroma of peppers awakened by hot oil, Yin Song clenched the hem of his clothes but couldn't help swallowing. 

"Hey! Old Yin! You came! Quick, sit, I'll make you a bowl of hot pot, you try it!" 
"No, no... Old Li, I... I want to buy some Qin pepper..." Yin Song took out his last few copper coins. "Look, just this much... just a little is fine." He paused. "Your peppers are good. I'll use them to cook an offering." 
"Brother, peppers are cheap this year, but with this..." Yao Zhaobu mentally calculated and knew this sale wouldn't work. 
"Say no more." Li Baiyuan cut him off. "Old Zhang, scoop a bowl of peppers. Sis, make a bowl of hot pot." 
Li Baiyuan then crouched, fiddled with something behind the stall, and handed Yin Song a cloth bag and a food box. 
"Here are the peppers. Open them at home, careful they don't spill." 
"This is the hot pot. There are two portions of guagua inside too. But this food box is quite valuable, please return it later, alright?" 
"If you like it, come again." 
Yin Song tried to refuse a hundred ways, but the others insisted he take it. Ashamed, he took the food box and left. 

If I die at home today, who will I trouble to return this box? 
Yin Song thought for a moment. Better to return the box first, then go find my son.

zh:
学会天下棋，要从下遍文津馆无敌手开始。
齐岐到文津馆的第一天，就把一个师兄杀得片甲不留。师兄不服，又下一盘，又输。
她收了棋子站起来，问，下一个。
大家说她是个怪人。下棋不说话，落子快，眼神冷。赢了也不笑，输了就复盘，复完再战。她不交朋友，不聊天，不是在天一楼就是在找人下棋。有人问她是哪儿来的，她只说，等我赢了这儿所有的人就走。
她到文津馆的两个月，把愿意和她下棋的人都找遍了。还剩最后一个，沈老师。
她一直没和沈老师下过棋。沈老师带她来了以后，安排她住下，带她认了天一楼的路，就很少露面。齐岐知道她不只教书，还有别的事要忙。有时候在走廊上远远看见一眼，沈老师朝她点点头，脚步不停，便走过去了。
第二年春天，齐岐去找沈老师。
沈老师正在窗下看书，看见她进来，放下书，把棋盘摆上，说，让你一个车。
齐岐输了。让马，又输。最后平下，齐岐撑到残局，输了半子。
沈老师从袖子里摸出一封信，放在棋盘上。信是镇上寄来的。沈老师走之前托了人照看老齐，信里说，老齐在她们走后的第九天走了。弥留之际，给齐岐留了句话。
齐岐没拆信，盯着棋盘，半天没动。
沈老师说，老齐说你下棋太急，而好棋都藏在慢的那一手里。
那天晚上，齐岐在天一楼里翻出一本虫蛀的《象戏谱》，对着残局摆到半夜。
她忽然发现，自己来文津馆这么久，从来没认认真真和一个人下过棋。她找人对弈，只是为了赢。赢了就可以回去见爷爷。可赢完一个又一个，总有下一个在等着。
她开始慢下来。
学着爷爷的样子，学着沈老师的样子，慢慢下，输了说一句“好棋”，复盘时先夸对方那步走得妙。有人问她怎么变了个人，她说，只是学棋。
她还是想赢。但不急了。爷爷说好棋都藏在慢的那一手里，那她慢慢下，一步一步下。等把天一楼里的棋谱一本本看完，等沈老师有一天不再给她让子，等到学遍天下棋。
爷爷一定还在那棵树底下等着她，等着她回去下棋。
en:
To master all the chess the world has to offer, one must first become unrivaled at the Inkbound Order.
On her very first day, Qi Qi dismantled a senior disciple on the board, leaving his defenses in ruins. Stung by the humiliation, he demanded a rematch and was crushed once more.
She calmly gathered her pieces, stood up, and simply asked, "Next."
The others whispered that she was strange. She played in dead silence, her moves swift and ruthless, her eyes cold and distant. She never smiled in victory. In defeat, she would meticulously reset the board, analyze the flaw, and demand another match. She made no friends and bothered with no small talk. If she wasn't buried in Tianyi Tower, she was hunting down her next opponent. When asked where she came from, she would only reply, "I will leave as soon as I beat everyone here."
Within two months, she had played every single person willing to face her. There was only one opponent left: Teacher Shen.
She hadn't played Teacher Shen since her arrival. After bringing Qi Qi here, securing her a room, and showing her around, Shen had rarely made an appearance. Qi Qi knew she carried burdens far heavier than teaching. Occasionally, Qi Qi would spot her from afar in the corridors. Teacher Shen would give a brief nod and walk right past without breaking her stride.
The following spring, Qi Qi finally sought her out.
Shen was reading by a window. Seeing the girl enter, she set her book aside, arranged the chessboard, and said, "I'll give you a Rook's handicap."
Qi Qi lost. Shen gave her a Knight's handicap, and Qi Qi lost again. Finally, they played an even match. Qi Qi fought bitterly into a grueling endgame, only to lose by a single move.
Teacher Shen reached into her sleeve, produced a letter, and placed it on the board. It was from the town. Before leaving, Shen had asked a neighbor to look after Old Qi. The letter said that he had passed away exactly nine days after they left. On his deathbed, he had left a final message for Qi Qi.
Qi Qi didn't open the letter. She simply stared at the board, motionless for a long, quiet time.
Teacher Shen broke the silence. "Old Qi said you play too frantically," she said softly. "He wanted you to know that the most brilliant moves are always hidden within the slow ones."
That night, Qi Qi unearthed a moth-eaten Xiangqi Manual deep in the library and sat alone over an endgame board until midnight.
It suddenly dawned on her: in all her time at the Inkbound Order, she hadn't truly played a single game. She had fought purely for the sake of winning, convinced that if she just won fast enough, she could finally go back to her grandfather. But every time she struck down one opponent, there was always another waiting.
So, she began to slow down.
She learned to mimic her grandfather's deliberate rhythm and Teacher Shen's quiet grace. She took her time. When she lost, she would softly say, "Beautifully played." When reviewing a match, she made sure to praise her opponent's most clever moves first. When people asked how she had become a completely different person, she simply replied, "I am just learning to play."
She still wanted to win, but the frantic urgency was gone. Her grandfather had told her that the best moves were hidden in the slow ones, and so she would play slowly, taking life one deliberate step at a time. She would wait until she had read every last chess manual in Tianyi Tower. She would wait until the day Teacher Shen no longer gave her a handicap. She would wait until she had learned all the chess the world had to offer.
Because surely, her grandfather was still waiting for her under that old tree, waiting for her to come home and play.

en:
Eternal Whispers, the waters of the Yellow River descending from Heaven,
Flowing to the sea never to return.
Eternal Whispers, bright mirrors in high halls lament white hair,
Morning like black silk, evening turned to snow.
When life is joyful, be Merry Maker,
Let not golden goblets face the moon in vain.
Heaven has made me talented, surely for use,
A thousand gold spent will come again.
Cook lamb, slaughter oxen, be merry,
Drink three hundred cups in one sitting.
Master Cen, Pill Hill scholar,
Bring in the wine, cups never stopping.
For you I sing a song,
Please lend me your ears.
Bells and drums, fine jade are not precious,
Only long drunkenness without waking.
Sages of old were all lonely,
Only drinkers left their names.
Prince Chen once feasted in Ping Le,
Ten thousand coins for wine, freely mocking.
Host, why speak of little money?
Just buy wine and drink with me.
Five-flower Horse, thousand-gold fur,
Call the boy to trade for fine wine,
To drown eternal sorrow with you.

zh:
毛手毛脚清洁铺铺长，也是唯一铺员。
铺子虽小，总有做大做强的一天吧。带着这样的期许，大强每日早出晚归，带着毛师傅帮它画的小告示，出现在不同人的家门前。
别看大强看着不大也不强，但抓小强可是一流哩！
不过猫手猫脚……在人的屋子辗转挪腾，确实不太方便。每晚回家，大强总是伤痕累累，不是磕着这里，就是抓到那里。有时候，甚至还要倒贴钱给屋主人……毛手毛脚清洁铺，又亏本啦！
好在大强是一只从不气馁的大猫，明日又是新的一日！明日，它一定会遇见心软的屋主人！不会让它倒贴钱的屋主人！
en:
The sole keeper and worker of the "Pawsitive Cleaning Co. Flyer." 
Though small and humble, the shop carries a quiet hope—to grow and thrive someday. From dawn till dusk, Dax visits doorsteps across town, advertising its services. 
Despite its modest size, Dax is unmatched at catching the pesky cockroaches! 
Yet navigating humans' homes is no easy task. Each night, Dax returns home scratched and weary—scuffed here, snagged there. Sometimes, it even has to pay the owners out of its own pocket... 
Still, Dax never loses heart. Tomorrow is another day, and surely it will meet a kind owner with a soft spot, one who won't leave it out of pocket!

晋师与契丹相持滹沱，得闻狂澜率部突围驰援，三军感奋。
然近日城关内外，却多见狂澜弟子之缉拿告令，方知晋军官兵屡遭义军残害。抗虏大局当前，天下志士本应同仇敌忾。尔等劫掠营地，斩杀兵官，自以为替天行道，实为藐视王法、扰乱军心，乃十恶不赦之重罪！
王某虽敬重贵军义勇，然为整肃军纪、稳固大局，不得不出面肃清乱行。今约大帅于入夜子时，会于滹沱南岸，一决死战，取尔项上人头，以慰军心。

王清 敬呈
en:
To Sect Master Jiujue,
The Jin army remains locked in stalemate with the Khitan along the Hutuo River. When word came that Raging Tides had cut through the enemy lines to bring relief, the whole army took heart.
And yet in recent days, wanted notices for Raging Tides' disciples have appeared both inside and outside the passes. Only then did it become clear that Jin officers and soldiers have repeatedly fallen victim to attacks by your sect. At a time like this, with the fight against the invaders hanging in the balance, all men of resolve under Heaven ought to stand together against the common enemy. Instead, you raid military camps and kill officers, all while thinking yourselves champions of justice. In truth, you defy the law, unsettle the army, and commit crimes too grave to forgive.
Much as I respect your sect's courage and sense of honor, I cannot ignore such lawless acts if military discipline is to be restored and the wider cause held together. I therefore invite you to meet me on the south bank of the Hutuo at midnight tonight, and there settle matters in a fight to the death. I will take your head and use it to steady the army's heart.
Respectfully,
Wang Qing

zh:
黄沙漫天，行路多艰。你行走于玉门关外的无垠沙海之中。口干舌燥之际，你来到一处沙丘的阴凉之处，发现了一口枯井。这口井宽可容人。你还记得这里。你曾帮助马头村的挖井人取回井下的油灯。此刻，井中传来隐隐的水声与人声。你决定…… #Y【井下晦暗，恐有凶物。】
你点起油灯，凝神屏气，一点一点向前走去。一阵风吹过，你手中的油灯摇曳挣扎，最终熄灭。好在前面有人举起火把，为你驱散了黑暗。#E你沿着水道来到一处临时搭建的落脚点。这里的人们向你自豪地讲述着马头村的过往，讲述着安西军饮马地的雄壮，讲述着几代挖井人的努力，还讲述了一位游侠的相助……你明知这是一场梦，但你仍相信，只要那盏油灯还在，井下就永远会清泉常涌，人的希望便永不枯竭。问渠哪得清如许，唯有万代执灯来。
en:
Yellow sand fills the sky, and the journey is arduous. You press on through the endless sea of dunes beyond Jade Gate Pass. Parched and faint with thirst, you come to the shaded side of a dune, where you find an old, dry well. The well is wide enough for a person to descend. You remember this place. Once, you helped the well-digger of Horsehelm Village recover an oil lamp from the depths below. At this moment, the faint murmur of water and human voices echoes from within the well. You decide to... #Y[Beware of monsters in the dark depths.]
You light the oil lamp, hold your breath in concentration, and edge forward inch by inch. A gust of wind blows past; the oil lamp in your hand flickers and struggles before finally going out. Fortunately, someone ahead raises a torch, driving away the darkness for you.#E Following the underground watercourse, you come upon a makeshift refuge. The people here speak to you with pride of Horsehelm Village's past, of the might of the Anxi Army's watering grounds, of the generations of well-diggers' efforts, and of the help once given by a wanderer... You know this is only a dream, yet you still believe that as long as that oil lamp burns, clear spring water will forever flow beneath, and human hope will never run dry. "How does the water remain so clear? Only because, through countless generations, lamp-bearers will come."

zh:
途师弟：
别来数日，北行途中余想度师弟构件之弊，或在初思。汝困于旧矩，未察其论辩相悖之处，恐继而往下，徒事无益。且暂弃此案，反其道推之，或有新得。
墨门之道，最幸熟思，思之有益。纵不得功成，亦去一错途，为后学来者留鉴。
随信附干花一枝，有老农言此独北地风物，余未曾于山中有见。特撷于信中，予二位师弟一观。临书不能万一，千万强学自重，不具。
en:
Junior Brother Tu:
Since we parted ways a few days ago, I have been pondering the flaws in your component design as I travel north. I suspect the issue lies in your initial assumptions. You are currently trapped within old conventions, failing to notice the logical contradictions they present. If you continue down this path, I fear it will be a fruitless endeavor. Set this draft aside for now and try working backward from the conclusion; perhaps you will gain a new perspective.
The greatest fortune in the Mohist Way is deep, thorough reflection, for there is always value in thought. Even if success eludes us, we at least eliminate a wrong path, serving as a cautionary guide for future scholars.
I have enclosed a dried flower with this letter. An old farmer told me this is a local flora unique to the north, something I had never seen in our mountain. I plucked it specifically to share with you two junior brothers. This brief letter cannot convey even a fraction of what is on my mind. Please strive in your studies and take good care of yourselves.

zh:
稻米算得上是承恩镇的原住民。
它出生那天，镇上燃着熊熊大火，人们四处逃窜。它的主人还没给它起名字就闭上了眼。
后来承恩镇来了许多人，稻米很开心，因为有个带着头巾的女人把它抱回了家。稻米的主人也很开心，因为田里重新长出黄黄的庄稼。
秋天到了，稻米的主人搓着饱满的稻壳，又哭又笑，泪眼朦胧间看到在田坎里玩闹的狗狗，对着它说：“你以后就叫稻米儿吧。”
稻米知道，主人和稻米一样，在承恩镇又有了家。
en:
Rice is practically a native of Gracetown.
The day he is born, the town burns. People flee everywhere. His first owner closes his eyes forever before he can even give him a name.
Then many new people come. Rice is happy, especially when a woman in a headscarf takes him home. His new owner is happy too, because golden grains are growing in the fields again.
When autumn comes, she rubs the full husks between her palms, laughing and crying, and through her tears she sees the dog playing in the rice paddies. "You," she says, "your name is Rice."
And Rice understands. Just like the rice, his owner has found a home again in Gracetown.

不一会儿，二人怀中皆塞满胜利红蛋。他们奋力挤出，盯着手里红蛋发懵，却见蛋壳裂开细纹，露出"八万""红中"麻将牌。二人对视，皆从对方眼中看出迷茫。

两人疑惑：“拿好……鸡蛋吗？”
张叔不答，只重复：“拿好了吗？”
二人看着蛋，支支吾吾：“拿……拿好了吧……”
张叔突然大吼：“快……送回去……送回去……”
“分五队……不……十队……送回去………”
两人呆滞“俩鸡蛋，分十队？送哪？”话音未落张叔飞一手一个，把二人拍向涌来的老头老太。喃喃：“小心……小心……一定要……送回去……”
望着眼睛精光的老头老太，二人自知，好嘛，又逃不掉了。
当阿达的裤腰带都松了三扣，阿达的腰带散成水草状时，老头老太终于放过了他们。
张叔魔怔般揪住他们：“送到了吗？十队！都送到了吗？”
“别说十队……二、三十队都有了……”阿景瘫在张叔面前。
张叔突然对着他们行了个抱拳礼，随后开怀大笑，转身离去。
两人一头雾水，“这也不至于给咱行礼吧？”阿达此时已经有些退缩。
“喂，还去吗？”
阿景咬咬牙，说：“都到这儿了，不问出些什么，我不甘心！”
于是二人又艰难地爬起，追随而去。
en:
Hobbling and stumbling, they followed Uncle Zhang to the competition arena. As Jing leaned against a crooked-neck locust tree by the Thirsty Horse River to catch his breath, seven or eight burly old men and women suddenly swarmed out from behind the tree. Bamboo tags marked "One Bam" and "Nine Dots" were stuck in their collars, and they clutched red eggs painted with the characters for "Victory" using cinnabar as they encircled the two youths and shouted, "Pick me! Pick me!" 
Before long, the two youths had an egg each. After fighting their way out, they stared blankly at the eggs in their hands. Then they noticed fine cracks appearing on the shells, revealing the mahjong tiles "Eight Characters" and "Red Dragon." They looked at each other, confusion mirrored in their eyes. 
"Got them?" A heavy blow landed on their backs. It was Uncle Zhang, his face stern. 
The two were puzzled. "Got... the eggs?" 
Uncle Zhang didn't answer, just repeated, "Got them?" 
Looking at the eggs, they stammered, "Yeah... I guess..."
Uncle Zhang suddenly roared, "Quick... send them back... send them back..."
"Divide into five teams... no... ten teams... send them back..."
The two stood stupefied. "Two eggs, into ten teams? Send them where?" Before they could finish, Uncle Zhang, moving like lightning, shoving them one after the other toward the oncoming old folks. He muttered, "Careful... careful... must... send them back..."
Facing the old men and women with their sharp eyes, the two knew well—once again, there was no escape. 
By the time Da's belt had loosened by three notches and Jing's had unraveled, the old folks finally let them go. 
Uncle Zhang, as if possessed, grabbed them. "Delivered? Ten teams! All delivered?" 
"Forget ten teams... twenty, thirty teams we've had..." Jing collapsed before Uncle Zhang. 
Uncle Zhang suddenly saluted them, then burst into hearty laughter and turned to leave. 
Completely baffled, Da said, "Was a salute really necessary?" He was already having second thoughts. 
"Hey, still going after him?" 
Jing gritted his teeth. "We've come this far. If I don't find out something, I won't rest easy!" 
So, with great effort, they rose and followed.

zh:
【宣公第七】

元年，春，王正月，公即位。
继故而言即位，与闻乎故也。
○公子遂如齐逆女。
○三月，遂以夫人妇姜至自齐。
其不言氏，丧未毕，故略之也。其曰妇，缘姑言之之辞也。遂之挈由上致之也。
○夏，季孙行父如齐。
○晋放其大夫胥甲父于卫。
放，犹屏也。称国以放，放无罪也。
○公会齐侯于平州。
○公子遂如齐。
○六月，齐人取济西田。
内不言取，言取，授之也，以是为赂齐也。
○秋，邾子来朝。
○楚子、郑人侵陈，遂侵宋。晋赵盾帅师救陈。宋公、陈侯、卫侯、曹伯会晋师于棐林，伐郑。
遂，继事也。善救陈也。列数诸侯而会晋赵盾，大赵盾之事也。其曰师何也？以其大之也。于棐林，地而从伐郑，疑辞也。此其地何？则著其美也。
○冬，晋赵穿帅师侵崇。
○晋人、宋人伐郑。

二年，春，王二月，壬子，宋华元帅师及郑公子归生帅师战于大棘，宋师败绩，获宋华元。
获者，不与之辞也。言尽其众，以救其将也。以三军敌华元，华元虽获，不病矣。
○秦师伐晋。
○夏，晋人、宋人、卫人、陈人侵郑。
○秋，九月，乙丑，晋赵盾弒其君夷皋。
穿弒也，盾不弒，而曰盾弒何也？以罪盾也。其以罪盾何也？曰灵公朝诸大夫而暴弹之，观其辟丸也。赵盾入谏，不听。出亡，至于郊。赵穿弒公，而后反赵盾。史狐书贼曰:"赵盾弒公。"盾曰:"天乎！天乎！予无罪，孰为盾而忍弒其君者乎？"史狐曰:"子为正卿，入谏不听，出亡不远。君弒，反不讨贼，则志同。志同则书重，非子而谁？"故书之曰，晋赵盾弒其君夷皋者，过在下也。曰，于盾也，见忠臣之至，于许世子止，见孝子之至。
○冬，十月，乙亥，天王崩。

……
en:
【Duke Xuan, Year 7】

Year 1, Spring, King's first month, the Duke assumed the throne.
When one succeeds to the throne after a ruler's unnatural death, it implies that he was involved in the circumstances of that death.
○Gongzi Sui went to Qi to welcome the bride.
○In the third month, Sui arrived from Qi with the Lady, Jiang of the wife's clan.
The omission of her clan name is because the mourning period was not yet completed, so the record is abbreviated. Calling her "the wife" is an expression spoken with reference to the mother-in-law. Sui's prominence is due to his role in escorting her here.
○Summer, Jisun Xingfu went to Qi.
○Jin exiled its Grand Master Xu Jiafu to Wei.
"Exile" is like being cast out. Naming the state in the exile indicates that the exile was without fault.
○The Duke met with the Marquis of Qi at Pingzhou.
○Gongzi Sui went to Qi.
○In the sixth month, the people of Qi took the fields west of Ji.
Within our state, we do not say "take"; saying "take" means it was given to them, as this was considered a bribe to Qi.
○Autumn, the Viscount of Zhu came to court.
○The Viscount of Chu and the people of Zheng invaded Chen, and then invaded Song. Jin's Zhao Dun led troops to rescue Chen. The Duke of Song, Marquis of Chen, Marquis of Wei, and Earl of Cao met with Jin's troops at Feilin to attack Zheng.
"Then" indicates a continuation of events. It praises the rescue of Chen. Listing the various lords together with Jin's Zhao Dun magnifies Zhao Dun's achievement. Why say "at Feilin"? Because it was a place from which they proceeded to attack Zheng, expressing doubt. Why record this place? To highlight their merit.
○Winter, Jin's Zhao Chuan led troops to invade Chong.
○The people of Jin and the people of Song attacked Zheng.

Year 2, Spring, King's second month, Renzi day, Song's Hua Yuan led troops and fought against Zheng's Gongzi Guisheng who led troops, at Daji. Song's troops were defeated, and Song's Hua Yuan was captured.
"Captured" is an expression of disapproval. It says that all his troops were exhausted in order to save their general. Pitting three armies against Hua Yuan, even though Hua Yuan was captured, he was not disgraced.
○Qin's troops attacked Jin.
○Summer, the people of Jin, Song, Wei, and Chen invaded Zheng.
○Autumn, ninth month, Yichou day, Jin's Zhao Dun assassinated his ruler Yigao.
It was Zhao Chuan who committed the assassination, not Zhao Dun. Why say "Zhao Dun assassinated him"? To condemn Zhao Dun. Why condemn Zhao Dun? It is said that Duke Ling summoned the great officers to court and violently shot at them with pellets, watching them dodge the pellets. Zhao Dun entered to remonstrate, but was not heeded. He went into exile, reaching the outskirts. Zhao Chuan assassinated the Duke, and then brought Zhao Dun back. The historian Hu recorded the criminal as saying: "Zhao Dun assassinated the Duke." Dun said: "Heaven! Heaven! I am innocent. Who would be Zhao Dun and bear to assassinate his ruler?" Hu said: "You were the chief minister. You entered to remonstrate and were not heeded. You went into exile but not far. When the ruler was assassinated, you returned but did not punish the criminal, so your intent was the same. When intent is the same, the record emphasizes the more important one. If not you, then who?" Therefore, it is recorded that Jin's Zhao Dun assassinated his ruler Yigao, because the fault lay with him. It is said that in Zhao Dun, we see the utmost of a loyal minister; in Xu's heir apparent Zhi, we see the utmost of a filial son.
○Winter, tenth month, Yihai day, the Heavenly King passed away.

……

8. Sugar Cakes

zh:
一曲惊舟湖上，不知归梦难留。玉京多情故人，弦上话说从头。

像江逸这样弱冠年纪便精通百般乐器的人，照理是可以狂妄的。但他其实没这个心情。于他来说，音乐只是语言的一种。字句说不清的东西，用音律偏能顺畅地说出来，于是江逸自然而然地终日与乐为伍，回过神来才听说自己被人称道“音律奇才”。但这门语言就像一种偏门的家乡话，知者甚少。大多数时，江逸只是一个漂泊的失乡之人。
所以当醉花阴邀他入樊楼奏乐赏曲，江逸是很高兴的。他知醉花阴有燕乐坊精研音律，有好乐亦有好乐人，于是急匆匆就赶去。

那是一个很好的日子。前往樊楼的花船上，江逸都已坐不住，立在船头，一靠岸便跳了上去。引荐者带他至燕乐坊，还未见人，先闻笛声。
耳朵一亮，心却一沉。那笛声清越，技巧无可挑剔，音色是明亮的，可亮色其下却是一股郁结。江逸不知乐手是谁，经历如何，但他为这笛声难过。
他在那人身后站定。在一首曲子的光景里，江逸就只是安静地看他。此人身材瘦削，笛声却气息充盈，声有贯天地之势。而当他转身看到江逸时，自然是吓了一跳，问他是谁。

“我是江逸，受邀来樊楼演乐”——原本只要这样说便好了，但他忽然激动得说不出话。那隐约好似将要靠岸的激动。他三步并作两步，坐到一旁的琴边，抚了一首曲子。乐音流出，方才所闻笛声中的叹息化入指间。一曲终了，他才抬起头。之前的吹笛人已坐在琴前，问他：“这曲子有名字吗？”
江逸这才开口：“只是随兴而弹。”
“有归人之细微情意，又有山海之大气；有‘海上明月共潮生’的妙丽，又有‘人生代代无穷已’的洒脱。叫《山海归梦》如何？”
江逸想想，点点头：“名字很好。”
那人冷不丁地又说：“你是江逸。”
“是我。先生是？”
他却没回答，只是一笑：“我为你的曲子取了个名字，那你给我的也取一个？”
“我不擅长取名，也不擅长说话，这才以琴代言。”
“原来如此。你说得很好。”吹笛人点了点他放在弦上的手。
“师傅怎在调笑贵客！”一个轻巧的女声打断他们。一位略显稚嫩的女子走进屋子，“江先生，您一转眼就不见了，原来您已经自己来见坊主了。”
江逸恍然：“坊主……这位是燕乐坊坊主，难怪笛声如此动人。”
坊主道：“与江先生或可相提并论？”
江逸连忙拱手：“远不比坊主先生。”
“坊主先生叫着生分，叫我韩微就好。玉茗，江先生的住处可安排好了？”
“都安排妥当。”唤作凌玉茗的娘子眉毛一挑，“方才我在楼下听有人抚琴，大气潇洒，不似师傅平日的琴声。原来是江逸先生弹的？真好听。”
韩微道：“什么意思，说我弹琴小气？”
凌玉茗嬉笑：“不及江先生气度！”
江逸红着脸打断：“你们夸得也太过头了，我无非就会得乐器多一些……韩先生年纪轻轻已是坊主，造诣自然比我高得多。”
凌玉茗叹气：“你听听，‘无非会得多一些’！听你们这些天才说话真是气死庸人。”
江逸瞪大眼睛，连连摆手：“我我我……我没这个意思，姑娘你……你的手指很长，很适合弹琴，怎会是庸人！”
韩微拍手大笑：“江先生百般乐器精通，这张嘴却是实在不太好使！”
江逸被人笑话却也没恼，收了笑，轻声道：“还是先生的笛声厉害，把话都说尽了。”
于是韩微就此一怔。
幽幽花香穿过厅堂。江逸到访之前，京城刚下过一场大雨，此时雨过天晴，高楼风好，琴曲余音荡漾；此时艳湖十曲的约定还没立下，韩微尚未遗世，江逸不曾归隐，凌玉茗还不是那个忧愁的花信风。那些举世无双的曲子还只是无名的随兴之作。而终将扑面的死亡与遗憾也只潜伏暗处，尚未露出爪牙。
那真是一个很好的日子。
en:
The zither's music spreads across the lake in gentle waves, a quiet sigh for how fate—not we—decides our meetings and farewells. In the capital, old bonds run deep, and through each lingering note, the stories of the past are softly told anew. 

Jiang Yi, though barely twenty, is already a virtuoso on countless instruments. By all rights, he could be arrogant—but he's not. To him, music is simply another language. What words cannot fully express, melodies carry with graceful ease. So naturally, he spends his days immersed in music, only gradually realizing others regard him as a "musical prodigy." Yet this language he speaks is rare, a dialect known to few, and most days, Jiang Yi feels like a wanderer far from home. 
That's why, when Velvet Shade invited him to perform at Revelry Hall and enjoy a night of music, Jiang was genuinely delighted. He knew Velvet Shade was closely connected with Grace Pavilion—a place famed for its masterful musicians and exquisite instruments—and so he hurried over without a moment's delay. 

It was a perfect day. On the flower-laden boat approaching Revelry Hall, Jiang could hardly contain himself; he stood at the bow, and the moment they reached shore, he leapt off the boat. Guided inside Grace Pavilion, he hadn't even caught sight of anyone before the sound of a flute reached his ears. 
His senses sharpened, yet a weight settled in his chest. The flute's tone was crystal clear, the technique flawless, and its timbre brilliantly radiant. But beneath that shining clarity lingered a profound sorrow, a hidden ache. Jiang didn't know who the player was or what trials he had endured, but the sadness in that music touched him deeply. 
He stood quietly behind the flutist, watching in silence as the melody unfolded. The man was slender, yet the breath behind his flute filled the room with a power that seemed to pierce through the skies. When the flutist finally turned and caught sight of Jiang, he startled, asking softly who the newcomer was. 

He had meant only to say, "I'm Jiang Yi, invited to perform at Revelry Hall," but the words caught in his throat, swept away by a sudden surge of emotion—like the quiet thrill of a boat drawing close to shore. Instead, he rushed to a nearby zither and let his hands speak for him. As the melody unfurled, the quiet ache he had heard in that flute earlier wove itself naturally into his playing. When the final note faded, he finally raised his head. The flutist was already seated opposite him at the zither bench, asking, "Does this piece have a name?" 
Jiang found his voice. "I just played what came to me." 
"There's the delicate longing of someone returning home, the vast breath of mountains and seas; a touch of the beauty in the moonlit sea, and the freedom of life flowing on through countless generations. What do you think of calling it ‘Dream of Mountains and Seas'?" 
Jiang considered it and then nodded. "It's a beautiful name." 
The man suddenly added, "So, you are Jiang Yi." 
"I am. And you, sir?" 
He didn't answer. He only smiled. "I named your piece. Shouldn't you name mine?" 
"I'm not good at naming things. I'm not good with words at all. That's why I let the music speak." 
"Ah. And you speak it well." The flutist tapped lightly on the hand Jiang still rested on the strings. 
"Master, how can you tease an honored guest like that!" A lively young voice cut in. A girl, still with a touch of youthful innocence, stepped into the room. "Master Jiang, you disappeared in an instant—I see you found the pavilion master all on your own." 
Jiang suddenly realized, "So this is the master of Grace Pavilion—no wonder the flute sounded so captivating." 
The master smiled, "Do you think you're on equal footing with me, Master Jiang?" 
Jiang quickly cupped his hands respectfully, "Far from it, Master Han." 
"Please, no need for such formalities—just call me Han Wei. Yuming, has Master Jiang's lodging been arranged?" 
"All taken care of," replied Ling Yuming, raising an intrigued brow. "Earlier, I caught the sound of a zither downstairs—bold and free, quite unlike your usual style. So it was Master Jiang? Truly exquisite." 
Han chuckled, "Are you implying my playing is stingy?" 
Ling teased gently, "Not nearly as grand as Master Jiang's." 
Blushing, Jiang hurried to interrupt, "You flatter me too much. I simply happen to know more instruments... As the young master of Grace Pavilion, Master Han outperforms me by far." 
Ling sighed with a smile, "Listen to that—‘just happen to know more instruments.' Hearing geniuses speak so modestly can frustrate the rest of us." 
Jiang's eyes widened as he waved his hands nervously, "No, no, not at all! Miss, your fingers are long and graceful—perfect for playing. You could never be ordinary!" 
Han laughed heartily, "Master Jiang may master many instruments, but he sure is shy of his words!" 
Taking their teasing in stride, Jian smiled softly, "Still, it's your flute, Master Han, that truly speaks—the words music cannot express." 
Han fell silent, a thoughtful look crossing his face. 
A delicate floral fragrance drifted through the hall. Before Jiang's arrival, rain had swept through the capital. Now, under clear skies and a gentle breeze weaving between the tall buildings, the lingering echoes of music filled the air. At this moment, the promise of the legendary "Ten Ballads of Pearlglow Lake" had yet to be made; Han was not yet withdrawn from the world; Jiang had not yet retreated into seclusion; and Ling was far from the wistful Flower Messenger she would become. Those unmatched melodies were still nameless, spontaneous creations, and the shadows of inevitable loss and sorrow lay quietly in wait, claws yet concealed. 
It was, in truth, a perfect day.

zh:
夫君是京城新晋的翰林院大学士，在他宴请宾朋把酒言欢那日，我却在产床上，一尸两命。原是因公主看上我夫君，而夫君为了攀附权贵，竟与公主里应外合，要扫清一切障碍。而我，便是那最大的绊脚石。
他们买通产婆，对我狠下毒手。而我那可怜的父母，还被蒙在鼓里，对他深信不疑。他，更是为了公主势力，不惜架空我家权势，最终害得我爹娘惨死。
我作为一缕孤魂，目睹了这一切。在我死后，他才在我墓前缓缓道出了真相。假的，全是假的。
我叫沈楚楚，是相国府至高无上的嫡千金小姐。而我的夫君，齐安旭，本是个落魄进士，若非我父母倾力相助，他怎会成为那最年轻的翰林院大学士？
想当年，他因状元宴上直言不讳，得罪了圣上，只能做个默默无闻的文书。而我，与他茶会初遇，为他的才学倾倒后。日日与他相会于聚德楼。即便他囊中羞涩，也总不肯让我破费半分，只说“小姐金枝玉叶，怎可让小姐出钱”。楼中时光，我们吟诗作对，情意渐浓。
而后某一日，突然不知哪处窜出个刺客，他，一届手无缚鸡之力的书生，竟为我挺身而出。那一刻，我便死心塌地要嫁给他，即便父母反对，我也执意如此。见我如此坚决，父母终是妥协，还赠予我丰厚的嫁妆。嫁入他家后，我倾尽所有，助他从那落魄小官，一步步跻身翰林掌院。
可谁曾想，那挺身而出，竟是提前买通的戏码；那诗词歌赋，皆是他人代笔之作；那茶楼付的金银，皆是他借来的外债。婚后，我还需用嫁妆为他填补那无尽的窟窿。我所付出的，所承受的，竟是一场天大的笑话！
这一世，我重生了。我在相会那日提前去了茶馆，果然听见他与他人侃侃而谈：“她不过是条狗，我要让对我痴迷不已，每日为我洗衣做饭，我岂会看上她？只是贪恋她家的权势罢了。”
还好，还好。我还未与父亲争执。现下，我心中已是一片清明。此生，我誓要为自己，为爹娘，讨回公道。
加入古书铺同仁会，百部话本任君借阅。
en:
My husband, newly appointed as a Grand Scholar of the Hanlin Academy, was raising a toast with his guests on the day I died in childbirth, taking our unborn child with me. It was all because a princess had set her sights on him. To climb the ladder and win her favor, he colluded with her to clear away any obstacles, and I was the greatest one.

They bribed the midwife to poison me. My poor parents, still kept in the dark, trusted him wholeheartedly. He even went so far as to strip my family of its power to better serve the princess's ambitions, leading to my parents' tragic deaths.

As a drifting soul, I witnessed it all. Only after my death did he stand before my grave and confess. The promises, the affection... all lies.

I am Shen Chuchu, the cherished daughter of the Chancellor's household. And my husband Qi Anxu was once a penniless palace graduate, a nobody. If not for my parents' full support, how could he ever have become the youngest Grand Scholar?

In the past, he had offended the Emperor during the Scholar's Banquet and was relegated to obscurity. I met him by chance at a tea party and was enchanted by his talents. We frequently met at the Jude Teahouse since then. Though he was poor, he never let me spend a coin, always saying, "How could a noble lady be made to pay?" We composed poetry and traded verses, our feelings for each other grew thicker.

One day, an assassin suddenly showed up. He, a frail scholar, shielded me with his own body. In that moment, I swore to marry him, no matter how my parents objected. Seeing my determination, they compromised, and even provided a generous dowry. After our marriage, I gave him everything, helping him rise from a lowly clerk all the way to the pinnacle of the Academy.

But who would have thought, the so-called heroic was staged, the poems ghostwritten, the money borrowed on credit. After our marriage, it was my dowry that filled the endless holes he left behind. Everything I sacrificed, everything I endured, was nothing but a cruel joke.

In this life, I have been reborn. I went to the teahouse early on the day we were to meet, and overheard him laughing with another: "She's just a dog. I'll make her fall for me, cook and clean for me every single day. You really think I'd ever really care for her? I'm only after her family's power."

Thank the heavens I had not yet confronted my father. Now, my heart is crystal clear. In this life, I swear to find justice for myself and for my parents.

81阶及以上等级的装备在完成定音后即可开放转律和变音。
#Y转律#E：消耗转律石，可变化一个指定的调律词条，且必定为一个选定流派内的推荐词条。可加入品质保底材料。每件装备最多转律一次。
每件装备最多转律一个词条，初始词条不能转，达到91阶的装备可以对已转律词条进行再转律，无次数限制有时间间隔，再转律时首次转律覆盖的词条、当前词条、当前装备使用相同转律库转出过的词条均不会再出现。
#Y变音#E：选择定音库后，消耗定音石和变音石后即可在对应定音库中重新随机一条。
变音前后的词条种类可能相同，游侠可自行选择是否覆盖旧定音效果，未选择词条会进入历史变音库，可消耗20长鸣玉重新启用。变音时若随机到与当前定音相同类型的词条，则数值必定提升。

#Y定音自选#E：达到91阶的装备变音累积达到一定次数时，可获得一次定音自选机会，每件装备的普通定音和止戈定音分别独立计数。
定音自选无需消耗变音材料，只能自选词条类型，选定后词条数值会按照变音规则随机生成。
转变为承音装备时会重置变音保底计数。
en:
Gear of Tier 81+ unlocks Retuning and Re-attuning after Attunement.
#YRetuning#E: Spend a Retuning Stone to replace one selected Tuning attribute with a recommended attribute from the chosen path. You may add a Quality Guarantee material. Each piece of gear can be Retuned once, and only one attribute can be Retuned.
Tier 91 gear can reroll the Retuned attribute multiple times, with a cooldown between rerolls. During rerolls, the originally replaced attribute, the current attribute, and any attributees previously rolled from the same Retuning pool for that gear will not appear again.
#YRe-attuning#E: Choose an Attunement pool, then spend an Attunement Stone plus a Re-attunement Stone to reroll one Attunement attribute from that pool. You can decide whether to replace the existing effect. Unchosen results are saved in Re-attuning History and can be reactivated for 20 Echo Jade. If you roll the same attribute type again, its value will increase.

zh:
孙乐天刚把他娘前一天熬好的臊子摆出来，正擦着洒出来的汁水，今天第一位客人就上门来了。
“哟，换新床子了？”来的客人年约四五十，看起来很面善。
“对，前几年就换了。”孙乐天笑了笑，“客官要点啥？”
“上次来你还在帮你娘算账呢，能独挡一面了，挺好。”
客人要了最普通的饸饹面加一份臊子。孙乐天把面团放进饸饹床子的凹槽里，看着它从底下漏成一条条面线，盘在碗中。
小的时候他总觉着轧面是件很有意思的事。放进去的是一个胖圆的面团子，轧出来的却是一碗细面。要是有不同的花头，还可以轧出柳叶面、宽面……
趁娘不注意的时候，小乐天会偷偷踮起脚去够桌上的木架子，瞪大了双眼等它从洞里漏出来，像是在看变戏法一样。
要是娘忙得忘了训斥他，会直接把小乐天轧出来的面浇上汁，端给客人。
小乐天就在一旁目不转睛地盯着客人的反应，稍有餍足之色，小乐天一整天都会沾沾自喜，觉着自己那一轧居功甚伟。
摊子上的客人来了又走，饸饹床子也坏了又修，修了又换。如今，孙乐天再也不觉得轧出细长的饸饹面有什么神奇的地方。
但他依旧会因为客人的几句赞扬而悄悄高兴。
孙乐天把这些夸赞都攒在心里，等回到家，慢慢说给娘听。
en:
Sun Letian had just set out the sauce his mother had simmered the day before. He was wiping up a spill when the first customer of the day stepped in.
"Well, look at that. New press?" The customer was a friendly-looking man in his forties or fifties.
"Yeah. Replaced it a few years back." Sun Letian smiled. "What can I get you?"
"Last time I came, you were still helping your ma with the books. Now you're running the stall yourself. Good. Real good."
The customer ordered the simplest bowl of Hele noodles, plus an extra serving of sauce.

Sun Letian packed the dough into the press and watched thin strands spill out from the bottom, coiling neatly into the bowl. As a kid, he used to find it fascinating: a plump ball of dough went in, and a bowl of fine noodles came out. With a few tweaks, you could even press different shapes.
Whenever his mother wasn't looking, little Letian would sneak up on tiptoe, eyes wide, waiting for the noodles to appear like a magic trick. If she was too busy to scold him, she'd ladle sauce over the noodles he pressed and serve them to a customer.
He would stand off to the side, studying the customer's face. The smallest hint of satisfaction would have him quietly proud all day, convinced he'd done something important.

Customers came and went. The press broke, got fixed, and was replaced again. These days, Letian no longer found anything magical about those long, thin strands.
But a few words of praise from a customer could still make him happy. He kept every compliment tucked away, saving them to tell his mother when he got home.

此处也算女子闺房，我不便进入，于是只是远远地观察了前院的景象。院落倒是宽敞，靠窗赫然养着一架花，开得极好。石桌上的棋局尚未结束，好像在等谁回来一决胜负，一只蹴鞠慢悠悠地滚过来，也不怕被人顺手捞走……明明她们此刻多半屏息噤声，投入到肃穆的宫务之中，但我总觉得那几声嬉笑还留在风里，就在这方庭院之中，未曾散去。
每当她们结束宫务，回到庭院中，这阵风又会顺从天性，活泼地流动起来吧。
en:
The palace's endless rows of bricks and tiles are enough to make your eyes blur, but there's one place you can recognize by ear alone. If you catch a burst of bright laughter, it's likely the Inner Quarters where the palace women live.
It's a private space, so I didn't go in. I only watched the front courtyard from a distance. It was spacious. A trellis by the window was heavy with blossoms. An unfinished game still sat on the stone table, as if waiting for someone to return and settle the score. A cuju ball rolled by at its own pace, not the least bit worried someone might scoop it up.
They are probably quiet now, absorbed in solemn palace duties, but I can't shake the feeling that the laughter is still in the wind, lingering in this courtyard. When their work is done and they come back, the breeze will surely grow lively again.

【国风·周南】

关雎

关关雎鸠，在河之洲。窈窕淑女，君子好逑。
参差荇菜，左右流之。窈窕淑女，寤寐求之。
求之不得，寤寐思服。悠哉悠哉，辗转反侧。
参差荇菜，左右采之。窈窕淑女，琴瑟友之。

葛覃

葛之覃兮，施于中谷，维叶萋萋。黄鸟于飞，集于灌木，其鸣喈喈。
葛之覃兮，施于中谷，维叶莫莫。是刈是濩，为𫄨为绤，服之无𭣧。
言告师氏，言告言归。薄污我私，薄澣我衣。害澣害否，归宁父母。

卷耳

采采卷耳，不盈顷筐。嗟我怀人，置彼周行。
陟彼崔嵬，我马虺𬯎。我姑酌彼金罍，维以不永怀。
陟彼高岗，我马玄黄。我姑酌彼兕觥，维以不永伤。
陟彼砠矣，我马瘏矣，我仆𤸵矣，云何吁矣。

樛木

南有樛木，葛藟累之。乐只君子，福履绥之。
南有樛木，葛藟荒之。乐只君子，福履将之。
南有樛木，葛藟萦之。乐只君子，福履成之。

螽斯

螽斯羽，诜诜兮，宜尔子孙，振振兮。
螽斯羽，薨薨兮，宜尔子孙，绳绳兮。
螽斯羽，揖揖兮，宜尔子孙，蛰蛰兮。

桃夭

桃之夭夭，灼灼其华。之子于归，宜其室家。
桃之夭夭，有蕡其实。之子于归，宜其家室。
桃之夭夭，其叶蓁蓁。之子于归，宜其家人。

兔罝

肃肃兔罝，椓之丁丁。赳赳武夫，公侯干城。
肃肃兔罝，施于中逵。赳赳武夫，公侯好仇。
肃肃兔罝，施于中林。赳赳武夫，公侯腹心。

芣苡

采采芣苡，薄言采之。采采芣苡，薄言有之。
采采芣苡，薄言掇之。采采芣苡，薄言捋之。
采采芣苡，薄言袺之。采采芣苡，薄言𮖱之。

汉广

南有乔木，不可休思。汉有游女，不可求思。汉之广矣，不可泳思。江之永矣，不可方思。
翘翘错薪，言刈其楚。之子于归，言秣其马。汉之广矣，不可泳思。江之永矣，不可方思。
翘翘错薪，言刈其蒌。之子于归，言秣其驹。汉之广矣，不可泳思。江之永矣，不可方思。

汝坟

遵彼汝坟，伐其条枚。未见君子，惄如调饥。
遵彼汝坟，伐其条肄。既见君子，不我遐弃。
鲂鱼赪尾，王室如毁。虽则如毁，父母孔迩。

麟之趾

麟之趾，振振公子。于嗟麟兮。
麟之定，振振公姓。于嗟麟兮。
麟之角，振振公族。于嗟麟兮。
en:
[Odes: Zhou South]

Guan Ju

Hark! from the islet in the stream the voice
Of the fish-hawks that o'er their nest rejoice!
From them our thoughts to that young lady go,
Modest and virtuous, loth herself to show.
Where could be found, to share our prince's state,
So fair, so virtuous, and so fit a mate?
See how the duckweed's stalks, or short or long,
Sway left and right, as moves the current strong!
So hard it was for him the maid to find!
By day, by night, our prince with constant mind
Sought for her long, but all his search was vain.
Awake, asleep, he ever felt the pain
Of longing thought, as when on restless bed,
Tossing about, one turns one's fevered head.
Here long, there short, afloat the duckweed lies;
But caught at last, we seize the longed-for prize.
The maiden modest, virtuous, coy, is found;
Strike every lute, and joyous welcome sound.
Ours now, the duckweed from the stream we bear,
And cook to use with other viands rare.
He has the maiden, modest, virtuous, bright;
Let bells and drums proclaim our great delight.

Ge Tan

Sweet was the scene. The spreading dolichos
Extended far, down to the valley's depths,
With leaves luxuriant. The orioles
Fluttered around, and on the bushy trees
In throngs collected—whence their pleasant notes
Resounded far in richest melody.
The spreading dolichos extended far,
Covering the valley's sides, down to its depths,
With leaves luxuriant and dense. I cut
It down, then boiled, and from the fibres span
Of cloth, both fine and coarse, large store,
To wear, unwearied of such simple dress.
Now back to my old home, my parents dear
To see, I go. The matron I have told,
Who will announcement make. Meanwhile my clothes,
My private clothes I wash, and rinse my robes.
Which of them need be rinsed and which need not?
My parents dear to visit, back I go.

Juan Er

Though small my basket, all my toil
Filled it with mouse-ears but in part.
I set it on the path, and sighed
For the dear master of my heart.
My steeds, o'er-tasked, their progress stayed,
When midway up that rocky height.
Give me a cup from that gilt vase,
When shall this longing end in sight?
To mount that lofty ridge I drove,
Until my steeds all changed their hue.
A cup from that rhinoceros' horn
May help my longing to subdue.
Striving to reach that flat-topped hill,
My steeds, worn out, relaxed their strain;
My driver also sank oppressed:
I'll never see my lord again!

Jiu Mu

In the South are the trees whose branches are bent,
And droop in such fashion that o'er their extent
All the dolichos' creepers fast cling.
See our princely lady, from whom we have got
Rejoicing that's endless! May her happy lot
And her honours repose ever bring!
In the South are the trees whose branches are bent,
And droop in such fashion that o'er their extent
All the dolichos' creepers are spread.
See our princely lady, from whom we have got
Rejoicing that's endless! Of her happy lot
And her honours the greatness ne'er fade!
In the South are the trees whose branches are bent,
And droop in such fashion that o'er their extent
All the dolichos' creepers entwine.
See our princely lady, from whom we have got
Rejoicing that's endless. May her happy lot
And her honours complete ever shine!

Zhong Si

Ye locusts, winged tribes,
Gather in concord fine;
Well your descendants may
In numerous bright hosts shine!
Ye locusts, winged tribes,
Your wings in flight resound;
Well your descendants may
In endless lines be found!
Ye locusts, winged tribes,
Together cluster strong;
Well your descendants may
In swarms for ever throng!

Tao Yao

Graceful and young the peach tree stands;
How rich its flowers, all gleaming bright!
This bride to her new home repairs;
Chamber and house she'll order right.
Graceful and young the peach tree stands;
Large crops of fruit it soon will show.
This bride to her new home repairs;
Chamber and house her sway shall know.
Graceful and young the peach tree stands,
Its foliage clustering green and full.
This bride to her new home repairs;
Her household will attest her rule.

Tu Ju

Careful he sets his rabbit-nets all round;
Chang-chang his blows upon the pegs resound.
Stalwart the man and bold his bearing all
Shows he might be his prince's shield and wall.
Careful he is his rabbit-nets to place,
Where many paths of rabbits' feet bear trace.
Stalwart the man and bold 'tis plain to see
He to his prince companion good would be.
Careful he is his rabbit-nets to spread,
Where in the forest's depth the trees give shade.
Stalwart the man and bold fit his the part
Guide to his prince to be, and faithful heart.

Fu Yi

We gather and gather the plantains;
Come gather them anyhow.
Yes, gather and gather the plantains,
And here we have got them now.
We gather and gather the plantains;
Now off the ears we must tear.
Yes, gather and gather the plantains,
And now the seeds are laid bare.
We gather and gather the plantains,
The seeds in our skirts are placed.
Yes, gather and gather the plantains.
Ho! safe in the girdled waist!

Han Guang

High and compressed, the southern trees
No shelter from the sun afford.
The girls free ramble by the Han,
But will not hear enticing word.
Like the broad Han are they,
Through which one cannot dive;
And like the Jiang's long stream,
Wherewith no raft can strive.
Many the faggots bound and piled;
The thorns I'd hew still more to make.
As brides, those girls their new homes seek;
Their colts to feed I'd undertake.
Like the broad Han are they,
Through which one cannot dive;
And like the Jiang's long stream,
Wherewith no raft can strive.
Many the faggots bound and piled;
The southernwood I'd cut for more.
As brides, those girls their new homes seek;
Food for their colts I'd bring large store.
Like the broad Han are they,
Through which one cannot dive;
And like the Jiang's long stream,
Wherewith no raft can strive.

Ru Fen

Along the raised banks of the Ru,
To hew slim stem and branch I wrought,
My lord away, my husband true,
Like hunger-pang my troubled thought!
Along the raised banks of the Ru,
Branch and fresh shoot confessed my art.
I've seen my lord, my husband true,
And still he folds me in his heart.
As the toiled bream makes red its tail,
Toil you, Sir, for the royal House,
Amidst its blazing fires, nor quail:
Your parents see you pay your vows.

Lin Zhi Zhi

As the feet of the lin, which avoid each living thing,
So our prince's noble sons no harm to people will bring.
They are the lin!
As the front of the lin, never forward thrust in wrath,
So our prince's noble grandsons of love tread the path.
They are the lin!
As the horn of the lin, flesh-tipped, no wound to give,
So our prince's noble kindred kindly with all live.
They are the lin!

有人在唱歌，所以她醒过来，坐在窗边听。

起风了，叶子刷刷响，才叫回阿然的心神。

对了，阿然还没有跟爹爹说过，大侠把金叶子带回来的那天晚上，她做了一个梦呢，梦见——
⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛
en:
Zheng Ran noticed that the crackling of fires in Kaifeng City had vanished, and the scorching, acrid smells had faded. When people walked down the streets, the jingle of the coin pouches in their robes sounded somehow fuller and weightier.
When did it begin...? Right, it was that night, the night someone was singing.
That singing woke her, so she sat by the window to listen.
Someone was roaring in anger, so she leaned out toward the sound, listening even more intently.
The wind picked up, and the rustling leaves brought Ran back to her senses.
Then... what happened then? Then the wanderer arrived! The street vendors' cries grew livelier, and the stench of rotting wood faded. Father came home!
Oh, right! Ran still hasn't told Father that on the night the wanderer brought back the gold leaf, she had a dream. She dreamed of...

游侠敬启： 
近来可好？托您的福，我已经进了行伍，成了正经的驿夫啦！我从开封出发，现下路过十六巷驿站，想了想，还是给您写封信！ 
故地重游，总会觉得很开心！上次来的时候还是元宵佳节，如今都已快三月了！可惜浮元子过季，掌柜说他们家马上要卖青团。下次我可一定要尝尝！ 
我没找到您，到处打听，没想到您的故事这么精彩！哈哈！每次打听到了您的消息，我都会告诉他们：“你们说的那位大侠，是我朋友！”有的人相信我说的话，可也有的人说我胡诌。等有机会，我一定请您在最好吃的馆子吃顿饭，好让他们看看！ 
您之前提到，可能要去河西。也不知道您出发了没。 
这艘福舟是我们一起做的，希望您带在身上，保佑平安！ 
让这艘福舟，随您逐水而去。世间流水，总能让人相遇。 
还记得做福舟的时候，我们最后的祈福嘛！ 
愿您——顺遂安宁，心想事成！
en:
To the Great Hero, 
How have you been? Thanks to your blessings, I've joined the military and become a proper courier now! I set off from Kaifeng and am currently passing through the Sixteen Lanes post station. After some thought, I decided to write you a letter! 
Revisiting old places always brings me joy! Last time I was here, it was during the Lantern Festival, and now it's almost March! Sadly, the seasonal glutinous rice balls are no longer available. The Shopkeeper said they'll soon be selling Qingtuan (green rice cakes). Next time, I must definitely try them! 
I couldn’t find you and asked around, only to discover how amazing your stories are! Ha Ha! Every time I heard news about you, I’d tell people, “That Great Hero you’re talking about is my friend!” Some believed me, while others said I was making it up. When the chance arises, I’ll treat you to a meal at the best restaurant—just to prove them wrong! 
You mentioned before that you might be heading to Hexi. I wonder if you’ve already set off. 
This Lucky Boat was made together by us—I hope you carry it with you for safety and blessings! 
May this Lucky Boat follow you as you journey along the waters. The world’s flowing streams always bring people together. 
Do you remember our final blessing when we made the Lucky Boat? 
Wishing you—peace, prosperity, and all your dreams fulfilled!

zh:
【定公第十一】

元年，春，王。
定何以无正月？正月者，正即位也。定无正月者，即位后也。即位何以后？昭公在外，得入不得入，未可知也。曷为未可知？在季氏也。定、哀多微辞，主人习其读而问其传，则未知己之有罪焉尔。
〇三月，晋人执宋仲几于京师。
仲几之罪何？不蓑城也。其言于京师何？伯讨也。伯讨则其称人何？贬。曷为贬？不与大夫专执也。曷为不与？实与而文不与。文曷为不与？大夫之义，不得专执也。
〇夏，六月，癸亥，公之丧至自乾侯。
〇戊辰，公即位。
癸亥，公之丧至自乾侯，则曷为以戊辰之日，然后即位？正棺于两楹之间，然后即位。子沈子曰："定君乎国，然后即位。"即位不日，此何以日？录乎内也。
〇秋，七月，癸巳，葬我君昭公。
〇九月，大雩。
〇立炀宫。
炀宫者何？炀公之宫也。立者何？立者不宜立也。立炀宫，非礼也。
〇冬，十月，𫕥霜杀菽。
何以书？记异也。此灾菽也，曷为以异书？异大乎灾也。

二年，春，王正月。
〇夏，五月，壬辰，雉门及两观灾。
其言雉门及两观灾何？两观微也。然则曷为不言雉门灾及两观？主灾者两观也。主灾者两观，则曷为后言之？不以微及大也。何以书？记灾也。
〇秋，楚人伐吴。
〇冬，十月，新作雉门及两观。
其言新作之何？修大也。修旧不书，此何以书？讥。何讥尔？不务乎公室也。

……
en:
【Duke Ding, Year 11】

First year, spring, the King.
Why does Ding not have the first month? The first month is for the proper enthronement. Ding has no first month because his enthronement came later. Why later? Duke Zhao was abroad; whether he could return or not was unknown. Why unknown? It depended on the Ji family. Ding and Ai contain many subtle expressions; the master, familiar with their reading, asks about their commentaries, yet does not know that he himself has faults.
〇Third month, the people of Jin seized Song Zhongji at the capital.
What was Zhongji's crime? He did not complete the city walls. Why mention "at the capital"? Because it was a punishment by the chief. If it was a punishment by the chief, why call them "people"? To贬低. Why贬低? Because it does not allow a minister to seize someone on his own authority. Why not allow it? In reality it allows it, but in writing it does not. Why does the writing not allow it? Because the duty of a minister is not to seize on his own authority.
〇Summer, sixth month, Guihai, the Duke's funeral cortege arrived from Qianhou.
〇Wuchen, the Duke assumed the throne.
If the funeral cortege arrived on Guihai, why did he assume the throne on the day of Wuchen? He first placed the coffin properly between the two pillars, then assumed the throne. Master Zishen said: "First settle the ruler in the state, then assume the throne." Enthronements are not dated; why is this one dated? To record what happened within the state.
〇Autumn, seventh month, Guisi, we buried our ruler Duke Zhao.
〇Ninth month, great rain sacrifice.
〇Established the Yang Temple.
What is the Yang Temple? It is the temple of Duke Yang. What does "established" mean? "Established" means it should not have been established. Establishing the Yang Temple was against ritual.
〇Winter, tenth month, frost killed the beans.
Why is this recorded? To record an anomaly. This harmed the beans; why record it as an anomaly? Because anomalies are greater than disasters.

Second year, spring, the King's first month.
〇Summer, fifth month, Renwu, the Pheasant Gate and the two towers caught fire.
Why say "the Pheasant Gate and the two towers caught fire"? The two towers were minor. If so, why not say "the Pheasant Gate fire and the two towers"? Because the main fire was in the two towers. If the main fire was in the two towers, why mention them later? To not let the minor overshadow the major. Why record it? To record a disaster.
〇Autumn, the people of Chu attacked Wu.
〇Winter, tenth month, newly built the Pheasant Gate and the two towers.
Why say "newly built"? Because it was a major repair. Repairs of old structures are not recorded; why is this recorded? To criticize. What is criticized? Not attending to the Duke's household.

……

只不过万事终究讲究个缘分。有缘才修得同船渡，无缘么对面手难牵。这世间大概只有春光，只要靠耐心就能等到。遇见花开是缘，遇见美人亦是缘。所以与其任由她对着西湖望水兴叹那些求不来的缘分，倒不如热热闹闹地打上一场，用痛快的拳脚将她从这春愁里彻底揍醒了。
en:
No one in Hangzhou knows when this hopeless romantic first arrived. She spends her days chasing after pretty girls and handsome boys, never taking a single thing seriously. But there are three things in this world you just cannot hate: spring flowers, West Lake, and genuine sweet talk. So, despite her antics, Luo Fengchun fits into Hangzhou perfectly.

Fate is a funny thing. If it is meant to be, your paths will cross. If not, you could be standing face-to-face and still miss each other. In this world, the only thing you can truly count on is spring. Seeing a flower bloom is fate, and meeting a beautiful person is fate, too. So, rather than letting her stand by the lake sighing over romances she cannot have, it is better to just give her a good, lively fight. A few solid punches should be enough to knock her right out of her springtime blues!

那一日，他在平野原见到了一位着急忙慌的中年男人，又见到了一位倒在麦田中已经奄奄一息的老妇人。
他们没有要药，因为他看得出，那中年男人也看得出，那老妇人救不活了。
那位男人问他要纸笔，他从包裹中扯了布，那老妇人将一个菜谱画在布上，她看起来已经稀里糊涂的了，口口声声念着自己在家，要给儿子留一碗面，她的眼泪落在那块破布上，把炭笔的痕迹糊成一块，她走得很疼，很辛苦，很舍不得。
他看出来了，那是一碗槐叶面的菜谱。
en:
One day out on the Plainfield, he came across a panicked middle-aged man and, not far off, an old woman lying in a wheat field, barely hanging on. 
They didn't ask for medicine—he could see, and so could the man, that there was no saving her. 
The man asked him for some paper and a brush, but he only had a scrap of cloth in his pack. The old woman took it and, with shaky hands, drew out a recipe. She was already fading, her mind clouded, mumbling over and over about leaving a bowl of noodles for her son back home. As she wrote, her tears soaked the cloth, smearing the charcoal marks. It was a hard, painful farewell. She clearly didn't want to let go. 
He realized it was a recipe for locust leaf noodles.

江南水市，有渔家载花而来，诸船相聚，遂成一集，名曰花船集。其市不甚用钱，别以花筹相易。
船中所贩，牡丹、月季之属，繁华可观；金木犀、栀子之属，清香袭人。每当晴午，花船未至，而香气已先浮满河面。舟行其间，恍若不在市中，而在春花繁盛处也。
然花船中亦有贩可入饮食者。茉莉以窨茶，香气清细；丝瓜花、南瓜花，裹粉入油，炸之色如碎金，入口外脆而中柔。初见者往往骇笑，以为花岂可食；及尝一箸，则又啧啧称奇。
或曰：“花者，瓶中清供也，奈何置之鼎镬？”余不与辩，但进茶点。其人饮之，称其芳润；食之，称其甘美。余笑曰：“此玫瑰饼与桂花蜜也。”其人哑然。何其怪哉，以清热之物进之，缘何不语。
夫花之为物，一盛而衰。其置于瓶中者，颜色渐改，香气终尽，数日之后，弃于尘土。其入馔者，趁其鲜妍，为茶为酒，入羹入饼，使其香味于人口中一绽而散。二者孰为得所，恐各花亦各有所愿，余不能定。
至若金银花、辛夷之属，能入药，清热解毒，通窍醒神，有济人之意。百花载至花船集时，彼等早在药铺中躺定，当乐入人口腹。
en:
On the waterways of Jiangnan, boatmen arrive carrying fresh flowers. When their boats gather together, they form a floating market known as the "Flower Boat Market." Hardly anyone uses cash here. Instead, people barter with special "flower tokens."
You'll find lush, vibrant blooms like peonies and roses alongside intensely fragrant gardenias and golden osmanthus. On a sunny afternoon, their perfume carries down the river long before the boats even appear. Drifting among them, you forget you're in a marketplace at all. It feels like gliding through a spring garden in full bloom.
Interestingly, some of the flowers sold here are meant for the kitchen. Jasmine is used to scent tea, giving it a refined, delicate aroma. Loofah and pumpkin blossoms are lightly battered and deep-fried until they look like shards of gold, crispy on the outside, tender on the inside. First-timers often laugh in disbelief, wondering how on earth you could eat a flower, only to be completely won over by their first bite.
Someone once challenged me on this, saying, "Flowers are elegant things meant for a vase. How can you throw them into a cooking pot?" I didn't bother arguing. I just served him some tea and pastries. He took a sip and praised the rich, mellow tea, then took a bite and raved about the sweet pastry. I smiled and told him, "That's just rose-petal cake and osmanthus honey." He didn't have another word to say. It's funny. Considering these ingredients are traditionally prescribed to soothe the throat, they certainly left him speechless.
By nature, flowers bloom briefly before fading. Left in a vase, they slowly lose their color and scent until, a few days later, they are thrown out with the dust. But edible flowers are harvested at the peak of their beauty to be turned into teas, wines, soups, and sweets. Their fragrance gets to bloom one last time on the tongue before disappearing forever. Which is the better fate? I suppose every flower has its own preference. It's not for me to say.
Then there are medicinal flowers like honeysuckle and magnolia buds, used to clear heat, draw out toxins, and clear the mind. By the time the ornamental blooms make their grand appearance at the river market, these healing flowers are likely already resting quietly in apothecary drawers. Given that their true purpose is to help people, I imagine they are more than happy to be consumed.

The Gold Leaf Case, Chapter III 
Three Khitans were found dead on their beds in an inn at Sangma, each with a gold leaf next to them. 
 Several small red punctures, possibly caused by being stabbed with a hairpin, were found between the end of their eyebrows and their ears (but the holes indicated that the strength of each stab was different, almost as if an amateur was looking for a pressure point). Poison was found in the punctures, and it was discovered that the victims were drugged and fell unconscious before their deaths. Qi, the innkeeper, claimed that he was resting due to a cold and did not notice anything out of the ordinary. A gold leaf was found in his home, but it was not woven in the same way as the evidence found at the scene. 
(Note: After inspection, it was discovered that these leaves were not all woven by the same person. How should I go on? Maybe I will quit...)

冒冒今日抓了新的小虫子，鬼鬼祟祟地走到美美窝边。正准备放下之时，被窝中窜出的一团毛绒猛地一撞。还未看清楚是谁，香气就已经钻入了冒冒的鼻腔。

冒冒跑啊跑啊，直至它的脸不烫了为止。
下次、下次不能这么偷偷摸摸的了。得给个正式的礼物才行。不能太常见，不能太招摇，又得蕴含自己的心意。
冒冒看着自己身上的猫毛，忽地有了主意。
只是下回，还是要想一个帅气的出场方式才行！
en:
Bold is new to town and couldn't understand why no cats hung around Beauty.
He'd seen her once in the moonlight and had been utterly smitten.
Not knowing her tastes, he leaves his own favorite things, a crunchy beetle, a smooth pebble, by her nest, not wanting to bother her.
One night, as he crept up with a new gift, a furry missile shot from the nest and bowled him over. Before he could even see who it was, her scent filled his senses.
Moonlit Beauty! His heart did a somersault, and his legs, each with a mind of its own, carried him away in a clumsy panic. He ran until his face stopped burning.
Next time, he vowed, no sneaking. He needed a proper gift. Something subtle, meaningful, and entirely him.
He looked at his own reflection in a puddle and had an idea.
Next time, he'd also need a much cooler escape.

zh:
……
六月廿一，又得万师师兄训斥。
不过运炁敲了敲百悬桥的钟，让同侪们早了一个时辰下课。其中张弛之道，师兄怎的不懂？
启蛰便说，既我前些时日方能引炁御剑，如今已可敲钟，照此下去，不出五日或许便能催动机巧器物……再过几年，御动天衍算阵也未可知。 
所言甚是！待到那时，得给墨门省下多少人力物力啊！不愧是我。
……
三月三十，师父领我回墨山道时，心里是怎么想的呢？
我问师父，他总不肯多说，只让我多出去走走看看。山外风物殊异，孩子们一听我从山中来，总瞪大双眼问个没完。当年的我，一定也是这般看着师父。师父都不嫌烦，真好。
……
九月十四，得巨子鹔指点，熟读天衍历年算稿。
又依万师师兄所辑历年水位，用巨子新设的试验算阵推演，整理水利测估薄记一卷，昨日已遣木鸢送去了山外，望能帮上师兄的忙。
……
八月廿六，年少之事，恍如隔世。而今师父虽不在身旁，却有好些事想同师父说。
第一件，是效师昔行，于山外捡回些孩子，安顿于慈幼堂。
第二件，是巨子鹔委部分事务于我，如今正忙于梳理算阵排布。
第三件，算阵推得些许殊异“时点”，待时点临近，观天地变动，便可反证算阵之效。
最要紧的一件：喂，师父可有好好吃饭？按时休息？待到秋日，定要寻个机会，去师父身边好生监察！
en:
...
21st Day of the Sixth Month
Got another scolding from Senior Brother Wanshi today.
But all I did was use qi to tap the bell at Myriadspan Bridge and let everyone out of class two hours early. Senior Brother is always talking about balance and timing, so how is it he can't see the balance and timing in that?
Qizhe said that since I only just learned to guide qi into a sword not long ago, and can already ring a bell with it now, then at this rate I might be able to drive mechanical devices within five days... and a few years from now, perhaps even initiate the Derivation Array.
Very true. Just think how much manpower and effort that would save Mohist Hill by then. Not bad, if I do say so myself.
...
30th Day of the Third Month
What was Master thinking when he first brought me back to Mohist Hill?
I've asked him before, but he never says much, only tells me to go out and see more of the world. Everything beyond the mountain is so different. Whenever children hear I came from the mountain, they stare at me with wide eyes and keep asking questions without end. Back then, I must have looked at Master the very same way. And he never found it bothersome. That was kind of him.
...
14th Day of the Ninth Month
Received guidance from Grandmaster Osprey and carefully read through the Derivation Array drafts from past years.
Using the water-level records from previous years compiled by Senior Brother Wanshi, and running them through the new trial calculation array Grandmaster Osprey set up, I sorted out a whole volume of notes on waterworks estimates. Yesterday I sent it beyond the mountain by wooden eagle. I hope it may be of some help to Senior Brother.
...
26th Day of the Eighth Month
The things of my younger days now feel like another lifetime. Master is no longer by my side, and yet there is still so much I want to tell him.
First, I followed Master's example and brought back some children from beyond the mountain, and settled them in Foundlings Hall.
Second, Grandmaster Osprey has entrusted part of his work to me, and I've been busy sorting through the arrangement of the calculation arrays.
Third, the arrays have produced a few unusual "time points." When those moments draw near, I'll be able to observe the changes in Heaven and Earth and use them to verify how effective the arrays truly are.
And most important of all: hey, has Master been eating properly? Resting on time? When autumn comes, I must find a chance to go and keep a proper eye on him!
Old Slips, New Tale

zh:
蔡敬行不是没想过死，可他每次想要走上绝路的时候，心里总会想起当年食客们说的话：
老蔡啊，你这份手艺，就算哪天不做火烧了，也准是个好厨子。
对，就算自己的火烧摊被砸了，就算做不了肉食，总还能做些素菜，做些粥饭。天下那么大，他这个做厨子的，总能给大伙做些东西吃，活一个厨子，就能活好几十号人。
于是老蔡也加入了逃难的流民队伍。起初，他还常常能找些野味、钓些河鲜，可渐渐地，契丹人占了滹沱河，鱼是钓不成了，野味也越来越少。于是蔡敬行就去寻些野菜做汤，他想，等野菜挖干净了，这仗，也就能打完了吧？
可他没想到，野菜挖完了，野花野果也都摘干净了，仗还是没打完。这时候，他身边的流民，已经开始挖奇形怪状的草根吃，有不少人吃着吃着，就两眼一翻，口吐白沫，再也没能醒来。
蔡敬行没了办法，他这辈子都没想过，原来有一天他的砧板上，只剩下墙土和树皮能够做些算不得食物的“食物”。
做了那么多年厨子，他怎么会不知道，这观音土和系命汤，能不能吃，吃多了会有什么后果？
可若是不吃这些，就什么都没得吃，就只能活活饿死。
他没得选，他们，也都没得选。
en:
Cai Jingxing had thought about dying more than once. Each time the thought grew near, the faces and voices of his old regulars stopped him.
"Cai, with hands like yours, even if the oven's gone, you'll still be a fine cook."
Right, even if his meat bun stall was smashed, even if he couldn't cook meat, he could still make some vegetarian dishes, porridge, and rice. In such a vast world, as a cook, he could always make something for everyone to eat. A good cook feeds whole families. One life keeps dozens alive.
So he fell in with the refugees. At first, there were still rabbits in the brush and fish in the streams; he could rustle up something to eat and keep hope alive, thinking the war would end before long. Then the Khitan took Hutuo River. No more fishing, no more game. He began making soups from wild greens, telling himself that when the plants ran out, the fighting would be over.
But the plants ran out, and the war did not. People started digging for any roots they could find; they scraped at clay from riverbanks. Some of those roots and soils were poisonous. Men who ate them would convulse, foam at the mouth, and never wake again.
After a lifetime at the cutting board, Cai knew enough to recognize names and symptoms: the so‑called "Guanyin clay," the bitter, life‑binding broths that ate at the body.
He understood what those things would do. He also understood what not eating them would do. Hunger was immediate and absolute.
But there was no choice, neither for him nor for the people who followed him.

#Y男子赢了。你见过寒姨藏起来的书信，也记得她将离人泪全部倒入河中的伤神模样。她定是输了，输掉了她最珍视的一颗心。#E
老人微笑，不置可否。他向你缓缓讲述着故事的余料。悬剑之义，天泉之义，洛神之义，燕北盟之义……每个人都站在了道义的箭锋之上，而引弦之手，从不由人。
en:
Beneath the Peace Bell Tower, the old bell-ringer's flute still sings as ever. Your arrival does nothing to disturb his quiet ease. Then the melody shifted, weeping and whispering like a grief too deep for words. This is not your first time here, yet this time, you seem at last to hear the story hidden within the song.
It is the clash between the surging Luo River and the gleaming white snow; the silent gaze between bitter winter plum and a deep, clear spring. It is the turning point where lovers become estranged, the stroke where love and duty leave their truest, most agonizing mark, the final parting that leaves them as strangers at the ends of the earth. You know who the story is about. Yet she has never spoken of that great battle, and you never learned who emerged victorious in the end. The old man seems to read your thoughts, tossing the same question back to you. After a moment's reflection, you give your answer...
#YThe man won. You've seen the letter Aunt Han kept hidden away, and still remember her grief-stricken look as she poured every drop of Parting Tears into the river. She must have lost, for she lost the heart she treasured above all else.#E
The old man only smiles, neither confirming nor denying it. Slowly, he recounts the untold fragments of the tale: the honor of the Hanging Blade, the honor of Well of Heaven, the honor of Water Lady, the honor of the Northern Vow… Each stood balanced upon the arrowhead of honor, yet the hand that drew the bowstring was never their own.

丁解香曾听一前辈高人言：“情深不寿，慧极必伤”。于是每每见到那人故作姿态，卖弄才智，她心中便一股无名火起。
“人说大智若愚，真正的智者，哪个像你叶卓这样张扬？”
那人总是眯眼笑着，一副泼皮模样：
“人说刀子嘴豆腐心，其实哪个嘴巴厉害的，都不如三师妹心软。”
丁解香只好败下阵来，草草留下一声冷哼，便赶忙走开调整表情去了。
这只狐狸太聪明，自己永远占不到上风，三言两语就破了功。她不喜欢那人骨子里透出的傲气，却又不自觉被那傲气吸引，仿佛天下间真没什么事能难倒他。她不喜欢自己被看透的感觉，可那人和她拌嘴时，好像每句话都能逗笑她。
讨厌那傲气，或许是因为那傲气更让丁解香觉得配不上他。
讨厌被看透，或许是因为她觉得自己的性格他一定不喜欢。
爱这件事，当局者迷。天下所有人都知道她和叶卓是一对，除了她自己。叶卓抚不平丁解香脸上的疤痕，但他默默用时间，抚平着丁解香心中的疤痕——直到那一天的到来。
世界上最完美的表演，也会败给直觉。当夜色之中，丁解香纵马赶上出山的人时，她第一次从他的脸上看到了惊慌。
叶卓的脸冷得像冬天房檐上倒悬的冰刺，而丁解香就像把冰刺掰下来挥舞玩耍的孩童。
这只臭狐狸，原来也有束手无策的时候？
“丁解香，出山容易回山难，擅自出山即是叛门，你当真清楚？”
“丁解香，我们出山不是去玩，城防战事，要死人的！”
“丁解香，你是不是喜欢我才非要黏着我啊？我一走你就跟着走？”
“丁解香！你到底要胡闹些什么？我们都走了，师父他老人家谁来照顾！”
“丁解香……你回山去……我求求你好不好？”
丁解香只是默默跟着赶路，天色将明，她对着叶卓笑了。第一次，那样没有负担地笑了。
“你说如果整个天下的人都像你们一样，不在乎我脸上的疤，我会不会早就嫁给你了？”
叶卓突然愣住了，他闭了嘴，他知道自己拦不住她了。
“叶卓，你只是比我先听到消息而已。我们出山的原因其实一样，因为我们是墨者。”
天光大亮，丁解香大大方方让那光芒洒在脸上，洒在那道疤痕上。那天清晨，她们所有人都闪着光。
en:
Ding Jiexiang once heard an elder say: "Profound love is fleeting; supreme wisdom brings its own ruin."
Thus, whenever she saw that man posturing and flaunting his brilliance, an inexplicable spark of anger would ignite within her.

"They say true wisdom hides in plain sight. Which true sage have you ever seen act as boastfully as you, Ye Zhuo?"
The man would just narrow his eyes and smile with that roguish air of his.
"They also say a razor's edge on the tongue hides a soft heart beneath. For all your bluster, no one is more tender-hearted than our Third Sister."

Ding Jiexiang could only admit defeat, leaving behind a hasty scoff as she quickly walked away to hide her shifting expression.
This fox was too clever. She could never gain the upper hand. With just a few words, he would completely shatter her defenses. She loathed the arrogance carved into his very bones, yet despite herself, she was entirely captivated by it, as if there was truly nothing in this world that could baffle him.

She hated the feeling of being seen through, yet whenever they bickered, every word he spoke seemed to make her want to laugh.
She hated his arrogance, perhaps because it made her feel she was unworthy of him.
She hated being seen through, perhaps because she believed he would never like her true self.

In the game of love, the players are always blind. The entire world knew that she and Ye Zhuo belonged together. Everyone, except her.
Ye Zhuo could not heal the scar upon Ding's face. But through the quiet passage of time, he silently smoothed over the scars hidden within her heart, until that day finally came.
The world's most flawless performance will always crumble before raw instinct.

When Ding spurred her horse through the dead of night to catch up with the departing group, she saw panic flicker across his face for the very first time.
Ye's expression turned cold, sharp as a winter icicle hanging beneath the eaves. Ding felt like a mischievous child who had snapped that icicle off simply to wave it around in play.
So, this smug fox also had moments when he was at a loss?

"Ding Jiexiang, leaving the mountain is easy, but returning is a path barred! To leave without permission is treason against the sect. Do you truly understand?"
"Ding Jiexiang, this is no sightseeing trip! This is city defense and open war. People are going to die out there!"
"Ding Jiexiang, is it because you like me that you insist on clinging to me? Must you shadow my every step?"
"Ding Jiexiang! What on earth are you doing? If we all leave, who will take care of the Master?"
"Ding... please go back... I'm begging you. Just this once, go back."

Ding Jiexiang followed the group in silence. As the sky began to brighten, she turned to Ye Zhuo and smiled. For the first time, her smile carried no burden.
"If the whole world were like you all," she said softly, "if everyone could look past the scar on my face... do you think I wouldn't have married you long ago?"
Ye Zhuo froze. He fell entirely silent. He knew then that his words no longer had the power to turn her back.

"Ye Zhuo, you merely received the news a heartbeat before I did. We descend the mountain for the exact same reason... Because we are Mohists."
The morning sun surged over the horizon. With open confidence, Ding held her head high, allowing the brilliant light to bathe her face and the scar across it.

In that early dawn light, every one of them was blazing.

zh:
初五：买青色绣线两把，花四文。给小娘子买麦芽糖，两文。
初八：扯了两尺粗布，十五文。
给小姐煎安神汤，桂枝少了半钱，明日再买。

今日又听杂役说我家小娘子痴呆，真是烂嘴。
她不过不爱说话，心里亮得很。
前儿个我盘算这本子上的糊涂账，怎么都想不起来那十几文钱花哪去了。小娘子走只扫了一眼，把哪天买了什么全说出来了。再一问，连前月我那本用完的账本花下多少，全都记得清清楚楚，更不用说她平日读的那些书了。

那些嚼舌根的人懂什么！小娘子看过的东西，全都死死装在脑瓜里，一件都忘不掉。别人家的孩子哪有这等本事？

我和那些人争辩，他们只说我是没见过世面的村妇。唉，我只顾好好照料小娘子，盼她平平安安长大。太聪明了，说不定反倒招祸……旁人不懂，就不懂吧。
en:
Day 5: Two skeins of blue-green embroidery thread, four coins. Malt candy for the young lady, two coins.
Day 8: About two feet of coarse cloth, fifteen coins.
Made the young lady's calming decoction. About two grams short of cinnamon twig. Buy more tomorrow.

Heard the servants calling my young lady stupid again today. Nasty tongues, the lot of them.
She doesn't say much, that's all. She understands perfectly well.
The other day, I couldn't make sense of this ledger. There were a dozen or so coins I couldn't account for. The young lady took one look and told me what I'd bought and on which day. When I asked, she could even remember every expense in the ledger I'd filled up the month before. And that's nothing compared to all the books she remembers.

What do those gossips know? Once she's seen something, it stays in her head. She doesn't forget a thing. How many children can do that?

I tried telling them, but they said I was just an ignorant village woman. Oh, well. I'll look after the young lady and hope she grows up safe and well. Perhaps being so clever only brings trouble... If they don't understand, let them be.
