写这封信，是想给你报个喜。多亏你先前帮忙，我才有了支起摊子的本钱，在开封南郊的麦香集里寻了个落脚处。当初从家里出来时，哪敢想有今日……
爷爷常说，谢人不能只挂在嘴上。想来想去，我把近日攒下的钱寄回富平老家，用大侠的名义承包了五亩柿子地，托爷爷和乡亲们照看。爷爷说，要让你瞧瞧，特意让村里的老画师给画了下来，我都能想象后头红彤彤的模样了！
不过今年老家的天儿有些邪乎……又是旱又是涝的没断过，八成会影响收成……等到了做柿饼的时候，总要送你些尝尝，可能不多，但都是乡亲们的心意。不知大侠住在何处？一定包得仔仔细细的给你送去！
<IMAGE id='im1' image_url='https://h72.fp.ps.netease.com/file/6937d9ff99a801cef19883d1aMopacRH07' size='1810*2704' color='255;255;255')'></IMAGE>
en:
Dear Wanderer,
How are you? I have a small token of my gratitude for you. To avoid any delay in its arrival, please press [<LINK id='link' color='#8c5823' url='https://research-game.163.com/htmls/46rzpk/paper.html?uid={uid}&role_id={pid}&server={hostnum}' is_underline='true'> to register your mailing address</LINK>] first. Allow me to explain:
I write with glad tidings. Thanks to your help, I've set up my stall at the Wheatwind Bazaar in Kaifeng Suburbs-South. When I left home, I never dreamed such a day…
Grandfather always said gratitude must be more than words. So I've sent my savings back to Fuping, my hometown, to lease five mu of persimmon groves in your name. Grandfather and the villagers tend them. He insisted on having the old painter paint them for you. I can already imagine the fiery red blaze!
But the weather's been cruel this year, drought and flood by turns. The harvest would likely suffer…
When the dried persimmons come, I'll send you some. Not much, perhaps, but grown from honest hearts. Where do you lodge? I'll package them with care and have them delivered.

There was a time when Buddhist devotion flourished in Qinghe. It was then that a wandering monk arrived, calling himself Miaoshan, a disciple of Master Baozhi from a hundred years ago. zh:
这一世，我本想着，不嫁给他，不给他眼神，我与爹娘便能安然无恙。谁曾想，因着我的觉醒，他竟提前与公主勾连上了。没想到这次没有我，他还是与往日一样，登上二品。但此次是因公主暗中相助。他们二人依旧合谋，欲架空我家。
他仍在我面前装作那痴情模样，对我虐恋情深，对外却散布我薄情的谣言。哼，看来，仅仅是自保，仍是不够安全，我还需得再想些法子，改写爹娘的命运……
我忽地忆起，他在我墓前曾说过，我与父母提及要嫁与他那一日，父母应允之时，他为了断绝后患，竟在那日雇人杀害了他的原配妻子。是的，我在那日才知道他家中已有妻室。他高中之后，以接她享富贵为由，暗中将人悄悄接往荒野勒死……
呵，藏的真好，上一世，我死后才得知此事。这一世，我定要在那之前，救下那无辜妇人，与她一同制裁那薄情郎。
只是，我不嫁于他，这事还会不会发生呢？我只能带上家中护卫，悄悄前去查看。只见那妇人美艳非常，我见犹怜。等待至夜晚，本想或许这一世有了变化。但突然，风云变幻。一名壮汉破门而入。果然，还是发生了。即便没有我，还有那公主不是么？在他妻子断气的前一刻，我救下了她。
殊不知，这一幕，都被那九皇子看在眼里。前世，他对我冷淡至极，可我知道，他暗藏锋芒，虽不受宠，最终登基为帝。还有那与我有娃娃亲的武人，前世我任性胡闹，断了这亲事。最后，他辅佐九皇子登基，成了护国大将军。我还碰到了那曾为他代笔之人，如今虽落魄，但我知道，这只是暂时的，后面他的才华会被发掘，被圣上直接点为状元……
最低三文，便可加入古书铺同仁会，畅读全书。
en:
In this life, I had thought that by simply avoiding him. By neither marrying nor even sparing him a glance, my parents and I would remain safe. Yet fate played a cruel joke. Since I awakened early, he conspired with the princess even earlier than before. Without me, he still rose to a second-rank official, this time with the princess's support. Together, they schemed once more to undermine my family's standing.

He continued to fake his deep affection before me, while secretly spreading slander that I was heartless and cold. Hmph. It seems that merely preserving myself is not enough. I must find a way to rewrite my parent's fate entirely.

Then I recalled he once muttered at my grave that on the day I convinced my parents to approve our marriage, he had already hired someone to eliminate his first wife to sever all loose ends. Yeah, that was the first time that I learned he had already been married. After earning his high position, he lured his wife with promises of wealth, only to have her strangled in the wilderness.

How well he had hidden it. In my previous life, I only uncovered the truth after death. This time, I would not let it happen. I would save that innocent woman, and together, we would bring down that faithless traitor.

But a doubt lingered: without marrying him, would the same tragedy still unfold? I brought my family's guards and went on a secret investigation. And there she was, stunningly beautiful, yet pitiful in her loneliness. I waited until night, hoping fate had shifted. But all of a sudden, a strongman burst through the door.

It was happening again. Even without me, the princess remained an accomplice in cruelty. Just before the woman drew her final breath, I intervened and saved her.

Little did I know, the Ninth Prince witnessed it all. In my previous life, he had been cold and distant toward me. Yet I knew, hidden beneath that emotionless exterior was a sharp mind. He was not favored by the Emperor, but eventually he ascended the throne. And then there was the martial man I had once been betrothed to. In my willful foolishness, I had broken off the engagement. He later became the Ninth Prince's greatest general and protector of the realm. I even encountered the man who ghostwrote poems for that traitor. Though he now lived in obscurity, I knew his brilliance would soon be recognized, and he would rise to the top, named Scholar Laureate by the Emperor himself.

先见猫再起名，还是先有名字，再从巷子角落长出一只猫来配，这是个问题。不管别的猫如何，斑斑却是昂着头，精神抖擞地认领了这个名字，好像自个儿从一生下来，就该配得上任何字眼。
“管中窥豹，可见一斑。”分明只是借由纹路起的名，却硬生生被人凑上一句高深典故，对于其中深意，斑斑一概不知，猫只是舔毛，跳上灌木，跳上更高的枝丫，随后居高临下地看人，也可能是望着熙熙攘攘的水道，鲜甜香美的果篮……猫有他的看法。
哪怕被冠上豹子的期许，斑斑也没有半分在意，凡有美食，必然大快朵颐，平坦的猫腹越发鼓鼓囊囊，纤细的猫身越发膨胀，如要越过溪水，绒软的肚皮毛便免不了沾层水汽，倘若玩捉迷藏，一整朵荷花也藏不住斑斑的身形……每逢喂食，人总对此略有担忧，猫却全不在意，照样大吃大嚼。
不仅如此，斑斑路过水影的时候，还总要刻意停留一会儿，临水照猫影，或许他对自己如今雄伟的身材还颇为满意呢。
en:
Whether the cat comes first and the name follows, or the name comes first and a cat grows to fit it from some corner of the alley... now that's a question worth pondering. Whatever the case may be for other cats, Spot held its head high and claimed this name with great spirit, as though it'd been worthy of any word one could give it since the very day it was born.
"Through the tube one glimpses the leopard, and by a single spot, the whole may be known." Though the name was surely given for nothing more than its markings, someone had gone and tacked on this lofty old saying regardless. As for its deeper meaning, Spot hadn't the faintest clue. A cat only licks its fur, leaps onto a shrub, leaps higher still onto a branch, and then looks down upon the world from above, or perhaps gazes instead at the bustling waterways below, at baskets brimming with sweet, fragrant fruit... a cat has its own way of seeing things.
Even burdened with the expectations of a leopard's name, Spot paid it no mind whatsoever. Wherever there was good food to be had, it ate its fill without fail, its once-flat belly growing ever rounder, its slender frame ever more swollen. Should it try to cross a stream, the soft fur of its belly could not help but come away damp; and were anyone to play hide-and-seek with it, not even a full-blooming lotus could conceal its shape... Whenever feeding time came round, folk always worried a little, but the cat paid it no heed at all, chewing away with the same hearty appetite as ever.
What's more, whenever Spot passed by a reflection in the water, it would always linger there for a moment, gazing down at its own image upon the surface, perhaps rather pleased, even now, with its own magnificently rounded figure.
The Renowned: February

zh:
钱，是会生钱的。
学会这几招，让钱追着你跑！

第一招：识面术
要说江湖上，易容哪家强，九流认第一，墨山居第二。
话虽如此，墨山道的易容实在不太够看。略通识面术，就能简单揪出几个墨山道弟子。拜托他们，为村民引水、为街坊修井，收取些许匠作费。不用吹灰之力，就月入三百文。
别担心，他们会越干越开心的，只要在一旁加油鼓劲，夸些“好手艺、好头脑”之类的话就好！

第二招：酿酒术
经一位墨山道弟子验证，酒里兑入适当的水能让酒更好喝。这样一来，每十坛酒就能多出一坛，若是一百坛、一千坛，就多出数不清的酒，也就能多赚到数不清的钱。
不过此术有个风险，容易被狂澜砸场子。

第三招：合作术
天泉好劫富济贫撒币，大家都知道。等在天泉路过的地方乞讨，已经是我门一大固定收入。但这样总归都是小钱，要赚大钱，还要学这一招——
话说凡节庆时候，瓦肆和坊市都人满为患，官府人力不足，也是没辙。可以借此机会与天泉合作，以安宁游玩为噱头，把脑满肠肥的富老爷引至僻静小巷中，待天泉大刀一亮，老爷钱袋一交，咱们趁势再找他们分点零头——就算零头，已是大赚特赚啊！

总而言之呢，钱的赚法还有很多，但笔记只能先写到这里。
望诸位后辈，在这条钱途上走得更远！

附录：
回顾过去的笔记，发现其中有一个漏洞，就是算学。
一文钱两文钱数得清，一千文三千文算起来就难。
为了补上这个漏洞，老夫特意请来一位孤云弟子，向她讨教算学门道，算是略有小成，再也不怕算不明白钱。
后辈们如果有意，可以去找驻地内的方过春。
en:
Money can make more money. 
Learn these techniques, and you'll have money coming to you! 

Technique One: Face Reading 
In the jianghu, when it comes to disguises, the Nine Mortal Ways leads the way, with Mohist Hill coming second. 
That said, the disguises from Mohist Hill aren't very convincing. With a bit of face-reading skill, you can easily spot several Mohist Hill disciples. Once identified, you can get them to do simple tasks like diverting water for villagers or fixing wells in neighborhoods, charging a modest fee for their work. With very little effort, this can earn you around 300 wen a month. 
No need to worry—they'll get more motivated the more they work, especially if you encourage them with praise like "great skills" or "sharp minds"! 

Technique Two: Brewing Technique 
A Mohist Hill disciple once confirmed that adding the right amount of water to wine can actually improve its taste. That means for every ten jars of wine, you effectively get an extra jar. Scale that up to a hundred or a thousand jars, and that's a lot of extra wine—and profit. 
There's a risk, though: this method might attract attention from the Raging Tides, who don't take kindly to such tricks. 

Technique Three: Partnership Strategy 
Everyone knows Well of Heaven is famous for robbing the rich to help the poor. Begging along their road has become a steady source of income for us, but that's only a little money. To make serious cash, here's the trick: 
During festivals, markets and shops get overcrowded, and the authorities are stretched thin. That's when you team up with Well of Heaven, using the promise of a peaceful outing to lure wealthy merchants into secluded alleys. When the Well of Heaven disciples strike, the merchants lose their purses—and we take a nice cut of the haul. Even small shares add up to big earnings! 

In short, there are many ways to make money, but this is all I'll cover for now. 
I hope the next generation will take these lessons further and go even deeper on the path to wealth. 

Appendix: 
Looking back at the earlier notes, I realized there was a gap—mathematics. 
Counting small amounts like one or two wen is easy, but adding up thousands gets tricky. 
To fix that, I invited a disciple from Lone Cloud to teach me some arithmetic skills. Now I'm no longer afraid of handling big sums. 
If you want to learn, find Fang Guochun at the base.

zh:
【庄公第三】

元年，春，王正月。
公何以不言即位？春秋君弑，子不言即位。君弑则子何以不言即位？隐之也。孰隐？隐子也。
〇三月，夫人孙于齐。
孙者何？孙犹孙也。内讳奔，谓之孙。夫人固在齐矣，其言孙于齐何？念母也。正月以存君，念母以首事。夫人何以不称姜氏？贬。曷为贬？与弑公也。其与弑公奈何？夫人谮公于齐侯，公曰："同非吾子，齐侯之子也。"齐侯怒，与之饮酒。于其出焉，使公子彭生送之。于其乘焉，搚干而杀之。念母者，所善也，则曷为于其念母焉贬？不与念母也。
〇夏，单伯逆王姬。
单伯者何？吾大夫之命乎天子者也。何以不称使？天子召而使之也。逆之者何？使我主之也。曷为使我主之？天子嫁女乎诸侯，必使诸侯同姓者主之；诸侯嫁女于大夫，必使大夫同姓者主之。
〇秋，筑王姬之馆于外。
何以书？讥。何讥尔？筑之，礼也；于外，非礼也。于外何以非礼？筑于外，非礼也。其筑之何以礼？主王姬者，必为之改筑。主王姬者，则曷为必为之改筑？于路寝则不可，小寝则嫌，群公子之舍则以卑矣。其道必为之改筑者也。
〇冬，十月乙亥，陈侯林卒。
〇王使荣叔来锡桓公命。
锡者何？赐也。命者何？加我服也。其言桓公何？追命也。
〇王姬归于齐。
何以书？我主之也。
〇齐师迁纪郱、鄑、郚。
迁之者何？取之也。取之则曷为不言取之也？为襄公讳也。外取邑不书，此何以书？大之也。何大尔？自是始灭也。

二年，春，王二月，葬陈庄公。
〇夏，公子庆父帅师伐余丘。
于余丘者何？邾娄之邑也。曷为不系乎邾娄？国之也。曷为国之？君存焉尔。
〇秋，七月，齐王姬卒。
外夫人不卒，此何以卒？录焉尔。曷为录焉尔？我主之也。
〇冬，十有二月，夫人姜氏会齐侯于郜。
〇乙酉，宋公冯卒。

……
en:
【Duke Zhuang, Year 3】

First year, spring, the king's first month.
Why does the Duke not speak of his accession? In the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a ruler is assassinated, the son does not speak of his accession. Why does the son not speak of his accession when the ruler is assassinated? To conceal it. Who conceals it? The son conceals it.
〇Third month, the Lady retreated to Qi.
What does "retreated" mean? "Retreated" is like fleeing. Internally, they avoid saying "fled" and call it "retreated." The Lady was already in Qi; why does it say she retreated to Qi? To remember her mother. In the first month, they preserve the ruler; remembering the mother begins with this matter. Why is the Lady not called Lady Jiang? Because she is degraded. Why is she degraded? Because she conspired in the assassination of the Duke. How did she conspire in the assassination of the Duke? The Lady slandered the Duke to the Marquis of Qi. The Duke said, "Tong is not my son; he is the son of the Marquis of Qi." The Marquis of Qi was angry and drank wine with him. When he left, he sent Duke's son Pengsheng to see him off. When he mounted the carriage, he broke his ribs and killed him. Remembering the mother is a good thing, so why degrade her for remembering her mother? Because it does not approve of remembering the mother.
〇Summer, Shan Bo went to meet the king's daughter.
Who is Shan Bo? He is our high official appointed by the Son of Heaven. Why is it not said that he was sent? Because the Son of Heaven summoned and sent him. Why go to meet her? To make us host her. Why make us host her? When the Son of Heaven marries his daughter to a feudal lord, he must have a feudal lord of the same surname host her; when a feudal lord marries his daughter to a high official, he must have a high official of the same surname host her.
〇Autumn, they built a lodge for the king's daughter outside the city.
Why is this recorded? To criticize. What is criticized? Building it is proper; building it outside is improper. Why is building it outside improper? Building outside is not proper. Why is building it proper? When hosting the king's daughter, one must build a new lodge for her. Why must one build a new lodge when hosting the king's daughter? In the main hall, it is not permissible; in the small hall, it would be suspect; in the residences of the various young lords, it would be too lowly. The proper way is to build a new lodge for her.
〇Winter, tenth month, on the day Yihai, Marquis Chen Lin died.
〇The king sent Rong Shu to come and bestow the mandate on Duke Huan.
What does "bestow" mean? It means to give. What does "mandate" mean? It means to add to our robes. Why does it say Duke Huan? Because it is a posthumous mandate.
〇The king's daughter returned to Qi.
Why is this recorded? Because we hosted her.
〇The Qi army moved Ji's Ping, Zan, and Wu.
What does "moved" mean? It means to take them. If they took them, why not say they took them? To conceal it for Duke Xiang. Taking cities from outside is not recorded; why is this recorded? To magnify it. Why magnify it? Because from this point, the destruction began.

Second year, spring, the king's second month, they buried Duke Zhuang of Chen.
〇Summer, Duke's son Qingfu led troops to attack Yuqiu.
What is Yuqiu? It is a city of Zhulou. Why is it not attached to Zhulou? Because it is treated as a state. Why is it treated as a state? Because the ruler was there.
〇Autumn, seventh month, the king's daughter of Qi died.
Foreign ladies are not recorded as deceased; why is this one recorded as deceased? To record her. Why record her? Because we hosted her.
〇Winter, twelfth month, the Lady Jiang met the Marquis of Qi at Gao.
〇On the day Yiyou, Duke Song Feng died.

……

许多文人墨客正在摊位前题诗作对。
墨香萦绕间，一个小孩挤到桌边，踮起脚尖，才勉强够到纸笔。
“写诗有什么好玩的呢？”$T(30)心里嘀咕着，思考了半天，而后抓起笔，认认真真地画了起来。
待$T(30)离开，几位大人好奇地围过去瞧——洁白的宣纸上，没有诗句，只有一个用墨线勾出的、圆滚滚的娃娃笑脸，嘴角翘得老高。
先是一静，随后，笑声便在人群中，轻轻漾开了。
en:
Scholars had gathered before a stall, trading lines and writing verses.
The air smelled of ink. A child pushed through the crowd and squeezed up to the edge of the table. Even on tiptoe, it was just enough to reach the brush.
"What's so fun about writing poems?" $T(30) stood there thinking for a while, then picked up the brush and got to work.
When $T(30) stepped away, a few of the adults leaned in to take a look. There was no poem on the paper. Just a round little face, drawn in bold ink lines, grinning from ear to ear.
For a moment, no one said a thing. Then the laughter spread, passing through the crowd like a ripple.

zh:
法一：食肉
晨起必啖肉，佐粥两碗。切记不可食凉粥，犯则肠鸣如雷，前功尽弃。

法二：熬骨
每日抡锤，从卯时练至辰时三刻，先举轻若重，后举重若轻。

法三：休沐
筋肉如面团，捶打后需静置，故每七日必歇一日，取艾草煮汤沐身，辅以竹罐拔除淤气。

法四：站桩
寻大树一株，马步立于其下。自百息渐至千息，待双腿颤抖如筛糠，汗出如泉涌时，方得其妙。

法五：裸奔
鸡鸣时裸身奔于野，效猛虎跳涧之势，做饿狼扑食之姿。切记避开菜地，踩坏了得赔钱。

法六 熬筋
冬月雪地赤膊练拳，夏伏正午抱石晒背。筋肉初如针扎，后似火燎，终得暖流自丹田涌起。

法七：养气
暮间盘坐河滩，观水流行气。默诵"气沉涌泉，力贯指尖"八字诀，浑身泰然。

此七法无须银钱，但缺不得三样：早起三更的狠劲，夏练三伏的痴劲，冬练三九的傻劲。
若能严格依照此七法苦练，不出三月，浑身腱子肉，力可比耕牛。诸君，共勉！
en:
Method 1 Eat Meat
Begin each morning with meat and two bowls of porridge. Never eat cold porridge.

Method 2 Bone Conditioning
Strike the bones with a hammer from dawn until late morning. Lift light weights as if heavy, heavy weights as if light.

Method 3 Respite
Take a day off every seven days. Bathe in mugwort tea and use bamboo cups to draw out toxins.

Method 4 Standing Meditation
Stand beneath a large tree in a horse stance. Breathe from 100 to 1,000 breaths until your legs tremble and sweat pours.

Method 5 Naked Running
At dawn, run naked through the fields. Avoid vegetable patches.

Method 6 Tendon Strengthening
Train shirtless in winter snow and bask under the summer sun, holding a stone.

Method 7 Qi Cultivation
At dusk, sit by the river, watching the water's flow as qi moves.

Practice these faithfully for three months, and your body will grow strong.

zh:
昔日有少年侠士，名曰凌云，与少女晴风青梅竹马，情愫暗生。
然天下动荡，凌云因故离开墨城，远行江湖，欲平天下之不平事。
二人自此天各一方，仅靠一只名曰“云逸”的木鸢通信传情。

晴风每见木鸢，便知凌云情深。
只叹世事弄人，晴风因病早逝，二人之恋无疾而终。
一年后，凌云也为救路边小儿牺牲于恶人刀下，似是追随爱人所去。

就此，木鸢“云逸”再无去处，遂借风力，茫然高飞于天地间。
三番四季轮转，跨越千山万水，“云逸”竟飞来晴风墓前。
此刻，只见那孤坟霎时金光闪烁！
片刻后，竟生生从中飞出一只木鸢，名曰“风舞”。

二鸢虽是初见，却如故人般重逢，情比金坚，誓死不离，任风雨再大也无法拆散。
终在月老庙前得神灵庇佑，化为一对活生生的双飞燕，
自此，时间有价，生死有命，却终能比翼齐飞，永结同心。
en:
Ling Yun, a young hero, and Qing Feng, his childhood sweetheart, fell in love. But chaos tore them apart: Ling Yun left Mohist City to right injustices, and they stayed connected only through a wooden eagle named "Cloud Zephyr."

Whenever Qing Feng saw the eagle, she felt his unwavering love. Sadly, she fell ill and died young, their love left unfulfilled. A year later, Ling Yun died protecting a child, as if following her in death.

The eagle "Cloud Zephyr," with nowhere to go, drifted on the wind until it reached Qing Feng's grave. There, a golden light emerged, and from it flew a new eagle, "Wind Dancer."

Though meeting for the first time, they felt like old souls reunited, inseparable through storms and time, and transformed into twin swallows.
From then on, bound by fate, they soared together, forever united.

zh:
【里仁第四】

子曰：“里仁为善，择不处仁，焉得智？”
子曰：“不仁者不可以久处约，不可以长处乐。仁者安仁，智者利仁。”
子曰：“唯仁者能好人，能恶人。”
子曰：“苟志于仁矣，无恶。”
子曰：“富与贵，是人之所欲也，不以其道得之，不处也。贫与贱，是人之所恶，不以其道得之，不去。君子去仁，恶乎成名？君子无终食之间违仁，造次必于是，颠沛必于是。”
子曰：“我未见好仁者，恶不仁者。好仁者，无以尚之，恶不仁者，其为仁矣，不使不仁者加乎其身。有能一日用其力于仁矣乎？我未见力不足者也。盖有之乎？我未之见也。”
子曰：“民之过也，各于其党。观过，斯知仁矣。”
子曰：“朝闻道，夕死可矣。”
子曰：“士志于道，而耻恶衣恶食者，未足与议也。”
子曰：“君子之于天下也，无适也，无莫也，义之与比也。”
子曰：“君子怀德，小人怀土。君子怀刑，小人怀惠。”
子曰：“放于利而行，多怨。”
子曰：“能以礼让为国乎？何有？不能以礼让为国，如礼何？”
子曰：“不患无位，患所以立，不患莫己知也，求为可知也。”
子曰：“参乎，吾道一以贯之哉。曾子曰：“唯。子出，门人问曰：“何谓也？曾子曰：“夫子之道，忠恕而已矣。”
子曰：“君子喻于义，小人喻于利。”
子曰：“见贤思齐焉，见不贤者而内自省也。”
子曰：“事父母几谏，见志不从，又敬不违，劳不怨。”
子曰：“父母在，子不远游，游必有方。”
子曰：“三年无改于父之道，可谓孝矣。”
子曰：“父母之年，不可不知也，一则以喜，一则以惧。”
子曰：“古者言之不出也，耻躬之不逮也。”
子曰：“以约失之者鲜矣。”
子曰：“君子欲讷于言而敏于行。”
子曰：“德不孤，必有邻。”
子游曰：“事君数，斯辱矣；朋友数，斯疏矣。”
en:
[Chapter 4: Dwelling in Virtue]

The Master said, "It is virtuous manners which constitute the excellence of a neighbourhood. If a person in selecting a residence, does not fix on one where such prevail, how can one be wise?"
The Master said, "Those who are without virtue, cannot abide long either in a condition of poverty and hardship, or in a condition of enjoyment. The virtuous rest in virtue; the wise desire virtue."
The Master said, "It is only the truly virtuous person, who can love, or who can hate, others."
The Master said, "If the will be set on virtue, there will be no practice of wickedness."
The Master said, "Riches and honours are what people desire. If it cannot be obtained in the proper way, they should not be held. Poverty and meanness are what people dislike. If it cannot be obtained in the proper way, they should not be avoided. If a superior person abandon virtue, how can one fulfil the requirements of that name? The superior person does not, even for the space of a single meal, act contrary to virtue. In moments of haste, one cleaves to it. In seasons of danger, one cleaves to it."
The Master said, "I have not seen a person who loved virtue, or one who hated what was not virtuous. One who loved virtue, would esteem nothing above it. One who hated what is not virtuous, would practise virtue in such a way that one would not allow anything that is not virtuous to approach one's person. Is anyone able for one day to apply one's strength to virtue? I have not seen the case in which one's strength would be insufficient. Should there possibly be any such case, I have not seen it."
The Master said, "The faults of people are characteristic of the class to which they belong. By observing a person's faults, it may be known that one is virtuous."
The Master said, "If a person in the morning hear the right way, one may die in the evening without regret."
The Master said, "A scholar, whose mind is set on truth, and who is ashamed of bad clothes and bad food, is not fit to be discoursed with."
The Master said, "The superior person, in the world, does not set one's mind either for anything, or against anything; but what is right one will follow."
The Master said, "The superior person thinks of virtue; the small person thinks of comfort. The superior person thinks of the sanctions of law; the small person thinks of favours which one may receive."
The Master said, "One who acts with a constant view to one's own advantage will be much murmured against."
The Master said, "Is a prince able to govern one's kingdom with the complaisance proper to the rules of propriety, what difficulty will one have? If one cannot govern it with that complaisance, what has one to do with the rules of propriety?"
The Master said, "A person should say, I am not concerned that I have no place, I am concerned how I may fit myself for one. I am not concerned that I am not known, I seek to be worthy to be known."
The Master said, "Shen, my doctrine is that of an all-pervading unity." The disciple Zeng replied, "Yes." The Master went out, and the other disciples asked, saying, "What do his words mean?" Zeng said, "The doctrine of our master is to be true to the principles of our nature and the benevolent exercise of them to others—this and nothing more."
The Master said, "The mind of the superior person is conversant with righteousness; the mind of the mean person is conversant with gain."
The Master said, "When we see people of worth, we should think of equalling them; when we see people of a contrary character, we should turn inwards and examine ourselves."
The Master said, "In serving one's parents, a child may remonstrate with them, but gently; when one sees that they do not incline to follow one's advice, one shows an increased degree of reverence, but does not abandon one's purpose; and should they punish one, one does not allow oneself to murmur."
The Master said, "While one's parents are alive, the child may not go abroad to a distance. If one does go abroad, one must have a fixed place to which one goes."
The Master said, "If the child for three years does not alter from the way of one's father, one may be called filial."
The Master said, "The years of parents may by no means not be kept in the memory, as an occasion at once for joy and for fear."
The Master said, "The reason why the ancients did not readily give utterance to their words, was that they feared lest their actions should not come up to them."
The Master said, "The cautious seldom err."
The Master said, "The superior person wishes to be slow in one's words and earnest in one's conduct."
The Master said, "Virtue is not left to stand alone. One who practises it will have neighbours."
Ziyou said, "In serving a prince, frequent remonstrances lead to disgrace. Between friends, frequent reproofs make the friendship distant."

zh:
显德中，清河隐月山有侠士。其名不可考，有人谓其来去无踪，剑出无痕。若月辉星煜，飘然出尘也。故武林中多称月神。月神行刺，鲜有失。市间多持千金以求月神者，其弗顾之。显德末，契丹使臣经清河，有众侠士伏围于此，欲杀虏贼而报国恨也。忽视人头飞而起之，伏围侠士皆为月神所戮！天下遂唾月神，不知其所踪也。
有人曾于隐月#Y丹崖#E，见月神入湖，不复见矣。后来者寻之，唯见神女倒影，向月而歌，其音清越久不息。
en:
During the Xiande era, there was a knight-errant in Qinghe's Moonveil Mountain. Her real name remains unknown, but people said she came and went without a trace, and her sword strikes left no mark. Like the radiance of the moon and the glow of stars, she was ethereal and beyond the mundane, so she was widely known as the "Lunar Goddess" in the martial world.
The Lunar Goddess rarely failed in assassinations. Although many in the market offered a thousand gold coins to hire her, she ignored them all. At the end of the Xiande era, when envoys from Khitan passed through Qinghe, numerous chivalrous warriors ambushed them, intending to kill the envoys and avenge national hatred.
Suddenly, human heads were seen flying up, and all the ambushing warriors were slain by the Lunar Goddess! The world then reviled the Lunar Goddess, who vanished without a trace, and no one knows where she went. 
Some once saw the Lunar Goddess enter the lake at Moonveil Mountain's #YCrimson Cliff#E, never to be seen again. Those who searched later found only the Goddess's reflection, singing to the moon with a clear voice that lingered endlessly.

zh:
钱，是不难赚的。
学会这几招，让江湖没有赚不到的钱！

第一招：赚钱第一步，练手文津馆
列数江湖门派，最好偷的就是文津馆。这些书生穿衣服层层叠叠，少一层都没感觉。按老夫的经验，他们的钱袋通常藏在第二层和第四层，第三层则会放一本书。只要察觉不对，就往第三层摸，谎称要读书，他们必定会师瘾大发，当场上课，这时再出手很容易成功。如果还是被捉住，只用哭诉一番自己的悲惨生平，一样能捞个馒头。初出茅庐，最适合去这里练手。
不过要赚钱，当然不能满足在馒头。假扮文津馆弟子混入其中，才能应有尽有。这法子难度极高，需要学一绝招《千字文》。此招不能记录在册，想学的后辈可以找徐锦文口传。

第二招：走街串巷，轻松入账
谁能比九流门更知道开封的路？谁能比九流门更熟每条巷子？这也能赚钱！
只需要一根烧黑的棍子，画出走过的路和巷子，找到穿红黑衣服的三更天，就能凭这张《情报地图》赚到带路费。画画功夫练起来以后，再多记住各家的人和位置，画得更多更细，不必带路，都能赚到钱。运气好的话，还能得两个免费的保镖。
来，现在就试试吧！

第三招：合二为一，成就大钱
练熟前两招，就可以尝试这一式——做醉花阴的……下线！
众所周知，樊楼的花蝴蝶们最爱听街头巷尾的杂闻。记录这些杂闻的内容、绘制传出的地点，就能从醉花阴弟子手里换得情报费。
文津馆的毕竟还是些书生，三更天的人行踪不定，书画熟练之后，和醉花阴的交易才是稳定的收入啊！
但是记住，别转手又花到了他们身上去。行走江湖，最忌讳动心，尤其是动要酒水花费的心！一定要记住！

学会这三招，不能说财源滚滚，衣食无忧已经不在话下。
还想赚得更多？中册还有秘方！
en:
Making money isn't as hard as you might think. 
Learn a few key techniques, and there's no money in the jianghu you can't get your hands on! 

Technique One: Getting Started – Practice at the Inkbound Order 
Among all the jianghu sects, the Inkbound Order is the easiest target. The scholars there wear multiple layers of clothing—missing a layer doesn't seem odd to them. From my experience, their money pouches are usually hidden in the second and fourth layers, and the third layer usually holds a book. If you sense something's off, reach for the third layer, pretending you want to read—their eagerness to teach will give you the perfect chance to act. If you get caught, just share a heartfelt story about your hardships—you'll at least get a simple meal. If you're new to this, this place is the best for gaining experience. 
But if you want to make real money, don't settle for just a meal. Disguising yourself as an Inkbound disciple to blend in is the way forward. This method is more challenging and requires mastering a special skill called the "Thousand-Character Classic." This isn't written down anywhere; those interested should seek out Xu Jinwen for direct instruction. 

Technique Two: Roaming the Streets and Alleys to Earn Easily 
Who knows the streets of Kaifeng better than the Nine Mortal Ways folk? Who's more familiar with every alley? You can turn this knowledge into cash! 
All you need is a charred stick to map the routes and alleys you've traveled. Then, find Midnight Blades disciples dressed in red and black. With your "Intelligence Map," you can charge a fee for guiding the way. As your drawing skills improve and your knowledge of people and places deepens, you can create even more detailed maps. Eventually, you may earn money simply by selling these maps without even guiding anyone. If fortune favors you, you might also gain two free bodyguards. 
Give it a try! 

Technique Three: Combining the First Two to Make Big Money 
Once you've mastered the first two techniques, it's time to attempt this—becoming an informant for Velvet Shade! 
As everyone knows, the beauties at Revelry Hall love gossip from everywhere. Record and map these rumors and where they come from, and exchange this information for a fee with Velvet Shade disciples. 
After all, the Inkbound Order scholars are just bookish types, and those from Midnight Blades are unpredictable. Once you're skilled at gathering information and drawing maps, Velvet Shade will offer you a steady income! 
But remember—don't spend your earnings on them again. The worst mistake in the jianghu is letting your feelings get involved, especially when it leads to spending on drinks! Keep this in mind! 

Master these three techniques, and you won't just earn steadily—you'll be well off in no time. 
Want to make even more? The next volume contains secret methods!

人云小十七乃一痴儿。魏仁浦倒觉得“有教无类”，小十七不过比常人迟钝一些。是以他曾教小十七算数，几番下来，小十七当真有了长进。魏问：今有田一亩，耕作需半月，耕十亩田需几月？小十七答曰：五。一亩田，岁收两石米，问：五亩田岁收几石？小十七答曰：十石。魏仁浦大喜，直呼孔圣人所言不虚。小十七见状，亦拍手称好。

柴荣身死后，悬剑倾覆。魏有言：万剑铸成之际，便是众人归来之时。小十七遂问：铸一把剑需几日？魏答曰：需一月。十七道：一万把剑需一万月，一年有十二月。待十七铸完万剑，龙当守约乎？ 魏虽不忍，犹答曰：然。
en:
People often said that Lucky Seventeen was a simpleton. But Wei Renpu believed otherwise. "Education knows no class," he would say. To him, Lucky Seventeen was simply a little slower than most. So he began teaching the boy math. After a few rounds of lessons, Lucky Seventeen truly began to improve. 

One day, Wei asked, "If it takes half a month to till one acre of land, how long would it take to till ten?"

"Five months," Shiqi answered.

"And if one acre yields two picul of grain per year, how much would five acres yield?"

"Ten piculs," said Lucky Seventeen.

Wei Renpu was overjoyed, "The sages spoke true!"
Seeing his joy, Shiqi clapped along with him and beamed with pride. 

After the death of Chai Rong, the Hanging Blade finally disbanded. Wei once said: "When ten thousand swords are forged, the day of return shall come." 

Lucky Seventeen, hearing this, asked innocently, "How long does it take to forge one sword?"

"A month," Wei replied.

"Then ten thousand swords will take ten thousand months. There are twelve months in a year..."

$N亲启：
又是一年中秋，你在他乡一切可都还好？
前几日整理药方时，偶然翻出几页旧纸，上面尽是墨渍。细看才发觉，竟是从前誊的功课。
还记得吗？那时你闯了祸，被寒娘子罚抄书，你惦记着逛灯会，央求我和豆豆帮你一起抄，结果咱们仨都睡着了，没赶上灯会不说，还沾了一脸的墨水。等到半夜醒来，灯会早散了，只剩一轮圆月高高挂在天上。
你当时问我，为何大人们偏都爱盯着那白玉盘看，我一时答不上来，只会说圆圆的月最好看。
而今我大抵明白了，哪里是月色喜人，分明是赏月时人都在身边，不曾离去。
也不知你身处何地，远游在外，总归要保重身体。
对了，别忘了，今天要抬头看一看月亮呀。
en:
Dear $N,

Another Mid-Autumn Festival has come. How fare you in distant lands?
The other day, while organizing prescriptions, I stumbled upon a few old pages stained with ink. Upon closer look, they were copied lessons from years past.
One day, you'd gotten into trouble, and Madam Han made you transcribe scriptures as punishment. You were desperate to attend the lantern fair, so you begged Doudou and me to help. The three of us transcribed together and ended up falling asleep, missing the fair entirely, our faces smudged with ink. When we woke at midnight, the Lantern Fair was long over. Only a full moon hung high in the sky.
You asked me then: why do adults always stare at that jade plate? I was lost for words and only told you that the moon was prettiest when it was round.
Now I know why. It's not the moonlight that delights; it is because those we cherish are by our side.
I have no idea where you are right now. Though far away from home, you should take care of yourself.
Oh, and don't forget to look up at the moon tonight.
...This flavor... it brings tears to this old man's eyes!
Li Feiyu

Carver Yang is a cat with a surname, and she's proud of it.

In the Thousand-Buddha Vale, every statue bears the mark of Carver's claws atop its head. She sharpens her claws on stone Buddhas, and Carver is proud.

zh: 祁晟成了燕夫人，她履行约定，嫁给了当初赢过他的绿袍小将。不久北伐失败，伏马庄因未能收回战争中的损失而愈加没落，祁晟跟随退出行伍的夫君燕荧定居丰禾村，倒也没受太大苦楚。婚后的祁大小姐并没有放弃下象棋的爱好，她反复打谱钻研，终于破解了当初输给燕荧的那局棋，顿觉吐气扬眉。可见她嘴上不说，但心里一直憋着气呢！或许是经过此番磨炼棋艺提高，她与夫君下棋虽然每每难解难分，但最后总能胜出。燕荧输棋也不在意，依旧笑眯眯地表示，等他研究一番再行比过。如此一进一退，夫妻二人很是相得，当真羡煞旁人。然而这份和谐在祁晟发现对方故意让子时被打破了。祁大小姐非常愤怒——这是对象棋的不尊重！这是对她的不尊重！大小姐雷厉风行、说一不二，立刻收拾东西回了娘家伏马庄。她撂下话来，此番燕荧若是不能拿出认错的诚意，她绝对不要回去！
en: Qi Sheng becomes Mrs. Yan, honoring her promise by marrying the young general in green who once bests her. Not long after, the northern expedition fails. Finesteed Hamlet, unable to recover its wartime losses, falls further into decline. Qi Sheng follows her husband Yan Ying, who retires from the military, and they settle in Harvestfall Village. Life there is modest, but not harsh. Even after marriage, the proud young lady never gives up her love for chess. She studies manuals day and night and eventually cracks the match she once lost to Yan Ying. Elated, she feels she finally clears her name. She stews over that loss all along. Her skill sharpens with the effort, and though she and her husband are often evenly matched, she starts winning more and more. Yan Ying doesn't mind losing; he always smiles and says he will study a bit and challenge her again later. This push and pull becomes their rhythm, a harmony that others envy. But that harmony shatters the day Qi Sheng realizes he has been letting her win. She is furious. Such moves insult the game and insult her. The lady of Finesteed Hamlet is not one to let things slide. Resolute and unbending, she packs her things and returns to her maiden home. Before leaving, she makes her stance clear: unless Yan Ying shows genuine remorse, she will not return.

zh: 木简，1973年出土于肩水金关遗址。简文记载是尹衡写给伟卿的一封问候信。信中多处表达了尹衡对伟卿的殷切问候，如“起居燥湿”“强饭厚自爱”“慎春气”等，都是汉时书信中寻常问候习语。尹衡在信里的一句“塞上诚毋它可道者”，道出了唯有在给友人写信时，才能打发边塞生活的乏味，聊表思乡之情。
en: Uncovered in 1973 at the Golden Pass Ruins, this bamboo slip contains a personal letter from a man named Yin Heng to his friend Weiqing. The text is filled with heartfelt well-wishes, featuring everyday greetings typical of the Han era. Yin Heng asks after his friend's "daily comfort" (literally, how he is adapting to the "dryness and dampness" of the weather), urges him to "eat heartily and take good care of yourself," and reminds him to "be mindful of the spring air." One poignant line captures the essence of the text: "Honestly, there is nothing else to speak of here on the frontier." This brief admission reveals how writing to a friend was his only solace, a fleeting escape from the crushing monotony of garrison life and a quiet expression of homesickness.

zh:
秦奋今年二十一，心里揣着一个违背父母期待的愿望——他，想当英雄！
才不是泛泛于田野的那种英雄，他的心愿具体得很，要先当捕快，再破大案，造福四方，名留青史。
按理来说，名留青史最难。可对秦奋来说，当上捕快这第一步已难上青天，谁叫秦奋有一对开文房四宝店的爹娘呢。
秦奋的爹娘在本地也算半个文人，自然盼着独子亦能饱腹诗书，有朝一日继承家业。
可惜秦奋打小就坐不住，只要一摊开书，不消一炷香的功夫就能梦游千里之外。
秦奋的爹娘为此着急上火，跟着书本学了不少劝学怪招，什么头悬梁、锥刺股、连家都搬了三次，专挨着常来铺子的老熟客住，却也不见效果……秦奋还是那个秦奋，沾书就着。

直到有一天，秦奋的爹娘意外地发现秦奋竟在挑灯夜读。
窗户外，他爹娘相拥而泣，感动得老泪纵横：还得是名字起得好啊，秦奋果然好学了！
第二日，秦奋打开卧房的门，同爹娘大声宣布——他，要去做捕快了！
爹娘这才知道，秦奋看的那是什么正经书，不过是一本叫做《不捕不快》三流小说。
后来发生的事，秦奋不愿回想。那是他第一次找到自己的愿望，也是第一次知道自己和愿望的距离竟然有那么远。
秦奋和爹娘争个不休，最后还是败下阵来，被爹娘托了关系、连捆带绑地送至墨城求学。
还没轮到他不捕不快人家，自己倒是被不捕不快了。
秦奋在墨城的学堂也坐上过几个月，长老们说得是好听。可是书里那个叫李三刀的捕快，左手一扶额、右手一抬指，就能在人群里一把揪出真凶的风流做派，总是反复出现在秦奋的眼前。
啊，当上捕快这件事，果真已一刻不能再等。

于是，秦奋四处打听，终于找到一个写着“解忧司”三个字的偏僻小院。
虽然环境不尽人意，但对秦奋来说，这就是他梦想着的地方。
他不顾甄贵的阻拦，死气白咧地就在这呆下了。甄贵不让他进屋，他就索性睡在院子里，一躺就是三个月。
更是不知去哪儿打了一件和甄贵一模一样的制服，从此甄贵去哪他去哪。
久而久之，山民们也自然把他认作了解忧司的一员，秦捕快、秦捕快的叫着。
“陈叔家的鸡还没找见，徐婶子托我把鸡蛋收回去，一会还要把这米给陶瘸子送过去……哦！木鸢原地打转，也得修修！”
或许是贪图这一声声秦捕快，秦奋每天两眼一睁就是干，像是有花不完的力气似的。
“诶，你真觉得在这你能当上英雄？”甄贵眯着眼打量着这个一腔热血的古怪年轻人，作出好意提醒。
此刻的秦奋左手抱着一篮子鸡蛋，右手提着一小袋粟米，头顶还顶着一根鸡毛，认真思考了一下，大声地说，“当然！”
en:
At twenty-one, Qin Fen harbored a secret ambition that went completely against his parents' wishes. He wanted to be a hero.

He didn't want to be the wandering, aimless sort of hero. His goal was specific: first, become a constable. Next, solve a massive case. Finally, bring peace to the land and go down in history.
Logically, going down in history should have been the hardest part. But for Qin Fen, just taking the first step to become a constable was as hard as climbing to the heavens. Who told him to be born to parents who ran a stationery shop selling the Four Treasures of the Study?

The elder Qins were minor scholars in their hometown and naturally hoped their only son would be well-read and eventually inherit the family business.
Unfortunately, Qin Fen was completely incapable of sitting still. The moment he opened a book, his mind would wander miles away in less time than it takes a stick of incense to burn.

His parents were frantic. They tried all the bizarre motivational tactics they read about in ancient texts, like tying his hair to a ceiling beam or pricking his thigh with an awl. They even moved three times just to live next door to the scholars who frequented their shop. Nothing worked. Qin Fen remained exactly the same: a boy who fell asleep the second he touched a book.

Until one day, his parents were shocked to find him burning the midnight oil, reading intently.
Outside his window, they hugged each other and wept tears of joy, praising their decision to name him Qin Fen, which sounded just like the word for "diligent." He was finally studying!
The next morning, Qin Fen threw open his bedroom door and proudly announced to his parents that he was going to become a constable.

Only then did they realize their son hadn't been reading any serious classics at all. It was just a cheap pulp novel titled "No Catch, No Peace."
Qin Fen preferred not to think about what happened next. It was the first time he had found his true calling, and also the first time he realized just how agonizingly far away it was.
After arguing with his parents endlessly, he ultimately lost. Through their connections, he was practically tied up and shipped off to Mohist City to study. 
Before he could go out catching criminals, he had been caught himself.

Qin Fen managed to sit in the classrooms of Mohist City for a few months. The elders spoke well enough, but the image of Li Sandao, the dashing constable from his novel who could pluck a murderer out of a crowd with a single point of his finger, kept flashing before his eyes.
Ah, he couldn't wait another second to become a constable!
So, after asking around, Qin Fen finally found a secluded courtyard with a plaque that read "Bureau of Relief."

It wasn't the most glamorous place, but to Qin Fen, it was exactly what he had dreamed of.
Ignoring Zhen Gui's endless attempts to chase him away, he stubbornly refused to leave. When Zhen Gui locked him out of the house, he simply slept in the yard for three months straight.
He even went off and somehow procured a uniform identical to Zhen Gui's. From then on, wherever Zhen Gui went, he followed.

Over time, the mountain villagers naturally assumed he was part of the Bureau of Relief, calling him "Constable Qin" this and "Constable Qin" that.
"Uncle Chen's chicken is still missing! Aunt Xu asked me to bring the eggs back, and later I need to deliver this millet to Lame Tao... Oh! And that wooden eagle is just spinning in circles, I need to fix that too!"
Perhaps he was just addicted to being called Constable Qin, but the moment he opened his eyes every morning, he worked like he had an endless supply of energy.

"Hey, do you really think you can become a hero here?" Zhen Gui asked, squinting at the passionate, eccentric young man, offering a word of well-meaning advice.
At that moment, Qin Fen was holding a basket of eggs in his left arm and a sack of millet in his right, with a stray chicken feather stuck in his hair. He thought about it seriously for a second and then shouted at the top of his lungs, "Absolutely!"

因为下棋赢了伏马庄的大小姐祁晟，燕荧抱得美人归。成亲前夜，他的大舅子祁玉棠约他到马场外谈心。一番拳脚相加的亲切交流之后，他便听大舅子开始了漫长的絮叨：什么便宜他了，自从小妹放下“谁下棋赢过她就嫁谁”的话，伏马庄上上下下严防死守，将来挑战棋艺的人是筛了又筛、过了又过，哪怕将人留成大姑娘，也不能看她嫁给不靠谱的男人，没想到却让他这个军汉子捡了漏啦；什么小妹不喜欢输棋，要是输棋就算面上看不出来，心里也能难受好几天，他不许再赢她棋，更不能惹她不开心啦；什么好好待小妹，要是敢欺负她一定揍得他满地找牙云云……
燕荧默默听着，一一应承下来——他当然会好好爱护他未来的娘子，叫她一辈子高高兴兴的。他喜欢看她笑，只有笑着的表情才最适合她。
en:
Because he had beaten the young lady of Finesteed Hamlet, Qi Sheng, at chess, Yan Ying was set to marry her. On the eve of the wedding, his soon-to-be brother-in-law, Qi Yutang, called him out to the stables for a private chat. After a "friendly" exchange that involved a few punches, Qi Yutang finally got down to business, launching into a long-winded rant. He said Yan Ying had gotten the deal of a lifetime. Ever since Qi Sheng had declared she'd marry the man who could beat her at chess, everyone at Finesteed Hamlet had kept a tight watch, testing every challenger. Better she stay unmarried than end up with someone unworthy. Somehow, this rough soldier had slipped through. Qi Yutang warned him that Qi Sheng hated losing at chess. Even if she smiled on the surface, a loss would sit with her for days. "So listen up, from now on, you let her win. Keep her smiling. If you ever make her cry, I'll beat you so bad you won't even find your teeth." Qi Yutang went on like that for a good while.
Yan Ying listened quietly, promising to take good care of his future wife and to make her happy. He loved her smile. When she smiled, it was as if the whole world shone.

听闻汝在乐安浦中，与乡人饮酒笑谈，携各派友人同游，日暮方归，好不快活！此间山水清旷，正合汝性情，为师倒也欣然。
然青州近日，风色有异。乐安浦地虽偏静，却通舟车，村中往来者杂。汝既在彼，且自游玩，只于醉饱之余，多抬抬眼，若遇寻常之外者，心中默识，不必刻意，切莫扰了乡间风光。

en:
To my disciple Youzhi:

I hear that you have been drinking and laughing with the locals at Tranquil Pier, touring the sights with friends from various sects, and returning only at sunset. What a joyous life! The scenery there is clear and open, perfectly suiting your nature. As your master, I am quite pleased for you.
However, the winds in Qingzhou have shifted recently. Tranquil Pier may be secluded, but it connects many routes by boat and carriage, drawing a complicated mix of travelers to the village. Since you are there, continue to enjoy yourself, but when you are full of wine and food, just keep your eyes open. If you notice anyone out of the ordinary, silently commit them to memory. There is no need to be deliberate about it, and make sure not to disturb the peaceful countryside.
All else remains as usual. Do not neglect your cultivation. And if you stumble upon anything amusing, do not forget to write back and tell your master!

四位师兄师姐游学在际，出山前，做毒虫机关，以奇音诱杀山中毒物。只为向师父证明，毒虫机关亦可为有益之事。并在共制五毒过程中，悄然将精微机关术的最后法门传授师弟。
铁心蜈为当年五毒虫之一，为三师姐丁解香所作。
愿得一铁心，不惧流言烁。此生不嗔恨，心皎如月光。
en:
A Mohist elder once took in five disciples. All studied delicate mechanisms, creating many wondrous devices. Among other disciples, they were jointly called the Five Wonders.
The youngest was a survivor of the war outside the mountains, who fled into Hidden Mountain. His heart full of hate, he used his skills to craft poisonous insects, intending revenge once his arts were mastered. Seeing his twisted intent, the elder never imparted the final secrets.
Before their study tours, the four senior disciples crafted insect mechanisms: using strange sounds to lure and eliminate mountain pests. They aimed to prove to their master that such mechanisms could also be beneficial. While jointly creating the "Five Poisons," they secretly passed the final techniques to their junior.
Ironheart Centipede, one of the original Five Poisons, was created by Third Senior Sister Ding Jiexiang.
Wishing for an iron heart, unafraid of slander's glare.
In this life, no resentment held, and a heart as bright as moonlight.

这十数年来本公子一直好奇，能从那吃人不吐骨头的疑冢里带出玄鸟佩的会是怎样一人，今日方知竟是你。想来也是，江湖传言你这人颇有几分狼性，一旦认定什么，便定要夺到手里，如此性子，确实肖似舅舅。
舅舅晚年一心欲寻像他之人承继未央城，为此他甚至破例许我与其诸子同经考验。我之所以能够胜过诸兄弟，便是因为足够贪婪迫切，我比他们每一个人都更需要城主之位，以此带母亲脱离苦海。
舅舅离世之前，将疑冢与玄鸟佩之事告知于我，他本欲以此寻得天下最肖他之人掌管未央城，遗憾此生终究无从得见。所幸于我生年，此人终于出现……很高兴认识你，本公子的对手，或者是……这世上与本公子最为相似之人？
en:
To $N,
For years, I've wondered who could possibly survive that deadly tomb with the Mystic Bird Pendant in hand. You made it. You remind me of my uncle.
In his later years, Uncle sought someone worthy to inherit Weiyang City. He even let me compete with his sons. I won because I had more at stake—to save my mom.
Before he died, Uncle shared with me the secret of the tomb and pendant. He hoped this path would bring him the most competent heir to Weiyang City. Sadly, he never lived to see it. It's my honor to meet you—my rival, or perhaps... my closest counterpart in this world?

Silken birds nest in the fragrance of lotuses, brocaded carp circle the shadow of the isle. 

Ornamental carp originated in China. In Ting Shi by Yue Ke, it is recorded: "Today, there are fish keepers in the capital who can turn fish golden, crucian carp being the finest, carp coming second. Wealthy nobles would often carve stone pools and place them by windows and eaves for viewing pleasure." The golden crucian carp mentioned here is the ancestor of today's goldfish, while the golden carp is the ancestor of ornamental carp. This shows that the history of ornamental carp farming in China dates back to the Song dynasty.

zh:
过了这河，她就能回家了。
秀秀望着河对岸簇簇营火，一时恍惚。她很少从这个角度，看自己的家。
那边过去是村口的老井，那里该是通往家门的小路，那儿……是她等爹爹回家时呆过的河滩。
从前阿爹来南岸割麦子，她就坐在那儿等阿爹。一个人害怕的时候，她就唱起那支阿爹教她的曲儿，阿爹听见了，就一边干活，一边应和着她。
“天上桫椤是什么人栽，地下的黄河是什么人开？”

也是在这片河滩，在那个逃难的夜里，她再一次唱起了这支歌。
远处的马蹄声和哭喊声还未停歇，她不知道自己要去哪里，不知道自己还能做些什么。
望着对岸的麦田，她不知不觉间，哼起了熟悉的调子。
水还在和着，风也还在和着，可在对岸唱歌的阿爹，再也回不来了。
“天上桫椤是王母娘娘栽，地下的黄河是老龙王开。”
不远处忽然传来一声细微的接唱。是阿爹吗？可阿爹他……
秀秀循着声音找去，那里只有一个与家人失散的孩子。孩子听了这曲儿，才知晓秀秀并非虏人，而是乡邻。
那个夜里，秀秀的歌声断断续续地在河岸旁响起。越来越多的人辨认出这熟悉的调子，慢慢聚拢到她身旁。
“去行营吧！”秀秀看着月光下，因着歌儿寻到彼此的乡邻们，原本不安的心，又生发出许多勇气。

曲儿从北岸飘来了南岸。
营地里，听歌的人多了，应和的人也多了。被马蹄声惊醒而无法入睡的孩童，因抗击虏人而伤病在榻的侠士，帮她一起给大家熬汤的婶娘……
“把歌儿唱起，大步往前走！”
秀秀又想起阿爹从麦田回来时总爱说的话。那支曲儿不仅仅帮她驱赶了恐惧，还引着许多人走出了这漫漫无垠的黑夜。
有些人听了曲儿，作了歇，心里有了底气，继续往南边走了。
有些人唱和着，打着拍子，喝了酒，手上有了力气，往北边去了。
再后来——
她看了看自己身边站着的这些人。他们从天南地北而来，正要跨过河去，把她的故乡一寸寸夺回来。
他们静静地听着她唱。
“什么人把守三关外——”
阿爹，我遇到了很多很厉害的大英雄，跟着他们，我……也能杀得了虏人。我要带着他们往北走，去给阿爹报仇，给咱家报仇。
“什么人离家就没有回来——”
阿爹，等我到了北岸，回了家，一点点把咱的屋子建起来。再在门口种一排麦子，阿爹闻着麦子香，听着曲儿，一定能找到回家的路。
en:
Once she crossed this river, she would be home.

Xiuxiu looked at the clusters of campfires on the far bank and lost herself for a moment. She did not often see her home from this side.
Over there was the old well at the entrance to the village. There should be the path that led to her door. And there... that was the stretch of riverbank where she used to wait for her father to come home.

Back then, when her father came to the south bank to cut wheat, she would sit there and wait for him. If she got scared being there alone, she would sing the tune he had taught her. When he heard it, he would sing back while he worked.

"Who planted the tree up in heaven?
Who carved out the Yellow River below?"

It was on that same stretch of riverbank, on the night they fled, that she sang the song again.

The sound of hoofbeats and crying had not yet died away. She did not know where she was supposed to go, or what she could still do.
Looking at the wheat fields across the river, she found herself humming that familiar tune.

The water still answered it. The wind still answered it too. But the father who used to sing back from the other side would never come back again.

"The Queen Mother planted the tree in heaven.
The Dragon King carved the Yellow River below."

Then, not far away, a faint voice picked up the song.

Was it her father?
But her father...

Xiuxiu followed the sound and found only a child who had been separated from his family. It was only after hearing the song that the child realized Xiuxiu was no invader, but someone from home.

That night, Xiuxiu's singing rose and fell along the riverbank, broken and unsteady.
More and more people recognized the tune and slowly gathered around her.

"Let's head for the camp!"

In the moonlight, Xiuxiu looked at the familiar faces finding one another through the song. The fear in her chest eased, and in its place came something like courage.

The tune drifted from the north bank to the south.

In the camp, more people listened, and more people joined in. Children who had been startled awake by hoofbeats and could not fall asleep again. Fighters laid up with wounds from battles against the invaders. Aunties helping her boil soup for everyone.

"Sing loud and keep walking."

Xiuxiu thought again of the words her father always liked to say when he came back from the wheat fields.

That song did more than drive away her fear. It helped lead many people out through that long, endless night.

Some heard the song, stopped to rest, found their footing again, and kept heading south.
Others sang along, clapped out the beat, drank their fill, found strength in their hands again, and turned north.
Later still...

She looked at the people standing beside her now.
They had come from all over, and soon they would cross the river and take back her homeland inch by inch.
They listened quietly as she sang.

"Who keeps watch beyond the passes..."

Father, I have met so many great heroes. With them beside me, I can kill the invaders too. I am going north with them, to avenge you, and to avenge our family.

"Who left home and never came back..."

Father, when I reach the north bank and go home, I will rebuild our house bit by bit. Then I will plant a row of wheat by the door. When you smell the wheat and hear this song, you will be able to find your way home.

胡辣汤豆腐脑两掺
谁说阴阳不可调和，谁说泾渭必须分明，谁说黑白注定对立？日月尚有同天之时，何况诱人的胡辣汤和豆腐脑。中原小吃摊上有着无穷的智慧：若汤太辣难以入口，便加进去一勺清香的白花花的豆腐脑。若豆腐脑无味，便加一勺麻辣咸香的胡辣汤。天与地本就同撑乾坤，王与后本就夫妻一体，正如掺在一起的胡辣汤和豆腐脑。如果并非阔绰又好胃口的成年人，也可以叫老板上一份两掺。一碗汤里黑白相拥，世间无尽奥妙滋味都在其中了。说到底，人这辈子也就图一个咸淡适中，既要又要的幸福生活。
en:
3. Hulatang and Tofu Pudding, Mixed

Who says opposites cannot mix? Who says black and white must stay apart? The sun and moon can share the same sky, so why not hulatang and tofu pudding?

Street stalls in the Central Plains know a thing or two. If the soup is too fiery, add a spoonful of pale, fragrant tofu pudding. If the tofu pudding tastes too mild, stir in a spoonful of hulatang, spicy, savory, and numbing.

Heaven and earth hold up the same world. A king and his queen belong together. So do these two, once you mix them. If you are not the kind of well-off, big-appetite adult who can finish two full bowls, just ask the vendor for a half-and-half.

In one bowl, black and white mingle, and all kinds of flavor open up. In the end, most of us are simply chasing a life that hits the right balance, salty and mild, wanting both and getting both.

zh:
一橹摇来半湖风，
七个手足各不同。
皆能破浪渡远客，
唯我上船人先倒。

大哥从小便告诫我们兄弟姐妹：我家世世代代在杭城摇橹吃饭，对水路的熟悉，须得胜过对自家门槛。
水纹往哪边散，客人往哪边看，风从哪座桥洞里钻出来，都要心里有数。
这是咱家的根基，亦是船会的脸面。我们【任你行】船会，向来讲究四个字：“舟行天下”。又有后四个字，大哥说须喊得响亮些，叫作：“杭行必达”。
算算家中七个兄弟姐妹，最出息的，除大哥外，便是四弟与五妹。
四弟天资聪颖，见一座桥能讲三段典故，见一棵柳能说出前朝风月；五妹能说会道，市井巷陌、人情往来，无一不通。坐上他们的船，客人总是心旷神怡，银钱也掏得爽快。
我便不是那块料。
……我晕船。
虽说生在湖边，晕船二字写出来有辱门楣，但人各有短，橹各有偏。
大哥原想替我排个日课：晨摇十圈，午摇十圈，暮摇十圈，七日一小结，半月一总评。我照办三日，吐在船舷两回，抱着桨杆说胡话一回。自此大哥叹曰：“摆三虽不能摆渡，尚可摆事。”原话其实是叫我别在船上吐了，赶紧滚上岸去。
我思量再三，既不能在水上尽责，便在岸上巡湖。水上的事归他们，这岸上的事，总得有人管吧？
世人只知泛舟是游湖，未必知道慢走、闲坐、搭话、劝阻、拾掇，也都是游湖的门道。
为了向大哥证明我绝非游手好闲，特拟此《西湖游览手记》：

北里湖
路旁若遇醉酒人，不可急着嫌他酒气冲天。
须先问他从哪家酒楼来，是否寻得归路。若他已醉得不省人事，只会指着湖面傻乐，高喊“好大一碗酒”……此时切莫硬拉，能劝其在岸边坐稳吹吹凉风，别一头栽进这“大碗”里，亦算维护了湖畔的清净。

孤山林荫
此处松鼠常出没。若见游人拿吃食饲喂松鼠，须上前阻止，言辞要软，身法要快。
为何？要么是客官不慎被松鼠咬上一口；要么是松鼠吃得太胖，跑不动道，改日便被天上的野鹰叼了去。尊重松鼠，人人有责，切记切记。

柳岸水亭
今日一青年望水出神，似是落榜，似是欠债，亦或单纯是不想回家。
此类不可贸然盘问，只宜上前轻声说一句：“风大，可要坐远些？”
若他愿说，便静静听着；
若他不愿说，便陪他一同看水。人在湖边，总要有个不被催促的时辰。

虽未摇橹，亦未载客，然北里湖、白堤、孤山、又一楼、柳岸诸处，皆已走到；醉者老者，孩童青年，松鼠野鸭，亦各有照应。若大哥仍问我这算不算船会正事，我便答：船在水上行，人也在岸上行。
我李摆三虽晕船，却不晕湖。舟可渡人，路可通人。天地之大，走在这西湖岸边，处处柳暗花明。只要心不沉底，哪里都是好风景。
en:
One oar stirs half the lake to breeze,
Seven siblings, each their own decree.
All can cleave the waves for guests from afar,
Yet I alone fall sick the moment I board.

Elder Brother warned us siblings since we were young: our family has rowed the oars of Hangzhou for generations, and our knowledge of the waterways must run deeper than the threshold of our own home.
Which way the ripples scatter, which way the passengers gaze, which archway the wind comes whistling through—all of it, we must have got it covered.
This is the foundation of our family, and the face of our boat guild. Our guild, Wanderer's Passage, has always lived by four words: "Boats Roam the World." And Elder Brother says the next three must be shouted louder still: "Hangzhou, Always Delivered."
Counting up our seven siblings, the most promising—besides Elder Brother—are Fourth Brother and Fifth Sister.
Fourth Brother is sharp of mind; show him a single bridge and he can recount three tales of old; show him one willow tree and he'll speak of the romances of the fallen dynasty. Fifth Sister has a silver tongue, versed in every matter of the streets and alleys, every thread of human affairs. Guests who board their boats always leave with hearts at ease, and their silver comes out all the more willingly.
I, however, am not cut from that cloth.
...I get seasick.
Though born by the lakeside, to admit to seasickness would shame the family name—but every man has his weakness, and every oar its own tilt.
Elder Brother once meant to set me a daily regimen: ten circuits at dawn, ten at noon, ten at dusk, a small review every seven days, a full account every half month. I followed it for three days, retched over the gunwale twice, and once, clutching the oar shaft, babbled nonsense. After that, Elder Brother sighed: "Though Third Son of the Li family cannot ferry others, he may yet ferry matters along." What he truly meant, of course, was: stop retching on the boat and get yourself ashore.
After much thought, since I could not fulfill my duty upon the water, I chose instead to patrol the lake by land. The waters belong to them—but surely someone must tend to the shore?
Most folk think that boating alone makes for a lake excursion, never knowing that a slow walk, an idle sit, a friendly word, a gentle warning, a bit of tidying up—these too are all part of the art of touring the lake.
To prove to Elder Brother that I am no idler, I have specially composed this West Lake Travel Notes:

North Lake
Should you come across a drunken man by the roadside, do not be quick to recoil from the reek of wine upon him.
First ask which tavern he has come from, and whether he can still find his way home. If he is already too far gone to know himself, only pointing foolishly at the lake and crying "What a great bowl of wine!" ...at such a time, do not drag him by force. Better to coax him into sitting steadily by the shore, letting the cool breeze clear his head, so he does not tumble headfirst into that "great bowl." This too is a way of keeping the lakeside peaceful.

Lone Hill's Shaded Grove
Squirrels often appear in this place. Should you see a tourist feeding them by hand, you must step in and stop it—words soft, movements quick.
Why so? Either the guest may be nipped by an unwary squirrel, or the squirrel, grown too fat to scurry away, may one day be snatched up by a wild hawk from the sky. Respecting the squirrels is everyone's duty—mark this well, mark this well.

Willow Bank Water Pavilion
Today, a young man stared blankly at the water, as though he had failed some examination, or owed some debt, or simply did not wish to go home.
Such a case is not to be pressed with questions. It is best only to step near and say softly: "The wind is strong—would you care to sit farther back?"
If he wishes to speak, then listen quietly;
if he does not, then simply watch the water together with him. A person by the lake should always be allowed one hour free from hurry.

Though I have not rowed an oar, nor carried a single passenger, I have walked through North Lake, Bai Causeway, Lone Hill, Another Tavern, Willow Bank, and all the rest; drunkards and elders, children and young men, squirrels and wild ducks—each has received its due care. Should Elder Brother still ask whether this counts as true business of the boat guild, I would answer: boats travel upon the water, but people travel upon the shore as well.
I, Li Baisan, may grow seasick upon a boat, but never sick of the lake. A boat may ferry a man across; a road may lead a man onward all the same. Vast as heaven and earth may be, walking along this shore of West Lake, one finds hope and brightness in every turn. So long as the heart does not sink to the bottom, every place is a fine view.

zh:
祁义棠与顾盼成婚时，有个少年没有赴宴，也再没能回来。本该喧腾的喜宴静得骇人，满座宾朋无人敢言语。唯独他们身上火红的喜服，张牙舞爪，像血。
他们等了一夜，只等来一纸荒唐的判决：自那日起，祁家同燕北盟成了一根绳上的蚂蚱。故土沦陷，族人蒙羞，亲友横死——那一张张愤恨的面容，早已化作了深夜灼人的梦魇，成了他们此生的宿命。
为着死于虏人手中的萤火弟子之仇，为着殁于幽州的祁氏亲友之仇，他们与至亲诀别，却与彼此相守，共同守护着心头那一簇小小的火苗。
他们曾笃信，那一簇火焰，终有一天会变成燎原的大火，烧尽他们所有的愤怒与不甘。
可到头来，那火什么也不是。是天地不仁，是世事无常，是不堪重托，又错付了忠心，他们一同陷入这阴谋的洪流。
火光渐微，在将熄的刹那，他们最后一次望向了彼此：复仇已告失败，可他们仍要奔赴，随那曾点燃他们的火苗的燕北盟，到王清将军身边去。他们将为柴为薪，投身怒火，死得其所，化作那永不熄灭的一缕灰。
en:
When Qi Yitang and Gu Pan were wed, one young man never came to the feast, and never came back at all. What should have rung with celebration lay instead in a silence that chilled the bone. The hall was full of guests, yet none dared speak; only the vivid red of the couple's wedding robes seemed to bare its teeth, red as blood.
They waited out the night, and all that came was one absurd decree: from that day on, the Qi family and the Northern Vow were bound to a single fate. Homeland fallen, kinsmen shamed, loved ones cut down. Those faces contorted with hatred had long since become the nightmares that scorched their sleep, and the destiny that would follow them all their lives.
For the Fireflies slain by invaders' hands, for the Qi kin who perished in Youzhou, they parted from their dearest and held only to each other, guarding together the small flame kindled in their hearts.
They once believed with all their souls that this flame would one day rage across the plains, and burn away every last measure of their fury and regret.
But in the end, the fire came to nothing. Heaven was merciless, the world unfaithful; their loyalty was misplaced and their trust ill-repaid, and together they were swept into the flood of another's treachery.
The firelight dwindled. In the instant before it died, they looked to each other one final time: their vengeance had failed, and still they would go. They would follow the Northern Vow that first lit their flame, all the way to General Wang Qing's side. They would be the kindling cast into the blaze, meeting a death well earned, becoming a single wisp of ash that would never go cold.
Yang Ming

On the west side of the Imperial City, Shengping Tower is a rare pocket of quiet elegance. The courtyard opens wide, with a pond, pavilions and terraces all around, and a central stage for music and dance.
It was built for banquets. Back when Empress Dowager Mingxian was alive, she often came to watch performances, and even hosted family feasts here with His Majesty and his brothers. The archery contests were the liveliest part, all to amuse their mother.
These days frugality is the rule, banquets are few, and the tower has gone quiet. The musicians and performers have time on their hands, and they do not seem to mind. If I weren't here on official business, I'd spend the night with a jar of wine and listen until dawn.

zh:
淇娘吾爱青鉴： 
桃林别后，白本以必死之志蹈虎狼之宴。忽得惊涛掌确讯，如见云隙漏月。然四顾皆敌，援手日稀，环伺欲噬我者益众。纵惊涛掌相助，难有万全之计。若无达摩渡江之机，金桃重托，恐成虚妄。 
吾计已决：倘力竭身死，必抱金桃共沉黄河。虽负藏贤掌临终之托，绝不予奸邪此宝，再增杀孽。悲乎？穷途不能遂志；幸哉！吾与卿此心同途。

每忆北山塬中，藏贤掌相告，寺僧舍命相护，厨医道沥血相援，白五内俱焚。 
又闻师门之难，白不能手刃仇雠，反屈身事之，虚与周旋。每念此，泣血锥心不能止也。
前人赤心，皆付于我；我今一死，其事弗彰。后世唯知“方白叛门”污名。此间肝胆，更与何人说？  
青史无情。金桃西行，已成迷雾。后之视今，亦犹今之视昔。千秋功罪，谁复辨之？ 
然狂风已至，前贤折尽。唯继踵而往。

吾不能与卿相守。愿卿得返无心谷，平安终老。愿卿移所以爱我者，爱此破碎河山——怜乱世白骨，恤孤寡无依，悲如卿一般于血海向光之人。
若此，则白以区区之死，照卿爱之弘毅。

临别悲绝，惟祈岁安。

方白
en:
My dear Qiniang,
Since we parted in the Peach Grove, I went to that banquet with no hope of returning alive. News of Palm Strike Master reached me and brought me hope, but enemies crowd ever closer. Those who might help us are dwindling; those who want me dead seem endless. Even with his help, our chances are slim. Without a miracle, the Golden Peach entrusted to me may never reach its end.
I have made my choice: if I fall fighting, I will sink into the Yellow River with the Golden Peach in my arms. Better to fail the trust of a dying friend than let wicked men seize it and spill even more blood. A pitiful end, isn't it? To reach the brink and still fall short. Still, I find comfort in knowing that our hearts will always be one.
Whenever I think of that day when Palm Strike Sage told me how the monks gave their lives to protect us, how cooks and healers shed their blood to help... it breaks my heart.
And now word comes that our sect has suffered. I cannot avenge it with my own hands; instead, I must bow to our enemies and play along with their lies. The thought leaves me gutted. Each tear feels laced with blood.
All the loyalty and courage of those before us now rest with me. If I die, their stories may die too, and the world will remember only "Fang Bai the traitor." Where can I lay down this grief, this devotion? 
History is a cold judge. The Golden Peach's journey west is already fading into obscurity. Future generations will look at us as we look at those long gone. Who can truly decide the right and wrong of centuries?
But the storm has come, and our elders have fallen. We can only keep walking.

I cannot grow old by your side. I can only hope you return safely to Hollow Vale and spend the rest of your life in peace. And I hope that the love you once gave me, you can give instead to this broken land, to the innocent caught in turmoil, to the lost and the lonely, to those, like you, who still look for light in the midst of bloodshed.
If you can do that, then even my small, unremarkable death will cast a little light on the love you hold.

My heart breaks as I write this. May you know peace, year after year.
Fang Bai

zh:
开运三年九月二十五日，阴。
今日入朝面圣，陈退虏之策，果未纳，更牵连郭将军被斥。恨矣！愧矣！
当今之计，唯北上拜会杜重威，盼借其之力，以中策退敌。然余知重威之为人，此行恐难奏效，甚忧。
临行之前幸得柴荣将军相送，得将军之言，余心中大悟，记之以醒余生。
柴将军曰：“昔日太宗玄武门下杀伐决断，方有贞观太平、百年盛世。大丈夫志在青云，当一目千里，何须与朝菌蟪蛄，议论春秋？”
壮哉，壮哉！吾去矣。
en:
25th Day of the Ninth Month, Third Year of Kaiyun. Cloudy.
Today I went to court and had an audience with the emperor, where I presented my plan for driving back the enemy. As expected, it was not accepted. Worse still, General Guo was rebuked because of me. How bitter. How shameful.
At present, the only course left is to head north and visit Du Chongwei, in hopes of securing his support and using it as an alternative strategy to drive back the enemy. Yet I know well what sort of man Zhongwei is. I fear this journey will come to nothing, and am deeply troubled by it.
Before setting out, I was fortunate enough to be seen off by General Chai Rong. His words brought me sudden clarity, and I record them here to remind myself for the rest of my life.
General Chai said, "In former days, Emperor Taizong acted with ruthless resolve at Xuanwu Gate, and only then came the Reign of Zhenguan and a century of flourishing rule. A true man sets his sights high and sees a thousand li at a glance. Why should he waste words on creatures as short-lived as morning mushrooms and summer cicadas?"
What stirring words. What stirring words. Off I go.

zh: 惟王建国，实曰京师，度地居民，固有前则。东京华夷辐辏，水陆会通，时向隆平，日增繁盛，而都城因旧，制度未恢，诸卫军营，或多窄隘，百司公署，无处兴修。加以坊市之中，邸店有限，工商外至，亿兆无穷，僦赁之资，添增不定，贫阙之户，供办实艰。而又屋宇交连，街衢湫隘，入夏有暑湿之苦，居常多烟火之忧。将便公私，须广都邑。宜令所司於京城四面别筑罗城，先立标帜，候将来冬末春初，农务闲时，即量差近甸人夫，渐次修筑。春作才动，便令放散。如或土功未毕，则迤逦次年修筑，所冀宽容办集。今後凡有营葬，及兴置宅灶并草市，并须去标帜七里外。基标帜内，候官中擘画定街巷军营仓场诸司公廨院务了，百姓即任营造。
en: When the king founded the nation, he established the capital accordingly, surveying the land and settling the people as precedent dictated. In Kaifeng city, peoples from all corners gather, waterways and roads converged, trade flourished, and prosperity grew day by day. Yet the city, built atop old foundations, had not been fully restored. Military camps were cramped, and government offices had no room for proper construction. Within the wards and markets, lodging houses were few, while merchants and artisans from afar poured in without end. Rental prices soared unpredictably, and poor households struggled to provide. Moreover, houses stood wall to wall, streets were narrow and congested, in summer, the heat and humidity became oppressive, and the risk of fires remained sky-high. For the convenience of both public and private life, it is now necessary to expand the city. Officials shall be ordered to construct an outer wall encircling the four sides of the capital. Markers must first be established, during the idle season between late winter and early spring, laborers from nearby fields shall be drafted to carry out the work. Once spring planting begins, they shall be released. If construction is unfinished, it will carry over to the following year, allowing matters to proceed with flexibility. From now on, any burials, new residences, hearths, or marketplaces must be built beyond seven li from the designated markers. Within the markers, once the officials have planned and allocated streets, camps, warehouses, and administrative offices, the people may then freely proceed with construction.

——种子到底在哪里呀？
——种子长大了吗？
——种子长得好吗？
……
你写下回信：
#Y【种子长大了。】你们有没有好好学习？许久未见，得空了定来找你们玩。#E
寄出信件之后，你寻空来到墨城，接上期盼已久的孩子们，又一次坐上建好轨道的云槎，重回碧云水涛。
种子在金灿灿的稻田里，在漫天花雨的桃林中，在淙淙的流水里……种子长得很好很好。
en:
Since parting ways at Jadestream Valley, you have frequently received letters from the Three Junior Paragons of Mohist City.
"Great Wanderer, why haven't you come to play with us yet?"
"Great Wanderer! How's the Sky Shuttle in the mountains coming along? When can you take us for another ride?"
But above all, they pester about Master Raven's "seeds."
"Where on earth are the seeds?"
"Have the seeds grown up yet?"
"Are the seeds doing well?"
...
You sit down to write back:
#Y[The seeds have grown up.] Have you all been studying hard? It's been a while since we last met. I'll surely visit you when I have the time.#E
After sending the letter, you visit Mohist City. You pick up the long-awaiting children and board the Sky Shuttle once more, gliding along the completed tracks back to Jadestream Valley.
The seeds are in the golden rice paddies, amidst the falling petals of Peach Grove, and within the gurgling brooks... The seeds are growing very, very well.

One stroke, bold and sweeping, as if a dragon has descended; another flows like a trailing thread, sealing every vital point. Wielding the Skybound Sword, blade and fan resonate together in continuous strikes against the enemy. After the first three stages of the skill land, press again to unleash the next strike, for a total of four stages when used solo. In the first stage, the sword pursues a distant target, dealing $D$F0.1$E damage. In the second stage, the sword performs swift strikes at the target ahead, dealing $D$F0.1$E damage. The third stage consumes an additional 30 Vitality and allows the blade to be hurled forward, knocking down the enemy and dealing $D$F0.1$E damage. In the final stage, the blade is unsheathed, and its Sword Energy surges forth, dealing $D$F0.7$E damage to the enemy.
When outside of the Arena and in open, level terrain, releasing the first stage of this skill will send an invitation to other Wanderers nearby within the party who carry this same technique. If they respond, they will then draw the Earthbound Sword to aid the Skybound Sword in unsheathing, entering the #YSuper Armor#E state and releasing a Rapport Combo, dealing a total of $D$F1.4$E damage to the enemy. When releasing the Combo, the Skybound Sword and Earthbound Sword consume 30 and 50 Vitality respectively. Upon successful execution, the cooldown of this technique increases to 180 seconds for both Wanderers.

Brother Lin,

...I have labored over this casket with my own hands. Though I have had only my shadow for company, the little cat by my side has done something to ease the loneliness...
...The hardships of the body I have always taken lightly. Yet whenever I hear that an old friend has passed on, it seems to me that the colors and sounds of this world grow dimmer still, the melodies that once lingered beneath the rafters fading ever farther away, and the heaviness in my chest growing harder and harder to dispel. I still remember those who once composed new airs with me in years past. How many of them are left now...

zh:
小友，展信安
近来听门中弟子闲聊，说山下有位慷慨游侠，为了安顿流民而四处奔走。这般热心肠，我一听便知是小友。
不知你那边可还忙得过来？若需要帮忙，尽管告诉朴某。
早些年，我曾跟随师兄去过滹沱南岸，在那的营地见到不少流民……他们为了活命，吃虫子、吃树皮、吃观音土……饿殍满地，哀鸿遍野，那般情景，我至今想来仍觉心头发沉。
旁的或许帮不上，但生火做饭这类事，你大可交给我。这段时间，我翻古方、试新菜，手艺总算有了些进益，连晓晓那丫头都愿意乖乖吃饭了。若你人手短缺，我便带上炊具过去，能让人吃上踏实的热饭，是最要紧的。
en:
To my young friend,
I hope this letter finds you well.
Lately, I have heard the disciples chatting among themselves about a generous wanderer at the foot of the mountain, running here and there to help settle the displaced. The moment I heard of such kindness, I knew it had to be you.
I wonder whether you are still managing over there. If you need help, do not hesitate to ask.
Years ago, I followed my senior brother to the south bank of the Hutuo River. In the camp there, I saw many displaced people. To stay alive, they ate insects, tree bark, even Guanyin clay. The ground was strewn with the starved dead, and cries of misery filled the air. Even now, the memory still weighs heavily on my heart.
I may be of little use in other matters, but you can leave cooking to me. Lately, I have been studying old recipes and trying new dishes, and my skills have finally improved a little. Even Xiaoxiao is now willing to eat without protest. If you are short on hands, I will bring my cookware and come at once. The most important thing is making sure people can eat a proper hot meal.

zh: 在活动中消耗长鸣珠可购买「福气锦袋」，打开1个「福气锦袋」后会获得1个「福龟」或其他奖励。当获得「福龟」时，如触发「对碰」「三连」或「全清」，则可获得兑换积分「儿时欢」，并返还一定数量的「福气锦袋」。返还的「福气锦袋」即刻开启并不进入背包，「儿时欢」可在活动商店中兑换限定外观和丰富奖励。每个角色最多购买1200次「福气锦袋」（不包括返还规则获得的福袋）。九宫格棋盘初始会赠送8个完全不同的「福龟」。当「福气锦袋」获得道具奖励时，不再获得「福龟」。活动结束后，购买的「福气锦袋」将以16个兑换1个袅袅之音·绑进行系统回收，不足16个的「福气锦袋」将以1:10兑换为长鸣玉。活动结束后至兑换下架期间内，可参与兑换不可参与祈福，最终未消耗的「儿时欢」积分将以16:1自动回收为长鸣玉。
en:
During the event, spend Echo Beads to purchase [Lucky Bags]. Each [Lucky Bag] grants 1 [Lucky Turtle] or other rewards. When a [Lucky Turtle] triggers a Pair Match, Triple Line, or All Unique, you receive [Turtle Plushie] and refunded [Lucky Bags]. Refunded bags open immediately and do not go into your inventory. 
[Turtle Plushie] can be exchanged for rewards in the event shop. Each character can purchase up to 1,200 [Lucky Bags] (excluding refunded bags). The 3×3 board starts with 8 different [Lucky Turtles]. 
When a [Lucky Bag] grants an item reward, you will not receive a [Lucky Turtle]. After the event ends, every 16 [Lucky Bags] will convert into 1 Lingering Melody: Bind. Fewer than 16 bags convert to Echo Jade at 1:10. 
During the exchange period, you can exchange rewards but cannot pray. Unused [Turtle Plushie] converts to Echo Jade at 16:1 when the event ends.

【三】

孟轲敦素，史鱼秉直。
庶几中庸，劳谦谨敕。
聆音察理，鉴貌辨色。
贻厥嘉猷，勉其祗植。
省躬讥诫，宠增抗极。
殆辱近耻，林皋幸即。
两疏见机，解组谁逼。
索居闲处，沉默寂寥。
求古寻论，散虑逍遥。
欣奏累遣，戚谢欢招。
渠荷的历，园莽抽条。
枇杷晚翠，梧桐蚤凋。
陈根委翳，落叶飘摇。
游鹍独运，凌摩绛霄。
耽读玩市，寓目囊箱。
易輶攸畏，属耳垣墙。
具膳餐饭，适口充肠。
饱饫烹宰，饥厌糟糠。
亲戚故旧，老少异粮。
妾御绩纺，侍巾帷房。
纨扇圆洁，银烛炜煌。
昼眠夕寐，蓝笋象床。
弦歌酒宴，接杯举殇。
矫手顿足，悦豫且康。
嫡后嗣续，祭祀烝尝。
稽颡再拜，悚惧恐惶。
笺牒简要，顾答审详。
骸垢想浴，执热愿凉。
驴骡犊特，骇跃超骧。
诛斩贼盗，捕获叛亡。
布射僚丸，嵇琴阮箫。
恬笔伦纸，钧巧任钓。
释纷利俗，并皆佳妙。
毛施淑姿，工颦妍笑。
年矢每催，曦晖朗曜。
璇玑悬斡，晦魄环照。
指薪修祜，永绥吉劭。
矩步引领，俯仰廊庙。
束带矜庄，徘徊瞻眺。
孤陋寡闻，愚蒙等诮。
谓语助者，焉哉乎也。
en:
[III]

Meng Ke cultivated simplicity; Shi Yu upheld integrity.
Strive for the middle way, working hard with humility and care.
Listen to words to discern truth, observe expressions to read character.
Leave behind wise counsel, and strive to nurture virtue with reverence.
Reflect upon oneself against criticism; excessive favor breeds extreme peril.
Approaching disgrace draws near to shame; it is fortunate to retreat to forest and hill.
The two Shus recognized the moment and retired; who forced them to relinquish their seals?
Living apart in quiet solitude, silent and still.
Seeking the ancients and searching their words, I scatter my worries and wander free.
Joy comes as burdens are cast off; sorrow fades as delight is welcomed.
Lotus blossoms bright in the ditch, garden weeds sprout new shoots.
The loquat stays green through late autumn; the tung tree withers early.
Old roots lie decayed and withered, fallen leaves drift and flutter.
The great kun-bird soars alone, rising high into the crimson sky.
Absorbed in reading like browsing a market stall, his eyes wandered over satchels and cases.
Beware of careless words, for even walls have ears.
Prepare meals and dishes fit to satisfy the palate and fill the stomach.
When full, even fine meats seem plain; when hungry, even dregs taste sweet.
Among kin and old friends, the old and young are served different fare.
Concubines spin and weave, attending with towel and comb in the chamber.
Round silk fans, pure and clean; silver candles burning bright.
Sleeping by day and resting by night, on beds of blue bamboo and ivory frame.
Songs and strings accompany the wine feast, cups passed and toasts raised.
Hands wave and feet stomp in dance, joyful hearts filled with peace.
The rightful heir continues the line, offering sacrifices in season.
They bow their heads to the ground in reverence, trembling with awe and fear.
His letters and memos were concise and essential, and his replies and responses were thorough and precise.
When dusty, one longs to bathe; when hot, one wishes for cool relief.
Donkeys, mules, calves, and bulls leap and bound in startled motion.
They punish thieves and bandits, capturing rebels and fugitives.
Bu's archery, Liao's ball tricks, Ji's zither, and Ruan's flute.
Tian's brush, Lun's paper, Jun's craftsmanship, and Ren's fishing skill.
They resolved disputes and benefited society, each excelling in their own art.
Mao and Shi possessed graceful beauty, skilled in charming frowns and smiles.
The years fly swiftly onward, as the bright sun casts its radiant glow.
The armillary sphere turns on its axis, the moon's phases circling in light.
As fire passes from log to log, cultivate blessings; find lasting peace and auspicious joy.
Walk with measured steps and dignified bearing, moving through the halls of court.
Dress with sash cinched and solemn dignity, pacing thoughtfully while gazing afar.
Narrow in learning and shallow in knowledge, one deserves mockery from fools and wise alike.
As for particles: yan, zai, hu, and ye.

en:
At the General's Shrine, you have seen the lively arena where villagers cheered, and met the blind, bewildered elder. You remember sharing a knapsack with her here, yet you still owe her a pine nut candy...
Now, things have changed and people are gone; the wind sweeps the wilderness, the moonlight traces the doors, and the night at the shrine is hushed and solemn. The general bled to bring this peace, and now he's barred from ever tasting it. Entering the General's Shrine once more, you only wish...
#YLet the lost come home. Spring comes and goes; the wind from the wilderness once brought you news of old friends. How you wish he and she could come home, and not just in dreams.#E
You bow solemnly, just as Uncle Jiang asked of you many years ago. You witnessed that story unfold across Qinghe, and unknowingly became a part of it yourself. The general fighting to the death in blood-stained armor; this is loyalty. The warrior casting aside his name and riding north in disguise; this is righteousness. This loyalty and righteousness sweep across the wilderness like winds, waiting only for future generations to recount.

zh:
【商书·仲虺之诰】

汤归自夏，至于大坰，仲虺作诰。
仲虺之诰：成汤放桀于南巢，惟有惭德，曰：“予恐来世以台为口实”。
仲虺乃作诰，曰：“呜呼！惟天生民有欲，无主乃乱。惟天生聪明时乂，有夏昏德，民坠涂炭。天乃锡王勇智，表正万邦，缵禹旧服。兹率厥典，奉若天命。
“夏王有罪，矫诬上天，以布命于下，帝用不臧。式商受命，用爽厥师。简贤附势，寔繁有徒，肇我邦于有夏，若苗之有莠，若粟之有秕，小大战战，罔不惧于非辜。矧予之德，言足听闻。
“惟王不迩声色，不殖货利。德懋懋官，功懋懋赏。用人惟己，改过不吝。克宽克仁，彰信兆民。
“乃葛伯仇饷，初征自葛。东征西夷怨，南征北狄怨。曰：‘奚独后予？’攸徂之民。室家相庆，曰：‘徯予后，后来其苏。’民之戴商，厥惟旧哉。
“佑贤辅德，显忠遂良，兼弱攻昧，取乱侮亡，推亡固存，邦乃其昌。德日新，万邦惟怀，志自满，九族乃离。王懋昭大德，建中于民，以义制事，以礼制心，垂裕后昆。予闻曰：‘能自得师者王，谓人莫已若者亡。好问则裕，自用则小。’呜呼！慎厥终，惟其始。殖有礼，覆昏暴。钦崇天道，永保天命。
……
en:
【Book of Shang · The Announcement of Zhong Hui】

Tang returned from Xia and arrived at Da Jiong, where Zhong Hui made an announcement.
The Announcement of Zhong Hui: Cheng Tang banished Jie to Nanchao, yet felt ashamed, saying, "I fear that future generations will use me as a pretext."
Zhong Hui then made the announcement, saying: "Alas! Heaven gives birth to the people with desires; without a ruler, there is chaos. Heaven, being intelligent, thus brings order. The Xia ruler was benighted in virtue, and the people fell into mire and charcoal. Heaven then bestowed upon the King courage and wisdom, to correct and lead all states, continuing Yu's ancient service. Thus he follows their statutes, reverently obeying Heaven's mandate.
"The Xia King had transgressions, falsely claiming Heaven's authority to issue commands below, so Heaven did not favor him. He then used Shang to receive the mandate, thereby enlightening its multitudes. Those who flattered the worthy and clung to power were indeed numerous, but they arose against our state of Xia, like tares among seedlings, like chaff among grain. Small and great trembled, none but feared for the innocent. How much more so with my virtue, whose words are worthy of hearing.
"The King does not approach music or women, nor does he accumulate wealth or profit. The virtuous are promoted to office, the meritorious are amply rewarded. He employs others as himself, and corrects faults without hesitation. He is capable of leniency and benevolence, making his sincerity manifest to the myriad people.
"When the Earl of Ge treated food-offerers as enemies, the first expedition began at Ge. When he campaigned in the east, the western barbarians complained; when he campaigned in the south, the northern tribes complained, saying, 'Why does he leave us until last?' The people of the places he visited celebrated in their households, saying, 'We await our lord; when he comes, we shall revive.' The people's support for Shang has indeed been longstanding.
"Assist the worthy and support the virtuous, make manifest the loyal and advance the good. Absorb the weak, attack the benighted, seize the disordered, and overthrow the doomed. Push down the perishing and secure the surviving, and the state will prosper. When virtue is renewed daily, all states cherish it; when the will becomes self-satisfied, even the nine clans will be estranged. The King should vigorously display great virtue, establishing the Mean among the people, governing affairs with righteousness and the heart with propriety, leaving a rich legacy to posterity. I have heard: 'He who can find teachers for himself becomes king; he who thinks none are his equal perishes. Being fond of inquiry leads to abundance; relying on oneself leads to narrowness.' Alas! To ensure a proper end, one must consider the beginning. Establish what is proper, and overthrow the dark and violent. Reverently honor the way of Heaven, and eternally preserve Heaven's mandate.
……

“霹雳”不是它的名字，也不止一个玄卫叫过“霹雳”，可它偏偏喜欢这两个字。每当听见呼唤，它便如雷霆乍惊，快如疾风。
还是小狗崽时，霹雳就懂得了自己的使命：巡逻，然后守卫这道宫墙。在它眼里，宫墙很高，天地很宽，墙里的人都需要它来保护。它喜欢从御道的这头跑到那头，熟悉的气味能让它心安。
但最近，宫里多了一道陌生的气息。霹雳不认识那人，却嗅得出那人身上有和自己一样的味道——那是风尘、铁锈，和守护某人的决心。它知道，只要心里有想要守护的人，太阳总会照常升起。
en:
"Bolt" isn't really its name, and it isn't the only guard dog to be called that. Still, it just loves this word.

Whenever it hears the call, it startles like sudden thunder and bolts like the wind. Even as a pup, it seemed to understand its duty. Patrol, and then stand watch over these palace walls.

To it, the walls are high and the world is wide, and everyone inside needs protecting. It loves sprinting from one end of the palace road to the other. Familiar scents are enough to set its heart at ease.

But lately, a strange scent has appeared within the palace. It doesn't know the person, yet it can smell something familiar on them. Dust and iron rust, and the resolve to protect someone.

It knows this much. As long as there is someone it wants to protect, the sun will rise as it always does.

由是长街人影婓婓，机关奇巧频出其间，而叫卖议价之声终日不绝。虽至深宵，恍若新昼。

en:
When the sun dips below the horizon and twilight descends, the lights at the foot of the mountain flicker to life one by one, and the market begins to hum.
Artisans set aside their tools, scholars lay down their brushes, and some trade their newly crafted devices. Others, without a care for commerce, gather in small circles to share and marvel over the latest mechanical wonders.
Along the winding streets, shadows dance, ingenious creations emerge at every corner, and the lively calls of vendors haggling fill the air from dawn until well into the night. Even in the depths of midnight, the city feels bright and vibrant, almost as if daylight never faded.
In these stolen moments of leisure amid the bustle, scholars exchange their ideas freely. Perhaps this, more than skill alone, is the true wisdom at the heart of their craft.
