en:
Deep within Mohist City, beneath the Divinecraft Pavilion, lies a hidden place. It is said that the Mohist sages once studied the heavens here, seeking the greater laws behind all things and deriving from them the countless transformations of mechanism.
Any who aspired to become Grandmaster would enter this place and brave its maze. By witnessing its ever-changing workings, they came to understand the boundless depth of the Mohist Way.
At the heart of the maze lies a hidden core below the earth, answering to the heavens above and the balance of yin and yang below. Only those of exceptional insight and unshakable resolve can hope to grasp even a trace of its mysteries.
Later, when calls to seal the mountain grew strong, a Grandmaster used this maze to lock away the martial teachings, mechanisms, and weapons of Mohism, to remain hidden until the proper time.
And so this secret place fell silent, waiting for the one who would come next.

zh:
璎璎，禁中宫人也，性沉毅，怀侠气。一夜巡更，忽闻瓦动，刹时一黑衣客坠于阶前，气若游丝。璎璎匿之冷宫，及醒，方知其为当世豪侠，为取神剑，涉险入禁。
（被划掉的部分）
璎敛容拜曰：“与其老死宫墙，化为尘泥，不若离宫，一览乾坤。汝若念恩，愿带妾出此樊笼，从此海阔天高，死亦无憾。”
侠客既允，遂于夜半偕行，共出宫闱。行至一门，门外上锁。侠客提气纵身，飘然越之，复为启其门扉。门方开，殿前禁军忽至。侠客以身为盾，于乱军中辟血路而出。然追兵复至，侠客掠阵，一击毙敌，其势不可当。
前路为高墙所阻。侠客乃屈身，以肩为梯，助璎逾之。璎落地，伤足，步履维艰。侠客未发一言，俯身负之而行。俄而，身后羽箭如蝗，破风声不绝。二人竟于万矢丛中，攀垣直上，竟登城头。
月色如水，二人终出樊笼，自此……天高海阔。
（又被划掉的部分）
侠客以身为盾……终寡不敌众，为武德司所擒。璎璎誓救侠客，决心潜行相救。时值禁卫巡守，璎璎匿迹潜踪，却闻侠客囚于天牢。初避一人，复又遇之，遂藏身木桶，混迹而行。
至后苑，闻诸娘子私语。风啸难辨，璎璎惟臆测其言，乃知天牢所在。方欲往救，忽现怨魂！逃之，未果。走避不得，遂执青葱驱之。
此举竟于无意间解一娘子之困，娘子感其恩，指以明路。然前路守备愈严，璎不得已，匿于车舆。轮毂飞转，撞翻戍卒。及至倾覆，坠入幽井，适为天牢暗道。
璎璎于黑暗中前行，历尽艰险，终抵天牢。见重兵环伺，乃拾弓矢，引爆火药，克一军士。复观其上，有机关，遂发之。囹圄既开，侠客终得出。二人合力，以弩车断后，追兵莫能近。
行见神剑之地，寒光凛然，正是侠客此行所求。璎璎拔之……乃得铁锹一柄。二人相视，愕然，亦莞尔。遂持此锹，于宫墙之下，辟地道而出……终归江湖。
（字迹清晰的部分，似乎是刚写就的）
璎璎执此锹，侠客紧随其后。深宫似海，欲寻生天，须过三道天堑，正是武德司闻风丧胆的四大高手。
第一关便是饕餮，此人身形魁梧，食可吞山。然璎璎知其癖，虽嗜桂花糕，食之必腹泻，亦甘之如饴。乃以糕饵之，饕餮见之，果露憨色，喃喃曰：“吾知汝心……”食毕，腹中翻江倒海，寻净房而去。此关遂破。
第二关乃天罗、地网二人，一人擅刀，一人擅扇，合则天下无敌。然璎璎知此二人每至戊时三刻，便要寻僻静处私会。果不其然，时辰一到，二人便斗起蛐蛐了。璎璎趁机潜行，安然过之。
最后一关，正是无名，传闻此人眼观六路，耳听八方。正屏息间，一犬摇尾而至，乃璎璎素日所饲。无名见之，竟一改冷峻，俯身软语道：“小汪汪！你来得正好，人家一个人站岗好~害~怕~”原来硬骨亦存柔情！
凭此，二人终出樊笼，立于宫墙之外。
侠问何以报，璎请授剑。侠曰：“汝年岁既长，根骨已定。习武如逆水行舟，恐难甚至。”
璎再拜，曰：“精卫衔微木，将以填沧海。一岁不成，则期十载。此生不成，亦无悔也。”
言罢，庭柏飒飒，似作金戈鸣。侠壮其志，拊掌称善，遂传衣钵。 
自此，天高海阔，任其驰骋。侠客望其背影，百感交集，然璎璎未发一言，径自转身，向江湖中走去。
……
江湖所称“侠女璎璎”，盖始于此。
en:
Yingying was a palace maid within the inner precincts. Quietly resolute by nature, she had a streak of gallantry in her as well.

One night, while making her rounds on watch duty, she heard tiles shifting overhead. In the next instant, a black-clad figure tumbled down before the steps, barely clinging to life. Yingying hid this intruder away in the Forlorn Palace, who
turned out to be a famed grandmaster of the age and had risked entering the palace in search of a divine sword.

(A section here has been crossed out.)

Lowering her gaze, Yingying bowed and said, "I would rather leave the palace and see the world than grow old behind these walls and turn to dust. If you mean to repay me, take me out of this cage. Once I am free, with sea and sky wide before me, I could die without regret."

The grandmaster agreed, and so the two slipped out together at midnight, leaving the palace behind.

When they reached a gate, they found it locked from the outside. The grandmaster drew a breath, sprang upward, and floated lightly over it, then turned to open the gate for her. But the moment the gate opened, the Imperial Guards before the hall rushed in. The grandmaster shielded Yingying with their own body and carved a bloody path through the chaos. Yet more pursuers arrived. Holding the rear, they struck down their foes one by one, unstoppable in force.

Ahead of them rose a high wall. The grandmaster bent low and offered their shoulder as a step so Yingying could climb over. When she landed, she hurt her foot and could barely walk. Without a word, the grandmaster stooped and carried her on their back. A moment later, arrows hissed behind them like a swarm of locusts, their sound ripping through the air without end. And yet, amid that storm of shafts, the two somehow scaled the wall itself and gained the top.

The moonlight lay like water. At last they escaped the cage, and from then on, sky and sea lay open before them.

(Another section here has been crossed out.)

The grandmaster used their body as a shield... yet in the end they were outnumbered and taken by the Imperial Service. Yingying swore she would save the grandmaster, and resolved to slip away in secret to do so. Just then the palace guards were making their rounds. Yingying concealed herself and crept along in hiding, only to hear that the grandmaster was imprisoned in the Dungeon. After avoiding one person only to run into another, she hid inside a wooden barrel and slipped along unnoticed.

When she reached the Rear Garden, she overheard some ladies whispering among themselves. The wind howled too fiercely to make out their words, so Yingying could only guess at what they said, but from this she learned the location of the Imperial Prison. Just as she was about to go to the rescue, a vengeful spirit suddenly appeared. She tried to flee, but could not. With no way to avoid it, she seized a handful of onions and drove it off.

By chance, this act freed one of the ladies from danger. Grateful for the favor, the lady pointed Yingying toward the right path. But the road ahead was under even tighter guard, and Yingying had no choice but to hide inside a carriage. The wheels spun wildly and knocked over the soldiers on watch. When the carriage overturned, she fell into a dark well, which just so happened to be the secret passage to the Imperial Prison.

In darkness, Yingying pressed onward. After countless perils, she finally reached the Imperial Prison. Seeing heavy guards all around, she picked up a bow and arrows, ignited the gunpowder, and brought down one of the soldiers. Then she spotted a mechanism above and triggered it. Once the cells were opened, the grandmaster was finally freed. Together the two fought their way out, using a ballista to cover their retreat so that none of the pursuers could come near.

On their way they came upon the place where the sacred sword was said to rest, its cold gleam sharp and awe-inspiring. It was exactly what the grandmaster had entered the palace to seek. Yingying drew it forth... and found instead an iron shovel. The two stared at one another in shock, then both laughed. So they took up the shovel, dug a tunnel beneath the palace wall, and escaped at last, returning to the jianghu.

(The following section is written in a clear hand, and seems to have been added only recently.)

Yingying gripped the shovel while the grandmaster followed close behind. The deep palace was like a boundless sea, and to find a path to freedom they first had to cross three great obstacles, namely the Four Masters of the Imperial Service.

The first one was The Hungering, a huge and powerfully built man who could devour mountains with his appetite. But Yingying knew his weakness. Though he doted on osmanthus cakes, they always sent him running to the privy. Still, he loved them all the same. So she used cakes as bait. Sure enough, the moment The Hungering saw them, his face softened foolishly and he murmured, "I knew you understood me..." After eating, his stomach churned like an overturned river and sea, and he fled in search of a latrine. Thus the first obstacle was broken.

The second obstacle was Net of Heaven and Web of Earth. One excelled with the blade, the other with the fan. Together, they were said to be unmatched under heaven. But Yingying knew that every day at the third quarter of the Hour of Xu, the two would seek out some secluded place for a private meeting. And sure enough, once the time came, the two of them started fighting crickets instead. Yingying slipped past them and crossed safely through.

The final obstacle was The Nameless One, said to be a man who saw in all directions and heard every sound under heaven. Just as Yingying held her breath, a dog came trotting over with its tail wagging. It was one she herself had long fed. At the sight of it, The Nameless One at once lost all his cold severity, crouched down, and cooed softly, "Little puppy, you came at just the right time. Standing guard here all alone is so very, very scary." So even the hardest bones may hide a tender heart.

And so, the two at last escaped the cage and stood beyond the palace walls.

The grandmaster asked how they might repay her. Yingying asked them to teach her the sword. The grandmaster said, "You are already grown, and your frame has long since set. To train in the martial way is like rowing against the current. I fear you may never reach its heights."

Yingying bowed again and said, "Like Jingwei carrying twigs to fill the sea, so shall I. If one year is not enough, I shall give ten. If even this life is not enough, I shall have no regrets."

As her words fell, the cypresses in the courtyard rustled, as though ringing with the clash of arms. The grandmaster was stirred by her resolve. They clapped in praise and agreed to pass on their art.

From then on, sky and sea lay open before her, free for her to cross at will.

The grandmaster watched her departing figure with a thousand feelings in their heart. Yet Yingying said nothing. She merely turned and walked on alone into the jianghu.

Thus began the tale of how the jianghu came to know her as heroine Yingying.

如果一个人的生可以支撑人的前半生，那一个人的死也足以支撑人的后半生，他的一生都困在了另一个人生死的瞬间，不、有些人甘愿被一个瞬间困住一生。
人的一生是一条漫漫的长路。
可对有些人来说，那些泥泞和鲜血中的道路本没有行走的意义，这条道路存在的本身，只是为了接住相逢时的那一场大雨。
他的道路至此干涸一片。
他不再需要任何人的记得。
en:
But the next time he saw General Wang Qing... The general was dead.
Wang Qing was dead.
This was the moment he'd spent years longing for, dreaming restlessly of, waiting for his next meeting with the general.
On Zhongdu Bridge, the general still wore his armor, just as he had the very first time they met.
Except now, there was a sword driven through his heart.
His eyes numbly traced the path from the sword's hilt to the hand holding it, then fixed on Jiang Yan's hand, and finally, Jiang Yan's face.
He didn't understand. Hadn't Jiang Yan already had enough? He'd already gotten the general's special attention, his smiles, his scoldings, and his time. Why did he have to take the only thing He Ran had, Wang Qing's very existence, and any hope of seeing him again?
If someone's life can sustain you through the first half of your own, then their death can carry you through the rest. In that moment, his whole life became trapped in someone else's death. And maybe, some people are willing to stay trapped in that moment forever.
Life is a long, winding road.
Yet for some, the blood and mud along the way mean nothing. The only purpose of that road was to bring you to the moment you meet someone in the pouring rain.
Now, his path had dried up, empty.
He no longer needed to be remembered by anyone.

河豚俗称“气泡鱼”，生活在河流淡水中。河豚身体钝圆，至尾部渐细。从秦汉时起，就有河豚“食之杀人”的记载。然而河豚味美，肉质洁白滑嫩，堪称鱼中极品，文人雅士对其赞不绝口，甘冒“性命之危”也要吃河豚。河豚在二月初最肥，三月后毒性渐增，故初春河豚初上之时，是吃河豚的最佳时节。
en:
When wild artemisia blankets the fields and tender reeds first sprout, the pufferfish begins its upstream journey. 

Nicknamed the "bubble fish," the river pufferfish lives in freshwater. With its rounded body tapering to a narrow tail, it has long held a dangerous allure. As early as the Qin and Han dynasties, it was said: "To eat it is to risk death." Yet its soft, snow-white flesh is considered a supreme delicacy. So much so that scholars and nobles have praised it across the centuries, willingly gambling with fate for a single taste. Fattest in early February and grow more toxic after March, it is best enjoyed in the brief window of early spring.

en:
Cen Shen (Tang Dynasty)
The north wind rolls the earth and breaks the grass; in August, snow flies o'er the Tartar pass.
As if a spring breeze comes overnight, and pear blossoms bloom in thousands white.
They enter silken curtains damp and cold; fur coats can't warm, thin quilts grow old.
The general's horn bow cannot be drawn; the governor's iron armor's hard to put on.
A hundred fathoms ice on desert wide; sad clouds dimly stretch for miles and hide.
In camp we wine our guest to say goodbye; with pipa, erhu, and flute we try.
At dusk snow falls thick round the camp gate; the red flag stiff with cold won't undulate.
At Luntai east gate I see you go, the road to Tianshan is all snow.
The mountain turns, you disappear from sight; on snow your horses' hoofprints still are bright.

师父御前对答之事轰动天下，恐怕慈心山院之地位将今非昔比，难道师父真是佛陀……（后面的文字被新写的杂乱文字盖住了，只能隐约看出一些新写的词语，大概是“勾结”、“串通”之类的。）

建隆元年 二月
师父离寺之后，音讯全无，恐遭不测。明日起，我将亲离山院，寻找师父。

建隆元年 三月
妙善此人，自始至终，皆是骗局。什么佛法圣僧，不过是钓名欺世的骗子！若非今日得获此旧信，恐怕我将一生蒙于歹人谎言之中。田英以佛言误我，使我为伥多年，半生尽毁，有生之年，我必报之！
如今思及十数年来那伪僧所传之佛法，只觉恶心。十二因缘，尽是虚妄，三界六道，都是鬼话！自今日始，凡佛颂者，我必反之，凡佛恶者，我必好之。泥塑造像，岂可骑在活人的头上？什么菩萨如来，我也做得！

建隆元年 四月
时至今日，竟仍有人满口阿弥陀佛，笃信田英，不知悔改，恶心至极！所幸慧勇等人本就出身山匪，早看不惯田英一党的做派，与我联手，将那些蠢猪一同打了出去。如今这慈心山院再无一点佛家晦气，实在是清净多了！
en:
Third Month, First Year of the Xiande Era
Abstain from all evil, practice all good, and purify the mind. This is the teaching of the Buddhas. Master Miaoshan... (The remaining text has been torn away.)

Fourth Month, First Year of the Xiande Era
Today, during Master's sermon at the Thousand Buddha Pagoda, divine radiance truly descended upon us... (The rest is smudged beyond legibility, with a furious scribble added below: "Sorcery and deception, utterly vile!")

Sixth Month, Second Year of the Xiande Era
"The Master's audience before the Emperor has shaken the realm. The status of Mercyheart Monastery will never be the same. Could he truly be... a Buddha? (The following lines are aggressively overwritten with fresh ink—only broken phrases like "collusion" and "scheming" can be discerned.)

Second Month, First Year of the Jianlong Era
Since the Master left the monastery, not a word has been heard. I fear the worst. Tomorrow, I shall depart to seek him.

Third Month, First Year of the Jianlong Era
Miaoshan—from start to finish, it was all a lie. "Holy monk of the Dharma?" A fraud, bloated on stolen reverence! Had I not uncovered these old letters, I might have died shackled to his deceit. Tian Ying ensnared me with Buddhist platitudes, turning me into his accomplice for years. My life, half-wasted! I will have vengeance.
Now, recalling the "Dharma" that charlatan preached for over a decade, I feel only revulsion. The Twelve Nidānas? Fabrications. The Three Realms and Six Paths? Delusions! From this day forth: All that sings Buddha's praise I defy. All that Buddha abhors I will glorify. Why should clay idols lord over the living? If he could pose as a Bodhisattva... why not I?

Fourth Month, First Year of the Jianlong Era
Even now, fools chant Amitabha and cling to Tian Ying's lies. Disgusting! Fortunately, Huiyong and his bandit-born brethren long despised Tian's faction. Together, we drove those swine out. Now, not a whiff of Buddhism taints Mercyheart Monastery. At last... peace!

当他们登顶时，雕佛村中忽起大火，全村陷入火海之中。禅师在山顶为众人讲经，世人拜服。日出之时，禅师讲经完毕，佛光现世。此即佛光顶的名字来源。
en:
One night, a Chan Master cried out beyond Buddha-Sculpting Village, denouncing the villagers' body mutilation as hypocrisy and false Buddhism. "Let those who repent follow me," he called. Some cursed the master, but he turned a deaf ear. Those willing to follow trekked with him to the peak of Nameless Mountain. 
As they reached the summit, Buddha-Sculpting Village erupted in flames, engulfed in a sea of fire. The Chan Master preached the scriptures on the peak, and all who heard were awed. At sunrise, when his sermon ended, a Buddhalight manifested—thus giving Halo Peak its name.

zh:
坤幺儿是个好人。得过坤幺儿恩情的人，都这么说。
坤幺儿也是个怪人。得过坤幺儿恩情的人，也从不否认这一点。
坤幺儿属实是个又好又怪的人。但坤幺儿也不是生来就这样的。

他从前是个流落各地的小乞丐。个头只有常人一半大小，又没什么本事，谁来了，看他不顺眼了，都能踹他一脚。他也没什么脾气，从不反抗。这么风里爬雨里滚的，也不知怎么的，硬是让他活下来了，而且还叫他摸索出了一些活下来的好法子。
比如，能叫人浑身发痒的药粉呀，能唬人一跳的爆竹呀……这些别人瞧不上眼的小玩意儿，于他而言都是生路。

但也有的时候，这些生路也不是那么好走。
倪老山头一回见着他的时候，他就受了好重的伤，血与雨水交织，他蜷缩在竹篮里，像是个阴沟里的小老鼠。
倪老山把这只小老鼠带回了地下的鬼市子。在那里，老鼠也能得到一方庇护。

坤幺儿从此便在鬼市子住了下来。
他曾淋过大雨，便总是心怀怜悯。他做了好多古怪的小玩意，还向大家传授活下去的法子。于是旁人说他是个好人。
但风雨之大，伤他太深。所以他总是嬉笑着捉弄他人，遮掩着敛起自己的真心。于是旁人说他是个怪人。

坤幺儿又好又怪，是因为这让人无可奈何的生活啊。
en:
Kun the Youngest was a good man. Everyone who had ever received his kindness said so.
Kun the Youngest was also a strange man. And none who had known his kindness would deny that either.
Indeed, Kun the Youngest was both good and strange, but he hadn't been born that way.

Once, he had been a little beggar wandering the land, barely half the size of a grown man and with no skills to speak of. Anyone who took a dislike to him could kick him aside, and he never fought back. Against all odds, he survived, wind-battered, rain-drenched, and along the way, he learned a few tricks to keep himself alive.
For example, powders that made a man itch uncontrollably. Firecrackers that startled pursuers into stumbling. Trinkets others scoffed at, but for him, they were lifelines.

Yet even lifelines sometimes frayed.
When Ni Laoshan first found him, the boy was grievously wounded, blood mingling with rainwater as he curled inside a bamboo basket like a sewer rat.
So Ni Laoshan carried this little rat back to the underground Ghostlight Market, where even vermin could find shelter.

There, Kun the Youngest made his home.
Having known the drenching cold of rain, he always carried compassion. He crafted quirky gadgets and taught others to survive, earning his reputation as "good". 
But the storms of his past ran deep. He hid his true heart behind pranks and laughter, earning the label "strange".

Kun the Youngest was good and strange, because life had left him no other choice.

说是，有位俗家女子，自称屁尼。所到之处，但凡有屁出现，她都宣称此屁是她所放，闻者收银十两。
说是，污言秽语不得人心，银钱自然所获寥寥。但竟真有人给她十两，她不吃不喝，拿着这银钱，买下一只猫。
猫名屁屁。
说是，难登大雅之堂者，养难登小雅之堂猫。一日，高僧路过，降魔成道，猫被点化后，竟也觉着羞赧，连夜咬着主人的破烂僧袍，将其拉至尼寺旁修身养性。
至于这位俗家女子是否当真皈依佛祖，暂不可考。
en:
There once was a woman who called herself Poony. Wherever she went, if a fart was heard, she'd claim it as hers—demanding ten taels of silver from anyone who caught the scent. 
Naturally, such crassness earned her few coins, but one day, someone actually paid her ten taels. She didn't spend it on food or drink; instead, she bought herself a cat. 
That cat's name was Poop. 
One day, a revered monk passed by. Touched by his presence, Poop felt a flush of shame, and that very night bit through its owner's worn monk's robe to drag it to a nearby nunnery for reflection. 
Whether the woman truly embraced the path of Buddha remains a mystery.

zh:
八王为乱，流民遍野。时巨子鹉，开山门一线，暗遣弟子出存粮以济山外百姓。
       然粮实不足。非匠作农人不倾力，实只此一山之地，何济于天下？只得令更拓耕地，望增粮，复救一二人，亦善矣。
       鹉亦暗自出山，见中原大地，以薪火葬亡人，如此方稍余资费以奉生者。乃记于手札：火葬可省资财，节耕地，利天下万民，该当推行。山中易俗，当自吾始。
       巨子妻鹦，出山医疟而自染疾。曾阅巨子手札，弥留际留遗言于鹉：“火葬推行之难，常不在死者而在生。巨子若行此礼，当自至亲始。如此，吾之死亦得利百姓。从生至死皆利天下，此非墨者之至愿耶？可喜之至矣。”
       巨子乃以火葬之礼，置妻之骨灰于旧城。又五年，鹉逝，同行火葬，骨灰归置旧城。
       时有门人言，墨子亦以为火葬之礼薄则薄矣，然至于甚。而今之巨子与妻鹦，以其利天下为之，略不以为薄。孰谓今人必不逮古人乎？
       此后，墨门皆行火葬而不疑，山中百姓亦从而效之。
en:
During the chaos of the Eight Princes' Rebellion, refugees were everywhere. Grandmaster Wu secretly opened a mountain gate to send stored grain to those outside, but supplies were scarce. Despite the farmers' efforts, one mountain's yield couldn't feed all. So Wu ordered more land cleared, hoping even a small extra harvest could save lives.
Wu once saw people in the Central Plains practice cremation, saving money and farmland for the living. He noted that cremation benefits all and should be promoted. Changing customs in the mountains had to start with him.
Wu's wife, Ying, fell ill while treating others outside the mountain. Near death, she urged Wu to start cremation with his own kin. So Wu cremated Ying and placed her ashes in the Old Mohist City. Five years later, he did the same. Though Mozi once saw cremation as modest but acceptable, Wu embraced it fully for the greater good. Who says today's people are any less than the old?
From then on, Moists accepted cremation, and mountain villagers followed suit.
Ming Ye Cang

zh:
善财是只橘猫，毛色像晒透的稻谷。
乐安浦家家户户的堂屋里，都供着一尊海神娘娘小像。
善财就趴在小像旁边，摇摇尾巴，眯缝着眼，看村民们来来往往。
每天清晨，钱婆婆会点一炷香，再恭敬地拜一拜。
善财仰起脸，喵了一声，婆婆便笑着给它一条小鱼干，这似乎已经成为惯例了。
善财渐渐明白……这些人，都是自己的信众！
它心安理得地享用着每日的“供奉”，吃饱了就挪到院子里，让太阳把自己晒得暖烘烘的。
偶尔有不懂事的孩子，指着小像叫海神娘娘，善财便竖起耳朵，心里想着——
“这孩子，连自己的娘娘都不认得了。”
它不知道那尊小像刻的是谁，也没人告诉它，但没关系，每天的小鱼干是真的，叩拜也是真的。
村民们弯腰叩首时念叨的“娘娘保佑”，在善财听来，就是“善财保佑”。
海神娘娘安安静静地立在香炉后，眉眼低垂，从不说话。
也许她早就默许了这只小猫，当自己在人间的使者。
en:
Gold Fur is an orange cat, its coat the color of thoroughly sun-dried paddy. In the village of Tranquil Pier, every household enshrines a small statue of the Sea Goddess in their main hall.

Gold Fur likes to sprawl next to the little statue, wagging its tail and squinting its eyes, watching the villagers come and go. Every morning, Granny Qian lights a stick of incense and bows respectfully. Gold Fur tilts its head up and lets out a meow, and the old woman smilingly offers it a small dried fish. This seems to have become a daily routine.

Gold Fur gradually came to understand. All these people were its worshippers!

It enjoys its daily "offerings" with complete peace of mind. Once its belly is full, it moves to the courtyard to let the sun warm it through. Occasionally, an ignorant child might point at the small statue and call out to the Sea Goddess. Gold Fur would prick up its ears, thinking to itself, "This child does not even recognize their own Goddess."

It does not know who the small statue represents, and no one has ever told it, but that does not matter. The daily dried fish is real, and the kowtows are real. When the villagers bow and murmur, "Goddess, please bless us," it sounds to Gold Fur exactly like, "Gold Fur, please bless us."

The Sea Goddess stands quietly behind the incense burner, her eyes lowered, never uttering a word. Perhaps she had long since given silent consent for this little cat to act as her envoy in the mortal realm.

Accept my deepest gratitude to you for finding this scroll. In the hurried secrecy of sketching a covert map of the imperial palace these past days, I must have carelessly dropped it. This scroll records court secrets of the highest order; should the authorities lay hands upon it, my life would be forfeit. 
Since you have already peeled back the gold leaf, it must surely be the will of Heaven. The treasure hidden within the scroll is yours to keep. I have also prepared a modest additional gift, and I do hope you will deign to accept it 
For now, I must steal back into the palace to finish the map. If I manage to escape with my hide intact, then next we meet upon the rivers and lakes, the wine is on me!

Unlike other places buried entirely by the sands, Horsehelm Village was fortunate enough to be remembered, yet cursed to lose every last one of its people. The Karez Wells, dug by hand with lives as their price, lie buried beneath stone and sand. Only a few broken wellheads remain, silently mourning the endless dunes. 
Ages have passed, and from afar, the ruins shimmer with what seems like flowing springs—a desert mirage or forgotten truth? Step closer, and you may find the answer.

选手须遵守《燕云十六声》通用赛事规则，详见燕云十六声赛事中心官网【通用赛事规则】一栏。

本届「争鸣赛」参赛限制装备最高为86阶，参与比赛的游侠务必保留好86阶【装备】，在比赛中选手的部分战斗属性进行调平（角色和武学等级为90级，心法为6重，奇术为5重9段，装备叠音最高生效四十五重，解锁当前赛季所有通用型止戈天赋），战斗规则沿用天下争鸣玩法规则。

海选赛开放时间内报名参赛的战队需要自行前往争鸣赛海选界面参与匹配，完成10场海选比赛，成绩审核期24h，次日16:30审核结束，排名前32名的战队进入下一阶段比赛。

小组赛比赛开始前15分钟参赛战队可组队并由队长进入准备场景（需确保5人皆为战队成员），海选晋级战队分为4个小组进行单循环积分赛，采用三局两胜制。
【1】匹配机制：系统将于14:00开始自动为各战队匹配未对阵过的对手，奇数战队数量的小组首领会出现轮空寻找对手较长的情况。
【2】匹配流程：每次返回准备场景后，系统会持续进行新一轮匹配，由于仅匹配未交战的对手，可能出现等待时间较长的情况，请耐心等待。
【3】单循环赛制：需与小组内所有战队完成一轮对阵，小组赛将在所有战队完成相互对阵后结束。
7月8日22点审核时间结束，各小组第一名晋级八强胜者组、第二名晋级八强败者组，奖励在审核期结束后领取。

战队排名依据（按优先级）：胜场总数 > 胜场平均存活人数 > 胜场平均用时（计算平均值时，仅计入非轮空的有效胜场数据）。
en:
Players must abide by the Where Winds Meet General Tournament Rules. See the [General Tournament Rules] section on the official Where Winds Meet Tournament Center website. 

The max Gear Tier for this "Contention Tournament" is Tier 86. Wanderers must keep their Tier 86 [Gear]. Combat attributes will be balanced during the match (Character and Martial Arts Level 90, Inner Ways Tier 6, Mystic Skill Tier 5 Rank 9, Gear Enhancement max 45 stacks, all current season general Arena Talents unlocked). Combat rules follow the 5v5 Arena rules. 

Teams registered during the Qualifiers period must proceed to the Contention Tournament Qualifiers interface to match. Complete 10 qualifying matches. Result review period is 24h, ending the next day at 16:30. The top 32 teams advance to the next stage. 

Participating teams can form a team and enter the preparation scene via the leader 15 minutes before the Group Stage match starts (ensure all 5 members are in the team). Qualifying teams are divided into 4 groups for a Single Round Robin tournament, using a Best of 3 format. 
[1] Matchmaking: The system will automatically match teams against opponents they haven't fought yet starting at 14:00. Groups with an odd number of teams may experience longer wait times due to byes. 
[2] Process: After returning to the preparation scene, the system will continue to match for the next round. Wait times may be longer as it only matches opponents not yet fought. Please wait patiently. 
[3] Round Robin: Teams must complete a match against every other team in the group. The Group Stage ends when all teams have fought each other. 
The review period ends on July 8 at 22:00. The 1st place of each group advances to the Top 8 Winners Bracket, and the 2nd place advances to the Top 8 Losers Bracket. Rewards are claimed after the review period. 

Team Ranking Criteria (Priority): Total Wins > Avg. Survivors in Wins > Avg. Time in Wins (Calculated using only valid winning matches, excluding byes).

en:
A crude short sword with a simple retractable design.
After Crane brought Halcyon and Raven back to the mountain, he left again, putting them under Zhang Wanshi's tutelage.
Halcyon, playful as a child, threw together this sword and turned it in as an assignment. Raven took one look and worried their senior brother would be furious. With the deadline on them, he hurriedly added a small needle launcher inside the blade.
When Zhang Wanshi reviewed it later, he said that for their age, a bit of childish whimsy was only fitting. Halcyon and Raven were mortified, and from then on, none of their work ever earned that kind of "whimsy" again.
Zhang Wanshi quietly kept this one-of-a-kind piece.

zh:
林小鱼自幼畏水。她总觉得，大海那沉碧色的波涛之下有好多尸体，有好多的鬼。
年年月月，沿海的渔户们总要往海里放水祭坛。她就坐在岸边，直勾勾地盯着那些小灯烛在水波里摇晃。祭坛的烛火映照之下，人们的脸像浮尸的面孔般折射令人惊悸的光，影影绰绰的，似在喧嚷，又似在哭。林小鱼疑心溺毙者的魂灵就在水面下熙攘。
林小鱼想，不如养羊。每天牵着羊群吃草，剪了羊毛纺线，挤了羊奶带去大集上卖，不愁吃穿，还比出海稳当。
可爹娘说，她生来是属于水的，眉眼像极了家家户户供奉的海神娘娘。他们往她的眉心点上一点红痣，乍看和神像一模一样。
林小鱼不想做海神娘娘，但做海神娘娘还是有好处的。每当那些半大孩子把她扎的小彩船弄得七零八落，她只需往高处一站，把脸一板，冷生生丢下一句：“海神娘娘不喜欢你了！”那群顽童便作鸟兽散。

林小鱼真正拥有自己羊群的那年，镇上来了商队，要招募舵手远航。
那些客商带走了她的爹娘，也带走了村里许多孩子的爹娘。此后好久好久，久到岸边的礁石又被削去一层棱角，依旧不见舟船归航。村子里的哭声此起彼伏，像海潮一样。
林小鱼没哭。她躲进屋里，扎了好多好多的小彩船，在岸边一个一个发给孩子们。她学着海神娘娘的腔调，郑重地对他们说：“阿爹阿娘阿爷阿奶都会回来！”
但她终究不是海神娘娘，庇佑不了远航的船。那年谁也没有回来，包括她的爹娘。
水祭坛沿着海岸线摆开，密密匝匝，林小鱼盯着水面，听老人们哭喊：“海神娘娘哟，让他们回来吧……”
她忽然不再害怕水了。海神娘娘在水里，家家户户的祖先也在水里，那是所有人的来处，也是所有人的归处。
她一步步朝海里走去，让海浪没过脚踝，再没过膝盖，最后温柔地托起她的整个身躯。老人们说得对，她天生属于大海。她像一尾被放归的鱼，恣意地伸展着肢体。
她又听见娘在灯下讲故事的声音，听见爹临行前絮絮叨叨的叮嘱，听见他们一起说：“海神娘娘哟，保佑我们的女儿哟……”

林小鱼在水中睁开眼，泪水融入咸腥的海。许许多多的爹娘死在海里，许许多多的孩子在海边哭泣。她在心里说：“海神娘娘哟，求您降下福祉，让爹娘的魂灵顺着海浪回来……”
没有人看见她哭。只有鱼看见。只有大海知道。
她在海里想了很久很久。想宝船，想爹娘，想传说中的大海之主，也想那些带走她爹娘的客商。
她什么都知道，大海也什么都知道。但游上岸之后，林小鱼把嘴唇抿得紧紧的，什么也没有同旁人说。
en:
Ever since childhood, Lin Xiaoyu had harbored a deep fear of the water. She always felt that beneath the ocean's deep emerald waves lay countless corpses and myriad ghosts.
Year after year, the coastal fisherfolk would set floating altars adrift upon the sea. She would sit on the shore, her gaze fixed upon those tiny candles flickering amidst the ripples. Illuminated by the altars' flames, the people's faces refracted a chilling light reminiscent of bloated corpses; their shifting silhouettes seemed to clamor, yet also seemed to weep. Xiaoyu suspected that the souls of the drowned were bustling just beneath the water's surface.
She thought to herself that it would be better to raise goats. By herding them daily to graze, shearing their wool to spin yarn, and taking their milk to sell at the grand market, she would never lack food or clothing, and it would be far safer than venturing out to sea.
Yet her parents claimed she was born to belong to the waters, for her features closely resembled the Matriarch of the Sea worshipped in every household. They dotted her brow with a red mole; at a glance, she looked exactly like the divine statue.
Lin Xiaoyu did not wish to be the Sea Goddess, though playing the part had its advantages. Whenever the older children tore apart the colorful little boats she had folded, she only needed to stand upon a high place, harden her face, and coldly declare, "The Sea Goddess no longer favors you!" The flock of mischievous brats would immediately scatter like frightened birds.
The year Lin Xiaoyu finally obtained a flock of goats of her own, a merchant caravan arrived in town, seeking to recruit helmsmen for a distant voyage.
Those merchants took her parents away, along with the parents of many other children in the village. A long, long time passed thereafter, so long that another layer of rough edges was worn away from the coastal reefs, yet still no ships returned. The sounds of weeping rose and fell across the village like the ocean tide.
Lin Xiaoyu did not cry. She hid in her house, crafting countless colorful little boats, and handed them out to the children on the shore one by one. Mimicking the tone of the Sea Goddess, she told them solemnly that their fathers, mothers, grandfathers, and grandmothers would all return!
But she was not the true Sea Goddess, and she could not shelter the distant ships. No one returned that year, including her parents.
Floating altars were lined up densely along the coastline. Staring at the water's surface, Xiaoyu listened to the elders cry out, "Oh, Sea Goddess, please let them return..."
Suddenly, she was no longer afraid of the water. The Sea Goddess resided within it, and the ancestors of every family resided within it too. It was the origin of all people, and the final destination for all.
Step by step, she walked into the sea, letting the waves wash over her ankles, then her knees, until the water gently lifted her entire body. The elders were right; she was born to belong to the sea. Like a fish released back into the wild, she stretched her limbs with unbridled freedom.
Once again, she heard her mother's voice telling stories beneath the lamp, heard her father's endless admonitions before his departure, and heard them praying together. "Oh, Sea Goddess, please bless our daughter..."
Lin Xiaoyu opened her eyes underwater, her tears dissolving into the salty brine. So many parents had perished in the sea, and so many children wept upon the shore. Deep down, she prayed, "Oh, Sea Goddess, I beg you to bestow your blessings, and let the souls of our parents ride the waves back home..."
No one saw her cry. Only the fish saw it. Only the sea knew.
She remained in the water for a very long time, pondering many things. She thought of the treasure ship, of her parents, of the legendary Master of the Seas, and of the merchants who had taken her parents away.
She knew everything, and the sea knew everything. Yet, upon swimming back to the shore, Lin Xiaoyu pressed her lips tightly together, speaking not a single word to anyone.

zh:
悬泉一驿，自汉武置亭燧于河西，迄今近千年矣！
凡西域文书，皆汇于此。今蕃虏猖獗，烽燧尽毁，驿舍将倾。
唯以残躯掘枯井三丈，藏文书八千卷于此，覆以油毡石椁，或可存百年耳……
倘后世君子掘此遗藏，见龟裂墨迹，须知此非朽纸，实乃戍卒望乡之泪、胡商思亲之语、将士沥血之誓……
若天怜此愿，使泉脉重通，则恳以清流载文卷，经冥水，过阳关，终归长安。

临书涕零，不知所言。  
驿卒张正 顿首再拜
en:
Celestial Spring Station has stood here since Emperor Wu of Han established beacon posts in Hexi, nearly a thousand years ago. All documents from the Western Regions once passed through this place. Now the barbarians run rampant, the beacons are destroyed, and the station is close to collapse.
With my failing strength, I dug a dry well three zhang deep and hid eight thousand scrolls within. I sealed them with oiled cloth and stone coffins, hoping they might endure for a hundred years.
Should a worthy person of later generations uncover this trove and see the cracked ink upon the pages, know that these are not rotted scraps of paper. They are the tears of garrison soldiers longing for home, the words of frontier merchants missing their kin, and the blood-bound vows of warriors.
If Heaven should take pity on this wish and allow the spring to flow again, may clear waters bear these scrolls through dark currents, past Yangguan Pass, and return them at last to Chang'an.

I write this in tears and no longer know my words.
Courier Zhang Zheng
Ning Xin An'an

zh:
王大犬小时候和阿婆并不亲热。
阿婆高高壮壮，既不贤惠也不貌美。粗粗的嗓门，火热的脾气，让尚且年幼的王大犬对她敬畏几分。
阿婆也知道——沉默的孩子最不安。她会翻出已经微微皱瘪的馍馍，不做声地塞到孩子的手中。
那馍馍是大锅出的，存储在篮子里吊着，早已干得掉渣。
王大犬小心翼翼地问阿婆，有没有新鲜的馍馍吃。
阿婆瞪起眉毛，鼻子重重哼了一声。王大犬吓得不敢说话，只是一味地低头啃着馍，听着阿婆推门出去才暗暗松了一口气。
窗外风声越来越紧，屋里渐渐昏暗。王大犬就趴在毯子上，沉沉睡去。
不多时，一阵幽香钻进他的鼻尖。那是一种麦子和肥肉的香气。揉着睡眼，王大犬被眼前的馍馍勾的口水直流。
“吃吧，刚出的。”阿婆粗粗的嗓音响起。她拿起一块馍馍，掰开吹了吹，递给王大犬。
“真是条馋狗。”看着王大犬狼吞虎咽的样，阿婆撇了撇嘴。“又浪费老娘一块肥肉。”
“你慢点吃！没人跟你抢！不够这还有！”
呵斥适时响起，但王大犬分明看到，阿婆眼里是平静的笑意。
en:
When Wang Daquan was little, he wasn't close to his grandma.
Grandma was tall and stout, neither particularly virtuous nor beautiful. Her gruff voice and fiery temper made the young Wang Daquan somewhat afraid of her.
Grandma knew too—silent children were the most uneasy. She would dig out slightly wrinkled, shrunken buns and silently stuff them into the child's hand.
Those buns were from the big pot, stored hanging in a basket, long since dried to crumbs.
Wang Daquan cautiously asked Grandma if there were any fresh buns to eat.
Grandma furrowed her brows and snorted heavily through her nose. Wang Daquan was too scared to speak, just lowered his head and gnawed on the bun, only daring to relax when he heard Grandma push the door open and leave.
Outside the window, the wind grew stronger; inside, it gradually darkened. Wang Daquan lay on the rug and fell sound asleep.
Not long after, a subtle fragrance drifted into his nose. It was the scent of wheat and fat meat. Rubbing sleepy eyes, Wang Daquan's mouth watered at the sight of the bun before him.
"Eat. Fresh out of the steamer." Grandma's rough voice sounded. She picked up a bun, broke it open, blew on it, and handed it to Wang Daquan.
"What a greedy pup," Grandma muttered, watching Wang Daquan wolf it down. "Wasted another piece of my fat meat."
"Slow down! No one's stealing it from you! There's plenty more!"
Scolding came at the right moment, but Wang Daquan clearly saw quiet amusement in Grandma's eyes.

【清誉加减规则】

#G加分：#E每日参与联机可获得10分，每日上限10分；每日与其他玩家组队可获得10分，每日上限10分；联机后被点赞可获得10分，每周上限50分；完成侠境、试剑后被点赞可获得10分，每周上限50分。

#R减分：#E通过联机、发起组队召集，利用特殊地形（毒水、蛇坑、卡点、建造高处、悬崖）导致其他玩家非正常重伤，被举报核实后，禁用邀请陌生人联机、邀请陌生人组队24小时，扣除100分；累计举报被核实多次，会禁用邀请陌生人联机、邀请陌生人组队，处罚时长视累计被举报次数而定。

语言违规行为一经核实扣除50分，限制联机权限12小时。
en:
Jianghu Honor starts at 200 points, with a maximum of 500.

Below 149: Co-op matchmaking and co-op recommendations are prohibited. Below 100: additionally prohibited from initiating co-op invitations or requests to strangers.

[Honor Addition/Subtraction Rules]

#GGain Points:#E Participating in co-op grants 10 points per day (max 10 per day). Teaming up with other players grants 10 points per day (max 10 per day). Receiving a like after co-op grants 10 points (max 50 per week). Receiving a like after Hero's Realm or Sword Trial grants 10 points (max 50 per week).

#RDeduct Points:#E If reported and verified for causing other players' abnormal critical injuries (poison water, snake pits, blocking points, high construction, cliffs) through co-op, team formation, or using special terrain, inviting strangers to co-op or team up will be banned for 24 hours, and 100 points will be deducted. Multiple verified reports will result in longer bans depending on the cumulative number of reports.

Language violations, once verified, deduct 50 points and restrict co-op permissions for 12 hours.

zh:
安安：
自汝别庭帏，倏已逾年。晨昏思悬，寝食难宁。堂萱虽荣，庭桂寂寂；每念汝容，辄添鬓雪。汝父恒抚卷叹惋，谓汝幼时诵读之勤、嬉戏之影，犹在目前。言及此，辄愀然久之。
近若得暇，幸拨冗归省。今虽子侄绕膝，终憾汝远隔云山。况汝素禀清羸，寒燠易侵。学业虽重，身犹本根。莫效昔人“焚膏继晷”，戕伐天和；当调摄以时，膳饮有节，毋使吾悬心。
另有要事，特询于汝：闻文津馆有迁址江南之议。乍聆欣然，徐思则恻。试问吾儿：此议果出汝衷，抑或汝门中群老掣肘？若汝本心，不复死守北地而愿南归，吾当力陈汝父，必不使汝有进退维谷之困。
若得遂此，则桑梓在望，晨昏可依。吾每日庖馐以分族中诸子，心终难慰。非为饮食计，实以念汝殷切，不能自抑耳。

思汝盼汝，早日归家。
en:
Son,
It has been more than a year since you left home, and from morning to night my thoughts are with you. I sleep poorly, I eat without appetite. Though the daylilies still bloom in the hall, the cassia in the courtyard stands quiet; whenever I think of your face, there seems to be a little more frost at my temples. Your father often takes up a book and sighs, saying that your diligence at study and the lively image of you at play still seem to linger before his eyes. Whenever he speaks of it, he falls silent for a long while.
If you can possibly spare the time, do come home for a visit. Though nephews and nieces fill the household, it is still our deepest regret that you remain so far away, beyond clouds and mountains. You have always been slight of build and easily affected by heat and cold. Your studies may be demanding, but your health is the root of all else. Do not imitate those of old who burned the midnight oil at the expense of their natural strength. Take proper rest, be moderate in food and drink, and do not leave me worrying over you.
There is another matter I wish especially to ask you about. I have heard that the Inkbound Order is considering a move to Jiangnan. My first reaction was joy, but the more I thought on it, the more uneasy I became. Tell me truthfully, my son: does this idea truly come from your own heart, or are the elders around you forcing your hand? If it is indeed your wish not to remain in the North, but to return to the South, then I will do all I can to persuade your father and make sure you are not left with no good way forward.
If it comes to pass, then home will be within sight, and we may have you near us again from morning to night. Every day I prepare food for the younger ones in the clan, yet my heart finds no comfort. It is not the food itself that matters, only that I miss you so deeply I cannot help myself.

We miss you and long for your return. Come home soon.

zh:
阳光正好，梨花又飘。午后的天光从竹叶罅隙中漏下，洒做碎金。暖洋洋的风像猫狸子，轻轻挠抓搔你的脸。十六岁离家后，你鲜少回到这里。檐下的蛛网结成画，屋子的主人去了天涯。你坐在昔日他坐着的长椅上，想起曾经自己的童言稚语，缓缓入睡。
恍惚间，你睁开眼，竟看到江叔牵着一匹马，向你走来。印象中的江叔背脊永远这般笔直，宽阔的肩膀如山如岗，为你挡下风雨。可如今你却发现他的衣摆有些脏了，脸上似乎也有了微不可察的疲惫。
此刻你有千言万语想说，但还未及开口，他便抬手止住。他似是猜到你所想，只微颔首，开口询问：
即便如此，你也想入江湖？
看着他的眼睛，你脱口而出——
#Y想。你想成为他那样的大侠，你想去见识更广阔的天地。重来一次，你依然会选择用自己的剑，救更多的人。#E
听见你的回答，江叔点点头。他的眼神并没有什么波动，仿佛你的回答正如他所预料。在他的面前，你可以畅所欲言。因为你知道，不管你的选择是什么，他永远都站在你的身后。曾经，你是他怀中熟睡的婴孩，是他与这个世界的纽系。未来，你会成为他的骄傲，或是牵挂吗。
你起身奔向江叔，想要问问他去了哪里，问问他过得好不好。倏忽间，你的腿抽动了一下，撞在了桌角——疼痛让你睁开了眼。
阳光依然好，梨花还在飘。天光撒做碎金。风里没有故人的消息，但又处处是他，和他们的消息。
en:
The sun shines bright, and pear blossoms drift down once more. Afternoon light filters through the bamboo leaves, scattering like flecks of gold. A warm breeze, soft as a cat's paw, gently teases your cheek. You have seldom returned since leaving home at sixteen. Cobwebs beneath the eaves have woven into intricate paintings, while the master of the house has wandered to the ends of the earth. Sitting on the long bench where he once sat, you recall your childish prattle from long ago and slowly drift off to sleep.
In a daze, you open your eyes, only to see Uncle Jiang leading a horse toward you. In your memory, Uncle Jiang's back is forever straight, his broad shoulders like a sturdy mountain sheltering you from the wind and rain. Yet now, you notice his hem is slightly soiled, and a barely perceptible weariness lingers on his face.
Thousands of words rush to your lips, but before you can even speak, he raises a hand to stop you. As if guessing your thoughts, he gives a slight nod and asks:
"Even so, do you still wish to wander in the jianghu?"

Meeting his gaze, you blurt out...
#YYes. You want to become a great wanderer like him; you want to see a vaster, broader world. If given the chance to start over, you would still wield your sword and save more lives.#E
Hearing your answer, Uncle Jiang nods. His gaze remains steady, as if your response is exactly as he expected. Before him, you can always speak your mind. For you know that no matter your choice, he will always stand behind you. Once, you were a sleeping infant in his arms, his tether to this world. In the future, will you become his pride, or his lingering worry?
You rise and run toward Uncle Jiang, curious about where he has been and whether he has been well. Suddenly, your leg twitches, striking the corner of the table. The pain jolts your eyes open.
The sun remains bright, and the pear blossoms keep drifting down. The daylight scatters like flecks of gold. The wind carries no news of old friends, yet traces of him, and of them all, can be found everywhere.

Insight has had a bit of a troubling time lately. By all reason, what worries could a mere orange cat possibly have? And yet Insight had truly run into a spot of trouble.
"Insight, Insight, here's some dried fish I begged my mother to buy. Please, you simply must put in a good word with the Buddha, and ask him to have my father go easier on his scoldings!"
"Insight, Insight, how was my kneading just now? Please, you must speak to Bodhisattva Manjushri on my behalf, and ask that next time the exam questions all be ones I already know..."
"Insight, Insight, we all pooled our money to buy you a new cushion. We beg you, put in a kind word for us with Lord Wenchang!"
Meow, meow! The dried fish smelled wonderful, the kneading was quite skillfully done, and the new cushion was ever so comfortable to lie upon, but... Insight, gazing at the little humans crowding before it, had long since lost count of just how many waves of visitors it was. It watched the chattering, peeking little figures before it, and gave its tail a flick. Ever since that one little human had stroked it while murmuring something about praying to come first in the next exam, Insight had lost its lazy afternoons entirely. Word had spread among the scholars of the Lin'an Academy that the little cat named Insight, at Fengguo Nunnery, was said to work true miracles. The dried fish piled up like a little mountain, and even so hearty an appetite as an orange cat's has its limits.
"Meow..."
Insight curled itself into a ball and drifted off to sleep, troubles and all. Having accepted so many gifts, one cannot easily refuse a favor in return. And so, having taken its due, Insight resolved to do all a cat could to put in a good word with whichever Buddha or Bodhisattva might listen. For more than any benefit it might gain from granting these little humans their wishes, what Insight truly wished to see was the way their brows unfurrowed, and how their eyes lit up brightly, whenever they spoke.

zh:
张晋卿呵着气，蹲在佛寺后门外，看着慧净意聚精会神地握着棋子。
“中！”慧净意一扬手，张晋卿最后的一枚棋子就出局了。
“你们出家人不是最讲究心怀慈悲么，咋这次下手这老重。” 
慧净意念了声佛号。“佛亦有忿怒相，况乎我等出家人。”

佛寺向来是清修之地，平日里大家的日子如古井无波。抄经，诵经，日子像盘起来的香，怎么烧都是一样的。
但自从认识了张晋卿后，慧净意的日子也开始不一样了。
张晋卿扛着一把陌刀，从山门进来，和每个小尼姑热情地打招呼。
她会热心地帮助医所的师姐们劈柴，帮着采药的师太整理药材。
她会溜进藏经阁，抱着无名的小猫和它一起念拗口的经文。
她会拿着扫把舞得虎虎生威，把院子里的积雪扫得干干净净。
她像一只没头没脑的小狗，一头闯进了寺院的宁夜，又向东边的彤云借了一缕晨曦。

“净意，啥前有空，咱一起去赶大集呗？”
“净意，你上次给我念的是什么玩意，我听着直瞌睡，你再给我念念呗。”
“净意，我找到一个贼有意思的玩意，叫嫖姚棋，咱俩试试呗……”
“净意……”
好吵啊。慧净意笑了笑。“安静些吧。佛都被你吵醒了。”
“佛醒了也不会怪我的。”“佛是好佛，人是好人。”
“贼好的人。”
en:
Zhang Jinqing crouched outside the temple's back door, watching Hui Jingyi concentrate on holding a game piece. 
"Got it!" With a flick of her hand, Hui Jingyi eliminated Zhang Jinqing's last piece. 
"Aren't you nuns supposed to be compassionate? That was harsh." 
Hui Jingyi chanted a Buddha's name. "Even the Buddha has a wrathful form, let alone us monastics." 

Temples are places of quiet cultivation; daily life was usually still. Copying sutras, chanting sutras—days were like coiled incense, burning the same way each time. 
But after meeting Zhang Jinqing, Hui Jingyi's life began to change. 
Zhang Jinqing would stride through the temple gate carrying a Mo Blade, greeting every young nun warmly. 
She eagerly helped the sisters in the infirmary chop wood, assisted the nun gathering herbs in sorting medicines. 
She would sneak into the scripture hall, holding a nameless kitten while reciting difficult sutras together. 
She would wield a broom with such vigor, sweeping the courtyard's snow clean. 
She was like a heedless puppy, charging into the temple's serene night, borrowing a strand of dawn glow from the eastern clouds. 

"Jingyi, when are you free? Let's go to the market!" 
"Jingyi, what was that thing you recited last time? It made me doze off. Recite it again?" 
"Jingyi, I found this really fun thing called Piaoyao Battleboard. Wanna try?" 
"Jingyi..." 
So noisy. Hui Jingyi smiled. "Be quiet. You'll wake the Buddha." 
"The Buddha won't mind if he wakes." "The Buddha is a good Buddha. People are good people." 
"Really good people."

zh:
沉疴久矣，命数所尽，天难救我，唯有三问不明。
一问与亲。您幼时论兵讲剑，蕴习武经，得孙武白起之精，见韬钤之骨髓。待年少之时，观荧惑而芒衰，知吐蕃之运尽。誓心归国，决意无疑。
咸通八年，父亲身死，您束身归阙，命葬他乡，托人相问，只得一言，
言您有时而无命，得遇梦奠之灾。
……早知今日，您亦束手？

二问与君。我辈将大唐置于心，唐既于我心，怎不见我辈肺腑，不见我辈赤胆，
今朝陨命，淮深唯恨战未平，恨天时杀我，人和断我，刀戈向我，杀我辈者，为何竟是自肚腹而出？

三问与己。此生今日，乌护噬我，竖子断我，大唐弃我。淮深环顾此生，不知何罪至此?
#N（于此停笔，未能写完）#E
en:
My long illness will soon claim me, beyond even heaven's saving. Yet three questions still puzzle me.

First, to my uncle. In youth, you mastered the military canon and grasped the essence of tactics. By reading the stars, you foresaw that Tubo Kingdom's fortune was waning. You vowed to return to the homeland with unwavering resolve. When my father died, you gave yourself to the throne. They kept you there until the end and buried you far from home. All you left me were these words: "My moment would come, but I would not live to see it.“ You knew all along, and still you submitted?

Second, to my Emperor. In our hearts we upheld the Tang. Yet, our devotion and loyalty went unseen. My only regret is that the war is not yet won. Fate failed me, and men betrayed me. But why must the knife in the back come from my own kin?!

Third, to myself. Oghuz have devoured me, traitors have betrayed me, the Tang have abandoned me... What sin did I commit to deserve this?

zh: 大相国寺，地处开封城东。广庭之内，花木罗生，中庑之外，僧居鳞次。岳立正殿，翼舒长廊，金碧辉映，云霞失容。大相国寺旧名建国寺，相传为魏公子无忌故宅，于北齐文宣帝天保六年改建为寺。唐延和元年七月，睿宗感梦，诏建国寺为相国寺，御书大相国寺。历世既久，数罹兵燹，幸而今犹立于开封城中。
en: The Grand Imperial Temple lies east of Kaifeng's urban center. Within its spacious courtyards, flowers and trees thrive; beyond the central corridors, monk quarters stand in neat rows. The main hall towers solemnly, corridors stretch like outspread wings—their golden hues shine so brilliantly that clouds pale in comparison. Originally named Jianguo Temple, it's said to stand on the former residence of Lord Xinling of Wei. In the 6th year of the Tianbao Reign (555 CE) under Emperor Wenxuan of the Northern Qi Dynasty, it was converted into a temple. In the 1st year of the Yanhe Reign (712 CE) of the Tang Dynasty, Emperor Ruizong, inspired by a prophetic dream, decreed Jianguo Temple renamed Xiangguo Temple and personally inscribed "Daxiangguo Temple" as its title. In the 1st year of the Yanhe Reign (712 CE) of the Tang Dynasty, Emperor Ruizong, inspired by a prophetic dream, decreed Jianguo Temple renamed Xiangguo Temple and personally inscribed "Grand Imperial Temple" as its title. Through the ages, it has weathered countless wars and fires, yet fortunately, it still stands today in the heart of Kaifeng.

zh:
燕荧心知伏马庄其实并不乐意将他们宠爱的掌珠嫁给他这个军汉。且不说吃穿用度可能受的委屈、夫妻聚少离多等问题，就说战场上刀剑无眼，他不定什么时候丢了性命，便害得媳妇成了寡妇。然而世事无常，世宗于北伐路上突发疾病，不久离世，伏马庄受此波及家道中落。而北伐军解散，燕荧与不愿跟随赵匡胤的同袍选定清河的丰禾村落脚，在村中当起了教书先生，倒也能给祁晟安定的生活。于是伏马庄渐渐接受了他这个姑爷，而燕荧亦不负所托，对妻子千依百顺、关怀备至。好在祁晟并没有大小姐的骄纵习气，只是对赢棋执着了些。为了哄她高兴，燕荧每每冥思苦想，要如何不漏声色地放水，还要输得惊心动魄，不让妻子失了与他对弈的兴趣。
若是生活能这样平静如水地度过该多好啊，可突然出现的靖北令却彻底打破了丰禾村的宁静！靖北令出，北伐军聚，可重聚的北伐军真的只是为了北伐吗？看着眼前的棋局，燕荧不禁陷入沉思，手下无意识走子，不过几步便将死了对方。寂静，异乎寻常的寂静令他回过神来。直到看清面前妻子愤怒的脸，他才惊觉自己露了馅。祁晟感到无比羞辱，当即表示自己要收拾东西回娘家。燕荧张了张口，道歉的话语终是转了个弯，变成刺人的声音：“走就走吧，我才不留！你以为你叫祁晟就是棋圣，我叫燕荧就不会赢棋吗？要不是你哥叮嘱我不能赢你，惹你不开心，我会一直让着你？我早就受够了！你走，快点走！”
祁晟哭了——这是婚后他们第一次争吵，也是燕荧第一次看她流泪，可他不能心软。走吧，就这样一无所知地离开才最安全。若靖北令只是皇权斗争下的一颗棋子，至少现在他还来得及护她无恙。望着妻子远去的背影，燕荧方敢松开握出指甲印的双手，长叹出声：“唉，果然你还是笑着比较好看……”
en:
Yan Ying knew all too well that her family wasn't entirely pleased with marrying their treasured daughter off to a mere soldier. It wasn't just the hardships of daily life they worried about, nor the long stretches of separation; the battlefield was a place without mercy, where death could come at any moment, leaving her widowed at a young age. But fate had its plans. During the northern expedition, Emperor Shizong fell ill and soon passed away, and the once-proud Finesteed Hamlet began to decline. With the northern expedition armies disbanded, Yan Ying and a handful of comrades who refused to serve Zhao Kuangyin settled in Harvestfall Village in Qinghe, where he took up teaching. It wasn't much, but it was enough to give Qi Sheng a steady life. In time, Finesteed Hamlet gradually accepted him as one of their own. Yan Ying was a devoted husband, patient, and attentive. Qi Sheng was not a pampered woman, but she had a competitive streak when it came to chess, so Yan Ying often found himself walking a delicate line, losing just enough to keep her happy, but skillfully enough that she never noticed. Otherwise, her interest in the game might have faded.
Life had been moving along quietly until the issuance of the Jingbei Order shattered that stillness in Harvestfall Village. The northern expedition armies were to be reassembled, but was this just another campaign? Or something more? Sitting before the chessboard, Yan Ying found his thoughts drifting far from the game. His gaze lingered on the pieces, but his mind was not. Absentmindedly, he checkmated his wife with a few moves. Only when he caught sight of her stunned expression did he realize what he'd done. Silence fell like a curtain. Qi Sheng's pride was wounded. Without a word, she stood up and snapped, "I'm going back to Finesteed Hamlet!" Yan Ying opened his mouth, an apology hovering on his lips, yet when he finally spoke, the words came out sharp and cold, "Go, then! I won't stop you! Do you think being called Qi Sheng makes you some kind of chess saint? Well, just because I'm Yan Ying doesn't mean I'm weary of winning! If your brother hadn't told me not to upset you, I would've stopped holding back a long time ago! I'm done walking on eggshells!"
Qi Sheng cried. It was the first time they had truly fought since getting married and the first time Yan Ying had seen her in tears. Yet he stood frozen, knowing that if the Jingbei Order was merely another move in a greater power struggle, there was still time, still a chance to protect her, to let her go. As she turned and walked away, Yan Ying slowly loosened his clenched fists. A long sigh escaped him, "You're always most beautiful when you smile..."
Tian Feng Zhan Ying Bai

他在等谁共饮？又在期待些什么？思考许久，你决定拿出……
⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛
静静地将图纸放在了他的身边。张万师似醉似醒，似是捕捉到了封页上的字眼。他用手轻轻一勾，拿起整摞图纸，看了两眼，又丢到了一旁。他拍了拍手，桃靥剑姬优雅地将你请离了墨守之心。
“此路无知己，明珠莫暗投……你且去吧。”

今夜，他依然与明月对饮。
en:
Ever since witnessing Zhang Wanshi's Aquatic Spectacle, you have been haunted by the memory of his Swordsworn automaton.
Thus, you dive beneath the waves once more to pay him a visit. Zhang Wanshi remains in a stupor, lying drunk upon the ground. Yet, unlike before, two brimful wine cups now rest in front of him.
Who is he waiting to drink with? What is he longing for? After much thought, you decide to present...

You quietly place the diagrams by his side. Half-drunk and half-awake, Zhang Wanshi seems to catch a glimpse of the words upon the cover. With a casual flick of his finger, he lifts the stack of diagrams, spares them a glance, and casts them aside. He claps his hands, and the Rosy-Faced Swordsworn elegantly ushers you out from the Changeless Heart.
"There's no one here who truly understands you. Don't let your gifts go to waste... You should move on."

Tonight, he drinks with the bright moon once more.

en:
Travel one hundred miles north from Heaven's Pier, and you will reach Jadebrook Mountain. These deeps are desolate, their paths long untrodden by travelers.
Ascend a few miles, and the forest grows dense and foreboding—a haven for bandits. This lawlessness is a lingering scar from the previous dynasty's persecution of Buddhism, which forced monks into lay life and left their followers scattered.
Another three miles up a flight of stone steps leads to the summit, where the Buddha's Light Pagoda stands, often bathed in sunlight.
It is named for a legend from the Xiande era. When Master Miaoshan preached here at sunrise, the light crested the peak in a perfect halo, seen by all as a sign of the Buddha's grace. Ever since, this place has been called Halo Peak.

en: Happy is quite pleased with its little domain. How vast the world of men may be, how vast the Jiangnan State... it does not know, and it does not care. Each day it gazes out at the setting sun from atop the temple roof, and it seems to it that even the sun itself is nothing more than some great bird's egg. Gods and mortals alike come and go beneath its paws. Some weep, some laugh, some tread with extreme caution, some stumble and curse their fate, some with hair turning from black to white, and some simply never appear again... Now and then Happy rolls itself over, belly turned up toward the sky, ears letting the sutras flow past its fur like running water. Through these ages it has passed, drifting again and again through the wheel of birth and death, watching all beings among gods, men, and the three lower realms, all bound by compassion and by cause and consequence, as fleeting as the moon upon the water, or a flower within a mirror.

zh:
开运中，契丹狼奔中原，欲居中国而制天下矣。清河守水陆之关，倍侵扰之。有忠义之士，集结为伍，自号#Y“燕北军众”#E，南撤清河，欲抗契丹之师，以为天下之屏。吾尝与义士为伍，见山河破碎，血流漂杵，今之清河贝州，曷异安史睢阳也！呜呼！一人之力当万夫之关，一城之系决天下之安。英雄何谓？不求此身百年，但求黎民无患也！
显德末，吾过清河，见#Y百草野#E上，有铃响入云，河山城破犹在。哀情入目，把酒一尊，为义士飨，敬哉。
en:
In the Kaiyun era, the Khitan swarmed into the Central Plains like wolves, aiming to occupy the Middle Kingdom and rule over all under heaven. Qinghe, guarding the vital juncture of land and water routes, suffered doubly from their incursions. Loyal patriots rallied together, calling themselves the #Y"Northern Alliance,"#E retreating south to Qinghe to resist the Khitan forces and serve as a bulwark for the realm. I once fought alongside these righteous men, witnessing how mountains and rivers lay shattered, blood flowing so profusely that it could float pestles. Today's Qinghe (Beizhou) is no different from Suiyang during the An Lushan Rebellion! Alas! One man's might can hold a pass against ten thousand, and the fate of a single city may decide the safety of the world. What defines a hero? Burial is the act of concealment, a means to ride the Vital Qi.
The breath of Yin and Yang exhales to become wind, ascends to form clouds, and descends as rain; yet when it courses through the veins of the earth, it becomes Vital Qi. Life itself is but the coalescence of this Qi. That which solidifies becomes bone, the sole remnant after death. Thus, burial is the act of returning Qi to the bone, thereby sheltering the paths of the living. As the scripture states: "When Qi resonates in the earth, the blessings of the spirits reach the living."
...

When their eyes gaze upon the Yang, no shadowy malevolence may intrude; when their claws firmly clasp the earth, the departed shall rest in peace. en: Once the most promising disciple of Master Miaoshan, Huiyao was well respected within the order, often acting as a mediator among its unruly ranks. Master Miaoshan's lax discipline had allowed all manner of riffraff into the fold, and it was Huiyao who held things together. But after Miaoshan's mysterious disappearance, Huiyao changed drastically. He joined forces with Huiyong, a former bandit turned monk, and seized every temple on the Sundara Land. Declaring himself the "Living Buddha," Huiyao ruled like a warlord, while Huiyong and his men resumed their old ways of plunder and pillage, staining the name of Miaoshan with blood and fire.
Wenming Hall

zh:
异香火烛 · 渍花

那年她去看拂菻人耍刀，误了回来的时辰——那日三人早就有约，要与她共贺生辰。
万师师兄做了一盏醒钟作为贺礼，鸦做了一道渍花蜜糕——那是青顶喜欢的甜食。
只是等她回来时，这蜜糕早就凉了。
她笨手笨脚地开火重烹，却惹得蜜糕着了火，冒出一股世上绝无仅有的奇异香味。
……最终，三人还是一同分食了那块变作碳色的蜜糕。

后来，不知又是谁做了这蜜糕味的火烛。
只要重新点上火烛，当年情境恍若历历眼前。
en:
Fragrant Candle - Preserved Flower

That year, she went to see the Romans perform their sword dance and missed the appointed time – the three had long agreed to celebrate her birthday together.
Senior Brother Wanshi made an alarm bell as a gift, and Raven made preserved flower honey cake – a sweet treat that Halcyon loved.
But by the time she returned, the cake was long cold.
Clumsily, she tried to reheat it, but ended up setting the cake on fire, producing a strange, unique fragrance in the world.
... In the end, the three still shared the cake that had turned to charcoal.

Later, someone made candles with the scent of that cake.
Whenever relit, the scene from that year feels vivid before her eyes.
Mhm. Lamb's the real treat.

zh:
冒昧了。
虽知今日未必是诉衷肠之吉时，然情之所至，如大江东去，难以为继。纵使您将此番言语视作勾栏戏言，然我一片赤诚，天地日月可鉴，绝非虚妄。
所谓情不知所起，一往而深。无论惊鸿一瞥，亦或日久生情，缘法之妙，往往只在刹那之间。
不瞒您说，我曾无数次徘徊于卿之窗外，暗诵卿之题壁诗稿，只为寻得只言片语之共鸣，哪怕分毫亦足慰平生。
然我未敢贸然留名喝彩，只恐唐突了您，反招嫌隙，令卿生厌。
唯愿不再对着虚空臆想，做那镜花水月之梦，亦不愿做那阴影中见不得光的痴人。
今日斗胆修书，只为道出一句：您之风采，实乃汴京城内难得之美好，我已倾慕良久。
话已至此，情真意切。
对了……
能否惠赐五十文？
我欲去那开封菜馆，买份脱骨五味鸡解解馋。
en:
My apologies for the intrusion.
Though I know today may not be the auspicious time to pour out my heart, my feelings are as unstoppable as the Yangtze flowing east. Even if you regard these words as mere theater, my sincerity is witnessed by heaven and earth, sun and moon, and is by no means false.
It is said that love arises without cause and runs deep. Whether it be a fleeting glance or a bond grown over time, the wonder of fate often lies in a single moment.
To tell you the truth, I have lingered outside your window countless times, silently reciting your verses from the wall, just to find a shred of resonance; even a fraction would suffice to comfort my soul for a lifetime.
Yet I dared not leave my name in praise, for fear of offending you and causing disdain.
I only wish to stop dreaming of mirrors and moons in water, and no longer be a fool hiding in the shadows.
I take the liberty to write today only to say: your grace is a rare beauty within Kaifeng City, and I have long admired you.
Having said this, my words are true and heartfelt.
By the way...
Could you bestow fifty coins?
I wish to go to the Kaifeng Cuisine to buy some Five-Flavor Boneless Chicken to satisfy my cravings.

en: The compilation of this work began in the late Tang dynasty. Co-authored by the scholars of the Inkbound Order, it remains an unfinished edition to this day. It curates poetry from the Tang era, categorizing them by a myriad of themes: farming, seasons and climates, day and night, flowers, bamboo and trees, astronomy, geography, palaces, implements, music, birds and beasts, insects, and human character. Compiled during times of chaos, it was designed as a beginner's guide to poetry. The true intent behind it, however, is to preserve these poetic masterpieces and safeguard the cultural lineage. Once these verses spread to rustic villages and city streets, becoming songs that even young children can recite casually, only then will the cultural lineage endure through the ages.

然门房年高体弱，需托付可靠之人代为巡寝。诸生藏物，各有机巧：违禁之物，或藏于枕衾柜桶，或匿于书页窗牖，须凝神细察，耳听八方。查获之物登记入簿，轻者暂扣，重者没收入库。巡毕复命，奖罚自有分寸。

Dorm inspections have long been a tradition. Beyond assessing students' studies, academies also inspected their daily conduct and living quarters, as a clean room fosters a clear mind, careful handling of belongings prevents trouble, and proper conduct is essential to learning.
The Inkbound Order upholds this tradition with three rules: keep your quarters clean, handle your belongings with care, and conduct yourself properly.
The dorm supervisor now needs your help. Students hide prohibited items in all sorts of places, so keep your eyes sharp and ears open. Record anything you find, confiscate minor offenses, and report back after inspection.

zh:
枕纸的耳朵灵光，听着屋外越来越近的说笑声，便知道是姑娘们来了。算准时间，小猫在她们进门的时候，恰恰好伸了个懒腰。“喵呜~”“啊呀，是枕纸！侬今朝也在？”姑娘中为首的那个已经弯腰下去，熟练地把猫抱在怀里。枕纸很满意，舒舒服服地往姑娘带着花香的臂弯里拱了拱。人，猫已经准备好了。姑娘们不疾不徐围桌而坐，研墨润笔，煮茗焚香。等绢纸铺开，就该轮到枕纸上场了。枕纸身姿轻盈，一跃便优雅上桌。它昂首挺胸巡视一圈，不放过任何一处会妨碍姑娘们一展画技的角落。枕纸挥动着小爪子，左边捋捋翘起的纸尖，右边抚平有些微褶皱的纸面，临了，满意一喵，趴在绢纸的最角落，蜷成一团。姑娘们瞧着枕纸行云流水的动作，总笑着夸它是玉壶园内一等一的小书童。
玉壶园毗邻西湖，四时多风。但你瞧，有了枕纸，就算是起了风，便再不需那冰凉呆板的镇纸了。
en:
Pillow Paper's ears were keen indeed, and upon hearing the laughter and chatter drawing nearer just outside, it knew at once the young ladies had arrived. Timing it just so, the little cat stretched itself out in a leisurely arch the very moment they stepped through the door. "Meow..." "Oh my, it's Pillow Paper! Are you here again today?" The young lady leading the group had already bent down, scooping the cat up into her arms with practiced ease. Pillow Paper, quite content, nuzzled comfortably into the crook of her flower-scented arm. O human, the cat is ready. The young ladies settled themselves around the table without hurry, grinding ink and moistening their brushes, brewing tea and lighting incense. Once the silk paper was laid out flat, it was Pillow Paper's turn to take the stage. Light and graceful in step, it leapt gracefully up onto the table with a single bound. Head held high and chest puffed out, it made a full circuit of inspection, letting no corner escape its notice that might hinder the ladies in showing off their skill with the brush. Pillow Paper waved its paws about, smoothing down a curled corner here, flattening a slight wrinkle there, and at last, with a satisfied meow, curled itself into a ball and settled at the very corner of the silk paper. Watching Pillow Paper's smooth, flowing movements, the young ladies would always laugh and praise it as the finest little study-page in all of Jadeheart Garden.
Jadeheart Garden lay close by West Lake, where the wind blew often through all four seasons. But you see, with Pillow Paper about, even when the wind rose, there was never any need for that cold, lifeless paperweight again.

游侠，见字如面。
前些时日，老朽随府尹大人巡查蒙学，见学堂里的娃娃们一个个正襟危坐，埋首书卷，连我等走近了都未曾察觉。
老朽心下好奇，是何等妙文，能让这些上蹿下跳的娃娃们如此专心？一问才知，他们手中所读，竟是你前些时日所赠。
老朽又问，这些书好在何处？娃娃们七嘴八舌，老朽这才知道，原来你竟为每个孩子都择了不同的书，实在是费心了。而听闻老朽与你相熟，他们都央着我，定要代他们向你道声谢。
只是，真要问他们想说什么，这群小家伙却面露羞赧，讷讷而止了。最后，老朽想了个法子，让他们把想说的话都诉诸笔端，一并封在信里了。至于写了什么，老朽绝未偷看！
对了，娃娃们还托我转交几幅画作，说是读了书卷后的有感而发。他们都说，游侠你是他们见过最有眼光的人，定能欣赏他们的大作。
哈哈，看来往后若再有与孩子们打交道的差事，找游侠准是没错了。

en:
Dear Wanderer,

The other day, I accompanied the Prefect on an inspection of the village school. The children sat straight at their desks, noses buried in scrolls, so absorbed they didn't even notice us draw near.
Curious what could hold their attention so completely, I asked. Turns out, they were reading the very books you gifted them not long ago.
I inquired further: what made these books so special? The little ones burst into chatter, and that's when I learned you had chosen a different book for each child. What thoughtfulness.
When they heard I knew you, they begged me to pass along their thanks.
But when I asked what they wanted to say, shyness took over, and words failed them. So I suggested they write it down instead. Their letters are enclosed. And no, I did not peek!
Oh, and they also asked me to send you a few drawings. Inspired, they said, by your books. They all agreed you're the most discerning person they've ever met, and that you'd surely appreciate their masterpieces.
Seems to me, whenever there's a task involving children, you're the one to call.

【鹊】

鹊
李峤
不分荆山抵，甘从石印飞。

绝句二首·其一

鸳鸯

锦机争织样，歌曲爱呼名。
好育顾栖息，堪怜泛浅清。
凫鸥皆尔类，惟羡独含情。

鸳鸯
李商隐
雌去雄飞万里天，云罗烟浪共缠绵。
如何肯到清秋节，已带斜阳又带烟。

【牛】

咏牛
杜甫
牛牛食草莫相触，官家截尔头上角。
牵牛去下犁上土，牛背日斜花满川。

牧童词
张籍
远牧牛，绕村四面禾黍稠。
陂中饥乌啄牛背，令我不得戏垅头。
入陂草多牛散行，白犊时向芦中鸣。
隔堤吹叶应同伴，还鼓长鞭三四声。
牛牛食草莫相触，官家截尔头上角。

牧牛歌
陆龟蒙
江草凄凄正秋半，十角吴牛放江岸。
耸肩抵尾乍依隈，横去斜奔忽分散。
荒陂断堑无端入，背上时时孤鸟立。
日暮相将带雨归，田家烟火微茫湿。

【马】

房兵曹胡马
杜甫
胡马大宛名，锋棱瘦骨成。
竹批双耳峻，风入四蹄轻。
所向无空阔，真堪托死生。
骁腾有如此，万里可横行。

白马
杜甫
白马东北来，空鞍贯双箭。
可怜马上郎，意气今谁见。
近时主将戮，中夜商於战。
丧乱死多门，呜呼泪如霰。

天马歌
李白
天马来出月支窟，背为虎文龙翼骨。
嘶青云，振绿发，兰筋权奇走灭没。
腾昆仑，历西极，四足无一蹶。
鸡鸣刷燕晡秣越，神行电迈蹑慌惚。
天马呼，飞龙趋，目明长庚臆双凫。
尾如流星首渴乌，口喷红光汗沟朱。
曾陪时龙蹑天衢，羁金络月照皇都。
逸气棱棱凌九区，白璧如山谁敢沽。
回头笑紫燕，但觉尔辈愚。
天马奔，恋君轩，駷跃惊矫浮云翻。
万里足踯躅，遥瞻阊阖门。
不逢寒风子，谁采逸景孙。
白云在青天，丘陵远崔嵬。
盐车上峻坂，倒行逆施畏日晚。
伯乐翦拂中道遗，少尽其力老弃之。
愿逢田子方，恻然为我悲。
虽有玉山禾，不能疗苦饥。
严霜五月凋桂枝，伏枥衔冤摧两眉。
请君赎献穆天子，犹堪弄影舞瑶池。
en:
【Birds and Beasts, Part II】

【Magpie】

The Magpie
Li Qiao
Not distinguishing the Jing Mountains' ridges, it gladly flies from the stone seal.
Its precarious nest fears the swift wind; circling the trees, it finds the stars sparse.
Joy follows the traveler's arrival; sorrow accompanies the Weaver Girl's return.
If it wanders within a bright mirror, morning and evening it stirs radiance.

【Mandarin Ducks】

Two Quatrains, No. 1
Du Fu
Late sun adorns the rivers and hills; spring breezes scent the grass and flowers.
Mud softens for swallows in flight; warm sand cradles sleeping mandarin ducks.

Mandarin Ducks
Du Mu
In pairs they play on sandy shores, long seeming too lovely for paint to capture.
Brocade looms vie to weave their likeness; songs delight in calling their name.
Fond of nurturing, they care for their roost; pitiable, they float on shallow clear waters.
Ducks and gulls are all your kind, yet only you are envied for holding deep affection.

Mandarin Ducks
Li Shangyin
The female departs, the male flies ten thousand miles to the sky, amidst misty nets and smoky waves, entwined together.
How could they bear to reach the clear autumn season, already bearing the slanting sun and again veiled in mist.

【Ox】

Ode to the Ox
Du Fu
Oxen, grazing on grass, do not butt each other; the officials will sever the horns from your heads.
Leading the ox to plow the soil below, on the ox's back the sun slants, flowers fill the riverbank.

Herdboy's Song
Zhang Ji
Grazing oxen far away, circling the village where millet grows thick on all sides.
In the pond, hungry crows peck the ox's back, keeping me from playing on the ridge.
Entering the pond where grass is plentiful, the oxen scatter; a white calf now and then lows towards the reeds.
Across the embankment, blowing a leaf answers my companion; still I crack the long whip three or four times.
Oxen, grazing on grass, do not butt each other; the officials will sever the horns from your heads.

Song of Herding Oxen
Lu Guimeng
River grasses mournful in mid-autumn, ten-horned Wu oxen are released on the riverbank.
Hunching shoulders, pressing tails, they lean against the bend; dashing sideways, running askew, they suddenly disperse.
Into desolate ponds and broken ditches they wander without cause; on their backs, a lone bird perches from time to time.
At dusk, they return together through the rain; the farmhouse's cooking smoke is faintly damp.

【Horse】

Fang Bingcao's Barbarian Steed
Du Fu
The barbarian steed, famed from Dayuan, its sharp edges formed of lean bone.
Bamboo-split ears stand tall and steep; wind enters its four hooves, making them light.
Wherever it charges, no distance is vast; truly fit to entrust life and death.
With such galloping vigor, it can roam ten thousand miles.

The White Horse
Du Fu
A white horse comes from the northeast, an empty saddle pierced by two arrows.
Pitiable the rider on the horse, where is his spirit seen now?
Recently, the commanding general was slain; at midnight, battle raged at Shangyu.
In the chaos of war, death comes by many doors; alas, tears fall like sleet.

Song of the Heavenly Horse
Li Bai
The Heavenly Horse comes from the Moon Clan's cave, its back marked with tiger stripes, dragon-wing bones.
Neighing at the blue clouds, shaking its green mane, orchid-tendoned, wondrously swift, it vanishes from sight.
Soaring over Kunlun, traversing the Western Pole, all four hooves never stumble.
Crowing at dawn, grooming in Yan, fed at dusk in Yue, divinely moving, swift as lightning, treading the indistinct.
The Heavenly Horse calls, the Flying Dragon hastens, eyes bright as the Evening Star, chest like a pair of ducks.
Tail like a shooting star, head like a thirsty crow, mouth spewing red light, sweat channels crimson.
Once it accompanied the timely dragon, treading the celestial path, bridled in gold, moon-illumined, shining on the imperial capital.
Its untamed spirit, angular and proud, towers over the nine regions; white jade piled like mountains, who dares to price it?
Turning its head, it laughs at the Purple Swallow, feeling only your kind is foolish.
The Heavenly Horse gallops, yearning for its lord's carriage, leaping startled, soaring, turning the floating clouds.
Its ten-thousand-mile hooves hesitate, gazing afar at the Gate of Heaven.
Not meeting the Son of the Cold Wind, who will gather the offspring of fleeting light?
White clouds are in the blue sky, hills and mounds rise far and steep.
Pulling a salt cart up a steep slope, moving backward, acting perversely, it fears the day's end.
Bole brushed and groomed it but abandoned it mid-way; in youth, its strength spent; in age, cast aside.
I wish to meet Tian Zifang, that he might sorrow for me with pity.
Though there be jade mountain grain, it cannot cure bitter hunger.
Severe frost in May withers the cassia branches; stalled at the trough, bearing grievance, it furrows both brows.
I beg you, redeem and present it to the Mu Son of Heaven; still it could frolic with its shadow, dancing in the Jasper Pool.

If you bestow fifty coins upon me now,

zh:
买春天，要多少钱？
我当然知道她想买什么，但我不想让她知道我知道。
于是我说：“那得看你买谁？若是东屋的陈姑娘，得要百贯铜钱，西屋的李姑娘，得是千贯，但你们屋的春姑娘啊……”
“要……要……”
“她可是咱们这的头牌。” 
我伸出食指，晃了晃：“万贯。”
她念着万贯走了，她真信了。

我没诓她，姑娘原本确实是咱们院的头牌。只是现在老了，病了，走不动了，也走不了了。
最初，姑娘开始喝药，她皱起脸，蹲在姑娘脚边，一直不走。
后来，姑娘走不出门，让客人自个儿进她房里。她就蹲在门口，跟个小石狮子似的。
再后来，姑娘的脸一日比一日苍白，姑娘的妆一日比一日浓，姑娘的价格一日比一日低。
她身上的伤却一日比一日多，随着伤口一同变多的，还有她的铜钱。

这笔买卖是在一个冬天落定的。
我正在擦桌子。那声音很响，我抬起头，看见她把三贯带血的铜钱拍在桌面上。
“我只有……没有……三贯……”
“换。迎春，春。”
她的春字说得最好，我开始信了，这是她说的第一个字。
“就要迎春？不退不换。”
“要……”
掌柜的眼角抽动了一下，我知道为什么。掌柜斜着眼招手：“小二，带她去。”

我是小二。
我先好心给了她一张我家里仅剩的破草席，然后带她去看了那具尸体。
我在等她反悔，等她把姑娘的尸体卷起来，再埋下去。
可她没有，她没用我的破草席。
尸体是走不了的，所以她只能将姑娘抱起来，她的衣摆染了血，铜钱也染了血。
染血的三贯铜钱落到我的手上。
这是一笔极不值当的买卖，尸体不值得银子，也不值得弄脏衣服，可她不觉得。
她奔向了春天里。
en:
"How much does it cost... to buy spring?"

Of course, I knew what she meant. But I didn't want her to know that I knew.

So I said, "Depends who you're buying. Miss Chen from the east wing? That'll cost a hundred strings of copper coins. Miss Li from the west? A thousand. But your Miss Chun..."

"Want... want..."

"She's our top courtesan," I said, holding up a single finger and giving it a wag, "Ten thousand."

She left, murmuring "ten thousand" under her breath. She really believed it.

I hadn't lied. Miss Chun truly had been the pride of our house.

But now... she was old, sick, barely able to move.

At first, when she started taking medicine, the girl would crouch by her feet, refusing to leave.

Later, when Miss Chun couldn't leave her room, she'd let the clients come to her. The girl would squat at the door like a little stone lion.

Then Miss Chun grew paler day by day, her makeup thicker, her prices cheaper.

The wounds on her body multiplied, and so did the copper coins she clutched.

The deal was struck on a winter's day.

I was wiping down the tables when I heard a loud slap.

She had slammed three bloody copper coins onto the surface.

"I have... only... three..."

"Exchange. Spring... Chun."

She said "Chun" so clearly, I almost believed it really was the first word she learned.

"You just want Miss Chun? No refunds, no exchanges."

"Want..."

The boss's eye twitched, and I understood why.

He shot me a look and waved me over.

"Waiter. Take her."

I'm the Waiter.

Out of pity, I gave her the last scrap of straw matting from my house, then took her to see the body.

I was waiting for her to regret it, to wrap the corpse in the mat, to bury it properly.

But she didn't.

She didn't use the mat.

The body couldn't walk, so she simply lifted Miss Chun into her arms.

Her dress was soaked in blood. So were the coins.

The three strings of bloodstained coins landed in my hand.

A poor bargain, by any measure.

A corpse not worth dirtying her silver, not worth dirtying her clothes.

But she didn't care.

She ran straight into the spring.

你问咱们跟着将军去做什么？去守乡守土，守你们这些孩子长大，守好年景到来。”

"Little Jiang Yan, look north. What do you see? Mountains? Yes, the Taihang Mountains. A decade ago, my home was on the other side. Now, even though the wind still blows from the north, I can only watch from here. Mountains are barriers; without them, we have no defense, leaving our heartland exposed. Countless souls have lost their homes and families. If we keep retreating, millions more will suffer. You ask what we are doing following the General? We are here to guard our homeland, to protect children like you as you grow, and to ensure a peaceful future arrives."

王清记得自己曾和师弟江远争论过何谓大侠。江远自幼便被门派收养，认为自己若是练就了一身武艺，自当帮扶同门，为门派效力。可王清不这样认为，他觉得江远的想法太过狭隘，侠者当然要为国为民，守住太平。二人尚且年幼，江远不理解王清，王清也不理解江远，争论推搡间便打了起来。最终二人被罚思过三天。

后来，王清真如他当时所说，去了前线抗击契丹。而江远也如他所愿，留在门派操持事务。直到王清在战场上不慎被契丹军围困。危急时刻，江远带了同门前来解围。那一战死伤惨重，中箭的江远只来得及将独子托付给王清便合上了双眼。王清看着眼前死去的弟兄，忽然想起很多年前江远说过的：若是练就了一身武艺，自当帮扶同门。原来，这便是他的侠义。
en:
Wang Qing can still recall the argument he once had with his junior, Jiang Yuan, over what it truly meant to be a great hero. Jiang Yuan, taken in by the sect as an orphan, believed that mastering martial arts came with the duty to support fellow disciples and serve the sect with loyalty. But to Wang Qing, that view was far too narrow. In his eyes, a real hero stood for something greater, serving the nation, protecting the people, and striving for peace and stability. They were both young then, too young to see the world through each other's eyes. Their disagreement grew heated, and when words failed, fists followed. The clash ended with both of them being punished and ordered to spend three days in quiet reflection.

 In the years that follow, Wang Qing stays true to his convictions, heading to the front lines to battle the Khitan. And Jiang Yuan also keeps his vow, dedicating himself to the affairs of the sect. But fate does not let their paths remain apart for long. In one brutal campaign, Wang Qing finds himself surrounded by the enemy. At the critical moment, it is Jiang Yuan who comes, leading a group of disciples into the heart of battle to save him. The fighting is fierce, and amid the chaos, Jiang Yuan takes an arrow to the chest. As he lies dying, he turns to Wang Qing and entrusts his young son to him with his final breath. Kneeling beside his fallen brother-in-arms, Wang Qing still hears the echo of words once spoken long ago, "A great hero helps his fellow disciples." Only then does he fully grasp what Jiang Yuan's idea of a great hero truly means.

zh:
春望篇·永新

“许家三娘歌声婉转，一定能讨得天子与贵妃欢喜。”
教坊使的赞美她从来不敢相信。
“声有误者，帝必觉而正之。”梨园由天子筹办，对于乐曲方面，皇帝比任何人都懂，出不得丝毫差错。
第一次入宫献艺的梨园弟子，当然是不敢抬起头的。
她战战兢兢，甚至不知道该把手脚放在什么位置。
“十三岁，还是个小娃娃呢。”
贵妃的声音温润得恰到好处。许三娘悄悄抬眼，只瞥见浅笑的梨涡，像极了此时的满园春光。

皇帝要把自己新谱的曲子，让伶人唱与贵妃听。
据说是采曲人搜罗的乡间小调，唱男子思慕爱人，辗转反侧。
帝王爱人，高高在上赐予天下最难得的珍宝，却又要效仿百姓的姿态，捧出略显局促的真心。

许三娘唱得小心翼翼，她很清楚，自己唱得不差，但也不算好。
教坊之中都是千挑万选来的人才，不好，就是错。
等待审判的时刻，那个声音传来“小娃儿，过来。”
三娘几乎要踩到自己的裙摆，磕磕绊绊上前。
贵妃噗嗤一笑。纤纤玉指拿着朱红的果子塞进她手里，说自己很是欢喜。

之后天子和贵妃说了什么，她没听进去，仿佛帝王在问，自己能得到怎般奖赏。
声音低沉威严，又仿佛带着几分讨好。
教坊的伶人们纷纷谢安领赏，梨园春光，且留予男子和他的爱人共赏。

自乐师家出生，她被选入宫，编入教坊，一切似乎水到渠成。
踏出宫门的那一刻，三娘暗自想，或许自己是喜欢唱歌的。
en:
Spring's Gaze: Eternal Renewal 

"Xu Sanniang has a voice like silk. Surely she'll charm both the Emperor and the Noble Consort." 
Sanniang never dared believe the overseer's praise. 
"One wrong note, and His Majesty will hear it at once." The Masked Troupe existed by imperial will; in matters of music, no one surpassed the Emperor's ear. There was simply no room for mistakes. 
For first‑time performers entering the palace, lifting one's head was unthinkable. 
Sanniang trembled so hard she barely knew what to do with her hands and feet. 
"She's thirteen—still just a little one." 
The Noble Consort said, her voice warm and gentle, pitched with perfect grace. Sanniang risked a glance upward. She saw a soft, dimpled smile—like spring light spilling over a garden in bloom. 

The Emperor wished to present a new composition, a song he wanted the troupe to sing for the Consort. 
It was said to be based on a village tune collected by wandering song‑gatherers—a melody about a young man longing for the one he loves, sleepless and restless. 
A man who ruled the world, able to bestow treasures beyond imagining—yet here he was, imitating the shy earnestness of a common boy, offering his heart a little awkwardly. 

Sanniang sang with exquisite care. She knew she wasn't bad—but she wasn't truly good either. 
In the imperial troupe, "not perfect" meant "wrong." 
As she waited for judgment, the words came: "Child, come here." 
She nearly stepped on her hem as she stumbled forward. 
The Noble Consort let out a soft laugh and placed a bright red fruit into her palm, saying she was delighted. 

Whatever the Emperor said afterward faded into a blur. It almost sounded as though he was asking what reward she desired— 
his voice low, authoritative, yet tinged with something gentler, almost coaxing. 
Around her, performers bowed, accepted their stipends, and withdrew. Spring lingered in the Masked Troupe, its warmth left to the Emperor and his beloved alone. 

Born into a family of musicians, chosen for the Masked Troupe, welcomed into the palace—everything had unfolded as naturally as water flowing downhill. 
And as she stepped through the palace gates once more, Sanniang realized, quietly and to her own surprise: Perhaps she truly did love to sing.

有人说，是胡子大战天上来群猫时掉的，英勇无比，很是威风。
只有胡子自己知道，那一半胡子，是偷吃贡品时被殿内的香火烧没的。
殿内的香火断了，胡子也就长出来了。
可那样，胡子怎么还能叫胡子呢？得换个名字，叫什么好呢……坝上的人们一边唱着久远的歌，一边想。
“瓠子决兮将奈何——”
“喵喵喵喵喵喵喵——”
“鱼沸郁兮柏冬日——”
“喵喵喵喵喵喵喵——”
瓠子金堤上，瓠子歌一响，猫咪的叫声便也跟着唱起来。
“呦，是个有灵性的，不如就叫'瓠子'吧！”
“喵——”胡子深表同意，这样自己的名字就再也不是一世英名的拖累。
这样，就再没有人记得万人殿的香火烧掉了的另一半胡子。
很久很久之后，人们只会记得瓠子金堤上响起的，人与猫的歌谣。
en:
Whisky used to be called Whisker, because she once lost half its whiskers.
Some say it happened in a heroic battle against the Heavenfall cats. It was a fearsome clash, full of glory!
But only Whisker knew the truth: that missing half was scorched off by incense when she snuck into a shrine to steal offerings.
Then the shrine's incense runs out and her whiskers grow back.
But that means she loses the unique trait! A new name is needed. A better name... People on the Levee are singing old songs as they ponder.
"The Whisky Levee breaches. What can we do?"
"Meow, meow, meow, meow, meow, meow, meow, meow..."
"Fish churn in a frenzy as winter's chill approaches."
"Meow, meow, meow, meow, meow, meow, meow, meow..."
Whenever the Ballad of Huzi rises, the cat will join in chorus.
"See, it responded. Let's call it Whisky!"
"Meow..." Whisky agreed at once. Now, its name will no longer bear the weight of a charred past and no one will remember the other half of the whisker burned by the incense.
They only remembered the songs sung by the cat and people on the Whisky Levee.
